feedback.gloss.battery.under: the line is in a band at or below the battery's own (%s with an instrument); it charges only from a higher band
feedback.jei.info.rectifier: Set it against a battery and wire it to an MV line: while it is fed, that battery charges in about three minutes from empty instead of ten. The extra current heats the battery more and a lead-acid one gasses sooner. It draws a small current whether or not a battery is there, and does nothing alone.
feedback.jei.info.battery: A battery: cells in series, rated the band of their case. It is a reserve store: it charges from the surplus of a generator of its own band on the same line, or from a line of its band or a higher one, and a lower band never charges it. Beside a generator it gives its band back only to cover what the generator cannot, holding its full current until almost empty. It stores Eu. Build it at a bench from a stack of plates (1 to 4 plates a cell, 1 to 12 cells in series) and an insulating case, place it, and fill it with an electrolyte from buckets or pipes: any ion-carrying liquid the plates are not eaten by (sulfuric acid for lead, lye for iron and nickel; a lithium cell takes only a non-water one), and water for the tank of a water-based cell. A powered Rectifier against it charges it in about three minutes. Overcharging boils water off and releases hydrogen, which a flame sets off; drawing too much current, running hot or sitting in a band above its case wears it. The cold costs capacity. A Hydrometer reads the charge.
feedback.jei.info.hydrometer: Use it on a battery to sample the acid, whose density falls as the cells discharge: it reads the state of charge to the nearest five per cent. Carry it in the instrument bag and a battery's Jade card gives the figure too.
feedback.gloss.battery.dry: the cells hold no acid yet; fill them from a bucket of sulfuric acid
feedback.gloss.battery.charging: drawing from a higher band on the line
feedback.gloss.battery.holding: on a line in its own band, neither taking nor giving
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.low: under %d%% of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.part: %2$d%% or more of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.nearly: %3$d%% or more of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.full: as full as the cells go
feedback.gloss.battery.runaway: the cells are heating themselves and burning their charge as heat; it ends when the charge is gone. Water makes it worse, sand beside it smothers it
feedback.gloss.battery.weeping: overcharged: it is boiling water into hydrogen. A flame near it is dangerous
feedback.gloss.battery.low_water: the plates are exposed and the cells hold less; top the water up
modular.feedback.role.plates.tip: The stack of plates. Its material sets how much charge a plate holds and how it fares in the cold; its size sets how many cells.
modular.feedback.role.case.tip: What holds the stack. Its material sets the highest band the battery can take without wearing.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.light_cell: A single plate for the cell: half the charge of the standard pair, 1 cell.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heavy_cell: Four plates of stock for one cell: twice the charge of the standard pair, 1 cell.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.three_cell: Like a pair of plates, but 6 plates of stock: 3 cells in series, 3 times the charge held.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_cell: Like a pair of plates, but 12 plates of stock: 6 cells in series, 6 times the charge held.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.twelve_cel: Like a pair of plates, but 24 plates of stock: 12 cells in series, 12 times the charge held.
modular.feedback.desc.part.battery_plate: Plates of a metal that can be charged and discharged, laid in a stack. A cell takes one to four plates, and a stack holds one to twelve cells. Cells in series add to the charge held but not to the current rated. A metal whose plates do not take a charge makes a stack that holds none.
feedback.battery.dry: No acid: the cells are dry
tooltip.feedback.battery.dry: Dry: fill the cells with acid once placed
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_frame: The frame the shaft's torque is carried through, in plate. Its size sets the most torque the machine carries (2, 16 or 64 Su), how much heat it holds and how large a wall it sheds heat through.
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_windi: The coil of wire. Its turns set the band a generator makes at a given speed, and the speed a motor runs at in a given band; its wire sets the current it carries, and the loss it makes as heat.
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_housi: The shell that sheds the machine's heat to the air, in plate. A metal that conducts heat well sheds more; a cooling addon fitted to it (plate fins, or pipe for a water jacket) sheds more.
modular.feedback.role.frame.tip: Carries the torque. Its size sets the most the machine can carry, and its heat capacity.
modular.feedback.role.machine_winding.ti: The coil. Its material must conduct: its current rating sets the amps; its turns set the band at a given speed.
modular.feedback.role.housing.tip: Sheds the machine's heat to the air. Its material's heat conduction sets how fast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.small: Carries 2 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.medium: 4 plates of stock: carries 16 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.large: 8 plates of stock: carries 64 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coarse: A single wire: few turns, a low band at a given speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fine: 2 wires of stock: four times the turns of coarse, a band higher at the same speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dense: 4 wires of stock: sixteen times the turns of coarse, two bands higher at the same speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heavy_dens: 8 wires of stock: sixty-four times the turns of coarse, three bands higher at the same speed.
tooltip.feedback.dynamotor.jacket: Water jacket: fill it with water once placed
feedback.jei.info.dynamotor: Turns rotation into electricity and back: a frame, a winding, a core and a housing built at a bench. Place it against the end of a shaft and run cable from any other face. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to switch it between generator and motor. The winding's turns set the band it puts on the line and the speed it is built for, its wire the current; a generator offers more packets the faster its shaft turns, and what the line draws is the load on the shaft; a bigger frame carries more torque. It heats in use and sheds the heat through its housing; a cooling addon of plate (fins) sheds more, and one of pipe is a water jacket that takes water from a bucket to shed twice as fast. Overdrawing it wears it, but never stops it.
feedback.jei.info.joint_link: Ties two bodies at a joint. Click a joint voxel that has nothing in front of it, then a voxel of the other body within a block and a half of its face: that body is held to the joint, as a body made from the blocks in front of it would be, but nothing is made and nothing is used up. Click the joint voxel with an empty hand to let it go. A chain closed this way is a loop; the Lift reports it, and the physics does what it can with it.
message.feedback.link.pick_joint: Click a joint voxel with nothing in front of it first
message.feedback.link.linked: Linked: the other body is held to the joint
message.feedback.link.other_world: The world is not a body to hold: pick a voxel of a lifted body
message.feedback.link.same_body: That is the joint's own body
message.feedback.link.too_far: Too far from the joint: within a block and a half
message.feedback.differential.mode.0: Open: the axle that resists less turns faster
message.feedback.differential.mode.1: Limited slip: the axles may differ by only a little
feedback.jei.info.differential: One shaft in, two axles out. The speed is shared by what each axle resists: open, the axle with less grip spins and the other stands; limited slip, they may differ by only a little; locked, a solid axle. Sneak-click to change. Place it on a shaft, in coarsespace or in finespace; the axles go out across the way you look.
message.feedback.joint.repaired: Fitted a new bearing: the joint and its brake pad are as built
feedback.jei.info.tire_rubber: Synthetic rubber pressed into a block: a grippy, soft building block that collides like any other, in coarsespace or cut into motes. It is not a wheel; a wheel is a tire hub on a turned body, fitted with a tire.
feedback.jei.info.micro_wedge: A four-step ramp. Place it in finespace and it is a ramp a quarter of a block long, falling away from you; click the top half of a face to hang it from above. What you see is what collides. Set the Fine Gauge to Wedge mode and any mote in your other hand goes in as a ramp of itself.
feedback.jei.info.ball_joint: A joint, in coarsespace or in finespace. Put it with its front towards what should swing, then use it with an empty hand: everything joined to its front face becomes a body that swings about the joint inside a cone. Sneak-use before assembling to choose a narrow, stock or wide cone.
feedback.jei.info.locked_joint: A joint, in coarsespace or in finespace, that holds two bodies as one rigid piece, so a part can be split off and put back later. Use it with an empty hand to assemble or put back. Link it to a controller card and a level of one half or more lets go: a spring parts the two bodies and the held one is free, a stage that has gone. With nothing in front of it but another body touching the cell there, use it to dock: it holds that body as it stands, until it is used again or released.
feedback.jei.info.slider_joint: A joint, in coarsespace or in finespace, that lets a body slide along its front axis against a spring: a suspension. Sneak-use before assembling to choose a soft, stock or stiff spring.
feedback.jei.info.piston_joint: A joint, in coarsespace or in finespace, that slides a body along its front axis to a level a controller card sets. It holds the position against a load and wears only if forced past it.
message.feedback.joint.role.0: Turns at the shaft's speed; a card can brake it.
message.feedback.joint.role.1: Steers: a card sets its angle.
message.feedback.joint.role.2: Roll surface: a card sets its angle.
message.feedback.joint.role.3: Pitch surface: a card sets its angle.
message.feedback.joint.role.4: Yaw surface: a card sets its angle.

message.feedback.micro.mode.box: Box: click one corner, then the other.
message.feedback.micro.mode.wedge: Wedge: the mote in your other hand goes in as a ramp of itself.

message.feedback.micro.planes_full: Three mirror planes at most. Click a plane's face again to remove it.
feedback.jei.info.large_ring_gear: A ring gear with a large cog's teeth: a small cog driving it turns what it carries at half the speed, and a large cog beside it turns it as it would a large cog. Everything else is as the Ring Gear.
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.assemble: Assembled: it turns with the shaft
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.empty: Nothing in front of it to turn
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.docked: Docked: it holds the body in front of it
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.too_big: Too big, or it touches the ground
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.blocked: Something stands where a block would go back
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.misalign: Turn it back first: the blocks on it would not line up with the grid
message.feedback.rotary_bearing.has_chil: Put back what its bearings carry first
tooltip.feedback.creative_treatise: Every volume of every treatise, those added later too.
feedback.tooltip.gear_cutter: Cuts a plate into a cog: set the tooth count with a sneaking click.
feedback.jei.info.gear_cutter: Cuts teeth into a plate: put a metal plate on its table with a right click, and a click with an empty hand (or a stroke of a Crank Linkage) makes one cut. The cog that comes out is of the plate's metal, with the tooth count the cutter is set to: sneak with an empty hand and pick 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32 teeth. Every count is on the same pitch, so any two cogs mesh at the ratio of their teeth: the smaller one turns faster. The metal not left on the cog falls as swarf, more for a cog with fewer teeth. A plate harder than the wheel can bite wears the machine and yields nothing. A heavier metal makes a heavier wheel to spin up.
feedback.tooltip.vice: Seat a thread rod as its screw, then close a piece in its jaws and work it with a hand tool; your other hand stays free.
feedback.jei.info.vice: Holds a piece while you work it. Right-click with a thread rod to seat it as the jaw screw, then right-click with a piece to close the jaws on it; hold a hand tool's use while looking at the vice to file or hammer the clamped piece, with your other hand free. A held piece shifts and loses part of every stroke; a clamped one loses only the play in its screw: a cut thread has little, a rolled thread more, and a softer metal more than a harder one. With no screw the jaws do not close. An empty hand takes the piece out, then the screw.

feedback.rolling_mill.too_cold: Too cold to bond: heat both plates first.
feedback.jei.info.rolling_mill: Rolls an ingot into a plate. A brittle stock (a mineral, crystal, ceramic or glass ingot or gem) does not flatten: the rolls grind it to dust, which reacts and melts faster than the lump. A ductile metal cannot be ground; its dust comes from a melt shattered in water in an atomising mold. Lay a second plate on a plate in the mill and roll it to clad the first with a skin of the second's metal: both plates must be hot enough to bond, and a skin rolled near its melting point comes out burnt. Hand a clad plate to a bench as the wearing part and the tool keeps the coat. Seat a roll by right-clicking with it; the roll sets how hard the mill may drive it. With no roll the mill does nothing.
feedback.gloss.profile.burst: %s%% of the way from 20 to 1500 J a hit carries
feedback.gloss.profile.tempo: %s%% of the way from half a hit to four hits a second
feedback.gloss.profile.precision: %s%% precise: a gun's tight cone, a bow's flat flight, or a light, long, hard-edged blade
feedback.gloss.profile.stealth: %s%% quiet: low report and light weight, a dull edge, a plate that does not clank
skill.feedback.move.concealed_carry.desc: Creatures notice you from nearer the quieter and lighter your held weapon is (stealth 60% or more). An item above the burn line glows and gives no help.
skill.feedback.move.hush_the_kill.desc: A kill on an unaware creature with a weapon of half stealth or more makes no vibration for sculk to hear.
skill.feedback.move.dull_edge.desc: A soft, dull edge (hardness under 2.5) clanks less: blows carry a fifth nearer to sculk sensors and wardens.
skill.feedback.move.clawhold.desc: With claws on your hands, a wall run lasts twice as long on wood, dirt or leaves. Stone and glass give no hold.
skill.feedback.move.opening_cut.desc: Claws on an unaware or back-turned creature open a bleed twice as deep.
skill.feedback.move.gouge.desc: A claw hit on a bleeding creature stacks the bleed, up to three, and leaves it in disorder. Runs half a dose of the pack's potion into the wound.
skill.feedback.move.tear_straps.desc: Claw hits wear each piece of the target's armor, and wear the claws a point a hit (never the last).
skill.feedback.move.burning_ground.desc: Kindle lights any floor, not only what burns, and keeps relighting it while the item stays hot. The item cools by every spot lit.
skill.feedback.move.overwatch.desc: Cast: hold a loaded gun on a lane for five seconds. Everything crossing the aim cone within twenty blocks is pinned, no shot fired, at 6 stamina each. Ends if you move or stow the gun. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.suppressing_fire.des: Held cast: the gun fires a round every few ticks, sweeping across a cone where you look, never on a target. Pin down slows what rounds pass. Ends on empty gun, empty bar or letting go. Costs 20 stamina, then 6 a second.
skill.feedback.move.plate_up.desc: Brace also holds with your armor's toughness: each point adds to what holds a blow.
skill.feedback.move.phalanx.desc: Allies behind you within three blocks are covered by Shield wall too.
skill.feedback.move.pavise.desc: Cast, crouched behind a shield: for four seconds every arrow, bolt and bullet from the front is stopped. The shield wears for the force stopped; you cannot move. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.lee_side.desc: Crouched with a full block against you, tethers pull half as hard and knockback is halved.
skill.feedback.move.called_draw.desc: Called shot works with a bow or crossbow: the next arrow flies at where the creature will be on arrival.
skill.feedback.move.held_draw.desc: A full draw held for a second leaves exactly down your look. Holding drains stamina; past five seconds your hands shake and the steadiness is lost.
skill.feedback.move.tipping_point.desc: A precise weapon (precision 50% or more) landing at the tip of its reach ignores a quarter of armor and does not knock back.
skill.feedback.move.thread_the_gap.desc: A precise weapon's Soft spot blow also staggers the target, longer the more precise the weapon.
cartridge.feedback.band.tip: Named by how much of its case's pressure rating the powder asks: light under %s percent, heavy (+P) from %s percent. More powder in the press is a heavier load; a heavy load wears the gun faster and a load over the rating can burst the case.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_casing: The shell round a charge. Its shape decides whether it holds the blast in or breaks into fragments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_primer: A small starter that sets the whole filler going.
modular.feedback.role.primer.tip: Optional. A booster makes the filler burn through for a harder blast and less fire; a flash primer makes the charge throw fire.
modular.feedback.role.payload.tip: Optional. Hard bits packed round the filler become shrapnel; a luminous powder makes a flash that blinds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shaped_cas: A cone-lined shell: placed against a block, the charge bores into it along a narrow line and breaks only what its power can cut. Thrown, it blasts as any charge.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.booster_pr: Burns the filler through: a harder blast, less fire.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flash_prim: Throws the unburnt filler as fire.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_fuse: A wick or a striker that sets a charge off. A wick burns for a time; a striker goes off on a blow.
modular.feedback.role.fuse.tip: How the charge is set off: a wick burns short, standard or long, or a striker goes off on the first hard hit. A charge with no fuse part burns the standard wick.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.short_fuse: A short wick: about 1.5 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.delay_fuse: A standard wick: about 3 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_fuse: A long wick: about 6 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impact_fus: A striker: a thrown charge goes off on the first thing it hits. A placed charge is lit by hand on the standard wick.
message.feedback.press.missing: Needs a case and a bullet.
message.feedback.press.too_much: A case takes at most %s charge.
message.feedback.gun.chain_fire: A pointed bullet set off the round ahead of it in the tube!
gun.feedback.spent: Spent: the chamber has let go
modular.feedback.desc.variant.boning: Narrow and keen: it does not skid on fat, but tough fiber pulls the cut toward the grain.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.slicer: Long and thin: it follows the stroke across tough fiber, but skids on fat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.turner: A plain blade: turns one piece.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wide_turne: A broad blade: turns two pieces side by side with one click.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.slotted_tu: Slots in the blade let juice run off: each piece loses a tenth of its moisture as it is turned.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.peen: A lean head with its weight in the peen: lighter, but lands a blow a fifth sharper for its weight.
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_beari: The bearing the rotor turns in.
modular.feedback.role.bearing.tip: Optional. Sets how much torque the rotor carries and how much friction heat it makes. A machine with none runs on its frame's own bore.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.right_woun: Wound the usual way round: the motor drives its shaft forward.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.left_wound: Wound the other way round: the motor drives its shaft backward.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.sleeve_bea: A plain bush: cheap, but it makes the most friction heat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ball_beari: Balls in a race: runs cool and carries more torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.roller_bea: Rollers in a race: carries the most torque, with a little friction.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tool_pommel: A weight on the end of the handle, behind the hand.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.knob: A small cap on the handle's end.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ball: A heavier ball behind the hand: the head comes round a little faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flat_ring: A plain flat ring: a mild seal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cup_seal: A cupped seal that grips the case: much less kick, little else.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.double_rin: Two rings: a tighter group, less kick cut.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dot_reticl: A dot that shows in the dark (light level 7 or less).
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ring_retic: A wide ring that shows in dim light (11 or less) but tightens the group less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cross_reti: A fine cross that shows only in deep dark (4 or less) and tightens the group most.
tooltip.feedback.instrument_bag.hint: Click an instrument onto it to stow; right-click it empty-handed to take one out
message.feedback.preheat_not_metal: Not a metal: the field does not couple to it
feedback.jei.info.cryocooler: A cold head on a wire (MV, 6 A). It chills the face it points at, the way it was placed, far under room temperature; a vessel against that face (a Reactor) settles a little short of the head's temperature, and a head with no power holds nothing. Right-click with an empty hand to cycle its stage: deep (about -194 Tu on the vessel), middle (about -190) or shallow (about -185). Compressed air liquefies only at the deep stage; warming that liquid air to the middle stage boils nitrogen off ahead of the oxygen; the shallow stage then boils argon off ahead of the oxygen. Too warm a stage does not separate: the cold liquid simply boils back to air.
feedback.stockpot.thin: There is nothing in it worth ladling.
feedback.tooltip.cable.gauge: Gauge: %s (%s times the standard cross-section: carries that much more, loses that much less)
feedback.electrolytic_cell.anode: Hung as the anode, to dissolve
feedback.electrolytic_cell.cathode: Hung as the cathode, to be plated
feedback.coherer.stuck: Coherer tapped: grains sintered, still welded
feedback.coherer.fused: Coherer: grains fused into one lump, a tap does nothing
feedback.coherer.refilled: Coherer refilled: fresh grains, loose and open
tooltip.feedback.sky_notebook.blank: An empty line, waiting for a planet.
tooltip.feedback.sky_notebook.acid_cloud: A yellow-green disc wrapped in thick cloud. Dense, acid air: hulls corrode, wings bite and thrusters struggle.
tooltip.feedback.sky_notebook.frozen_moo: A small pale blue disc, cold to the poles. Its seas are liquid gas: cryogenic coolant waits there.
tooltip.feedback.sky_notebook.crystal: A violet disc with sharp glints. Huge geodes of crystal hold stored experience.
tooltip.feedback.photograph: A small picture. Use it to look.
feedback.jei.info.camera: Hold use to expose and let go to take a photograph of what you see. A telescope in the other hand is the lens: its magnification crops the picture and its blur softens it (a telescope that is out of focus, a steel tube in the cold, takes a soft picture). With no telescope the camera is a pinhole: no zoom and a soft picture. Use the photograph to look at it.
feedback.jei.info.coherer_clapper: A small electromagnet and iron rod that taps a coherer's grains loose after a spark welds them, and again a moment later while they stay welded. Use it on a coherer to seat it. Without one the coherer stays welded until someone taps it by hand or a controller switches it off.
message.feedback.hammer.no_cam: The hammer has no cam seated.
feedback.jei.info.hammer_cam: A cam is cut from a part you have forged by hand and a metal plate, in a crafting grid; the part comes back. Seated in a Mechanical Hammer (use it on the hammer), it makes the head strike that shape's notes. A cam for another shape plays the wrong notes, and the part comes out worse.
message.feedback.radio.antenna_full: The antenna cannot take more wire.
tooltip.feedback.instrument.fitted: Circuit-fitted: reads in steps %s%% of the bare instrument's.
tooltip.feedback.instrument.fittable: Craft with a Basic Electronic Circuit to read finer.
feedback.xp.run: Run at level %s, %s points; moving %s, leaking %s
feedback.readout.xp_run: Run at level %s, %s points; moving %s, leaking %s
feedback.debug.heat_probe.total: Heat reaching this block: %1$s Tu (ambient %2$s Tu)
feedback.debug.heat_probe.source: from %2$s on the %1$s side: fire %3$s Tu, reach %4$s%% (it faces %5$s)
feedback.diagram.not_on_vehicle: This sensor must be on a vehicle.
gui.feedback.computer.diagram_none: Link a Flight Sensor to an Input card.
screen.feedback.creative.band: Band (0 LV, 1 MV, 2 HV, 3 UHV, 4 EHV, 5 Trunk)
feedback.data_connector.wire: A link that long needs %s wire in your inventory.
feedback.data_connector.fibre: A fiber link that long needs %s fiber in your inventory.
feedback.data_connector.fibre_dead: No fiber you carry would carry a reading that far.
feedback.data_connector.fibre_no_crystal: An optical terminal needs a crystal before a fiber can join it.
feedback.data_connector.range: No wire reaches that far (%s blocks). A circuit with gain at an end reaches further.
feedback.data_connector.mode.clear: cut every link on a node
feedback.readout.faint: Too faint to read: it needs a circuit with gain
feedback.readout.wire.bare: Bare: shocks, and arcs to a bare wire an air block away
feedback.tooltip.cable.insulated: Insulated to %s; a higher band burns it off
feedback.tooltip.cable.bare: Bare: shocks, and arcs to a bare wire an air block away
feedback.jei.cable.gauge_note: Fine wire gives thin cable, wire standard, four wires in a square heavy, and a plate a bus bar
feedback.jei.cable.insulate: Three of an insulating material in a row below coat the cable
feedback.readout.jar.stored: Holds a charge in the %s band
feedback.gloss.jar.charging: drawing current from its line; anything else on the line gets less
feedback.gloss.jar.holding: charged or full and drawing nothing
feedback.gloss.jar.discharging: giving its charge back as a source
tooltip.feedback.reach_probe.empty: Right-click a machine to link it. Sneak-use in the air to forget it.
feedback.jei.info.reach_probe: Right-click a machine that states its reach (a vessel, boiler, pressure vessel or flywheel) to link it. While you carry the probe, a recipe card in the browser sets that machine's reach beside each temperature, pressure and speed the recipe asks for. The figures are the machine's own spec, printed exactly; how finely you read what the recipe asks for is up to the best instrument you carry. Sneak-use in the air to forget the link.
feedback.jei.info.light_meter: A photocell behind a pinhole. Right-click a block to read the light at its face, block light and sky light apart, in steps of two levels. A needle pointed into a source far past its range, or knocked in a fall, reads off; set it against a lit lamp and it reads true again.
tooltip.feedback.copper_bucket.empty: Empty. Use on a fluid source to fill it.
tooltip.feedback.jar_baton.empty: Empty. Use on a charged Leyden jar to draw its charge.
feedback.jei.tool_table_tool.fine: Fine: drawn so on a blueprint in the Engineering Table's blueprint slot, it is made from a quarter of the parts (%s) and stands only in finespace.
feedback.jei.tool_table_tool.dish: Made at the Prep Table: pick this dish there, then put in a container and foods. The parts decide what is made, and a seasoning is poured on at the end.
feedback.jei.tool_table_tool.slots: Six slots; the parts decide what is made, and they may sit in any slot.
feedback.jei.tool_table_part.note: Choose the shape at the table and put the stock in its cells. Steel and the like must be hot.
feedback.jei.tool_table_part.forged: Forged: choose it at the table, put in the stock, and play the pattern. Steel and the like must be hot.
feedback.jei.modular.tip: Tip: a Tip part (a gem, shard or nugget shaped at a bench, harder than the body) in a spare slot, or added to a finished tool in the tool slot. Bites like the tip, holds like the body.
feedback.jei.modular.binding: Binding: a Binding part (string, leather or wire shaped at a bench) in a spare slot, or added to a finished tool. A stronger binding holds a heavier head.
feedback.jei.modular.studs: Studs: gems set in the plate, each covering a tenth. Hardness without a brittle plate.
feedback.jei.modular.grind: Edge: shift-use a grindstone to change it, at a little durability.
feedback.jei.modular.coat: Plate it in an electrolytic cell for a coat: corrosion resistance, and a harder skin on armor.
tooltip.feedback.mold.nothing: This mold can make nothing of it
tooltip.feedback.mold.set: Set: use it to turn it out
feedback.jei.reaction.bed: a bed of the catalyst in the slot
feedback.jei.mined.note: Break the ore with a pick. Silk touch keeps the block.
feedback.jei.material.attenuation.tip: How much light a meter of a fiber drawn from it loses. The lower it is, the longer a fiber link of it reaches cleanly. Absent means it carries no light.
feedback.jei.material.crush_energy.tip: How much a liter of it absorbs as it is crushed, as a foam does. As an armor lining it pads like a harder material would.
feedback.jei.material.kind.tip: What sort of stuff this is. Hover the value to see why it matters.
feedback.jei.material.hardness.tip: How hard it is to cut or deform. Each blow does less work on harder material.
feedback.jei.material.density.tip: Mass per volume. Denser things weigh more and sink in lighter fluids.
feedback.jei.material.melting_point.tip: The temperature where it turns liquid.
feedback.jei.material.boiling_point.tip: The temperature where it turns to vapor.
feedback.jei.material.anneal.tip: Heat it past this and it softens, so it can be worked and relieved of stress.
feedback.jei.material.service.tip: The hottest it can sit for long without weakening.
feedback.jei.material.shock_limit.tip: The sudden jump in temperature it takes without crazing. Past it, a hot piece dropped in cold water is marked.
feedback.jei.material.expansion.tip: How much longer a solid gets for each Tu it warms, in millionths of its length. A telescope tube that is longer or shorter than its lenses want blurs; steel is 12, invar about 1.
feedback.jei.material.oxidation.tip: Above this temperature air starts to burn, char or rust it.
feedback.jei.material.thermal_conductivi: How fast heat moves through it. High means it warms and cools quickly.
feedback.jei.material.cooling_rate.tip: How quickly it loses heat to the air around it.
feedback.jei.material.toughness.tip: How much punishment it takes before it breaks.
feedback.jei.material.ductility.tip: How far it can be bent or drawn before it cracks.
feedback.jei.material.yield.tip: How much load it takes before it stays bent.
feedback.jei.material.friction.tip: How much it grips against other surfaces.
feedback.jei.material.permeability.tip: How much gas a full gas cell wrapped in a skin of it loses each tick. Absent means gas-tight.
feedback.jei.material.abrasiveness.tip: How much it wears down whatever rubs on it.
feedback.jei.material.hardenable.tip: Heating then quenching it makes it much harder.
feedback.jei.material.electrical_conduct: How easily current flows through it.
feedback.jei.material.corrosion.tip: How well it holds up against rust and decay. Higher is better.
feedback.jei.material.flame.tip: How hot it burns when used as fuel.
feedback.jei.material.flash_point.tip: The temperature where it gives off vapor that can catch fire.
feedback.jei.material.burn_ticks.tip: How long it burns as fuel, in ticks (20 ticks is a second).
feedback.jei.material.ignition.tip: The temperature where it ignites as a propellant.
How strongly it speeds up a reaction without being used up.
feedback.jei.material.oxygen_fraction.ti: The share of this gas that is oxygen a lung can use.
feedback.jei.material.xp_top_level.tip: The highest level an XP container of this material can stand at.
feedback.jei.material.xp_capacitance.tip: Points of XP one cell of this material holds.
feedback.jei.material.xp_conductance.tip: Points a tick an XP wire of this material moves for each level of difference.
feedback.jei.material.xp_leak.tip: The share of what moves through the wire that escapes as XP orbs.
feedback.jei.material.moisture.tip: How wet it is. Wet food spoils faster and cooks slower.
feedback.jei.material.fat.tip: How much fat it has. It makes a dish richer and heavier.
feedback.jei.material.fibre.tip: How much fiber it has. It makes a dish denser.
feedback.jei.material.pathogen.tip: How many germs raw it carries. Cooking clears it.
feedback.jei.material.toxin.tip: How much poison it holds. Cooking may not remove it.
feedback.jei.material.qu_note: A figure in Qu is an amount per item: one Qu is the amount of metal in a nugget.
feedback.jei.material.char.tip: The temperature where it burns instead of cooking.
feedback.jei.material.shelf.tip: How much slower it spoils than ordinary food.
feedback.jei.compound.sugar.tip: Eaten, gives a burst of speed. A slowdown follows when it wears off.
feedback.jei.compound.stimulant.tip: Eaten, gives haste. Mining fatigue follows when it wears off.
feedback.jei.compound.protein.tip: Eaten, gives strength for a while.
feedback.jei.compound.mineral.tip: Eaten, gives damage resistance for a while.
feedback.jei.compound.vitamin.tip: Eaten, gives night vision for a while.
feedback.jei.kind.metal.tip: Hammered, cast and rolled into plates, rods and wire. Conducts heat and electricity.
feedback.jei.kind.mineral.tip: Stone, rock and mineral stuff. Hard and heavy, cut or ground, not hammered.
feedback.jei.kind.crystal.tip: Gems and ordered solids. Brittle and clear, cut and ground.
feedback.jei.kind.ceramic.tip: Fired clay. Heat-proof and hard, but it shatters.
feedback.jei.kind.glass.tip: Melted and blown or cast. Clear and brittle.
feedback.jei.kind.granular.tip: Sand, dust and powder. It pours and packs, and is shaped by moulds.
feedback.jei.kind.organic.tip: Wood, bone and plant matter. Light and easy to cut, and it burns.
feedback.jei.kind.grain.tip: Seeds of grasses and legumes. Dry, keeps long, and is milled or boiled.
feedback.jei.kind.vegetable.tip: Roots, leaves and stems. Wet and fibrous, cooked or eaten raw, and spoils.
feedback.jei.kind.fruit.tip: Sweet, juicy plant flesh. Eaten as it is, and spoils fast.
feedback.jei.kind.fungus.tip: Mushrooms. Wet and earthy, cooked or dried.
feedback.jei.kind.flower.tip: Petals and blooms. Light and scented, wilts quickly, and steeps well.
feedback.jei.kind.herb.tip: Leaves, ferns and green stems. Fragrant, dries well, and steeps well.
feedback.jei.kind.animal.tip: Flesh and eggs. Rich in protein, and spoils unless cooked or cured.
feedback.jei.kind.seafood.tip: Fish. Wet and delicate, and spoils fastest of all.
feedback.jei.kind.dough.tip: Flour worked into a mass, then baked or boiled. Kneaded, rolled and cut.
feedback.jei.kind.dish.tip: Cooked and combined foods, served from a pot or bowl.
feedback.jei.kind.fluid.tip: Poured and piped, never cut. It is stored in tanks and moved by pumps.
feedback.jei.kind.composite.tip: Two stuffs bonded into one body that is neither: fiber in resin, veneers in glue. Moulded and laid up like a polymer.
feedback.jei.kind.polymer.tip: Plastics and rubbers. Moulded and cast like a metal, but light and insulating.
feedback.jei.perk.fire_aspect.tip: Sets what it hits on fire. A bare hand gets burned.
feedback.jei.perk.echo.tip: A struck target is outlined and heard by sculk.
feedback.jei.perk.featherlight.tip: Swings as if it were lighter.
feedback.jei.perk.bounce.tip: A struck target is thrown up.
feedback.jei.perk.radiant.tip: A struck target withers and glows.
feedback.jei.perk.siphon.tip: Kills give a little extra experience.
feedback.jei.perk.blink.tip: A kill steps you into its place.
feedback.jei.perk.ring.tip: A struck target is slowed by the sound, and hostile mobs nearby turn on you.
message.feedback.lift.lifted: Lifted. Use to raise, sneak-use to lower, sneak-use at the bottom to put it back as blocks, break the lift to drop it.
message.feedback.lift.lowered: Back in the world as blocks.
message.feedback.lift.blocked: Something is in the way of putting it back as blocks.
message.feedback.lift.too_big: Too big -- is it touching something besides the lift?
message.feedback.lift.on_vehicle: This lift is part of a vehicle -- it can't lift.
message.feedback.lift.loops: %s closed joint loops: they will be stiff and may jitter.
message.feedback.lift.joined: Two vehicles are joined to this one at a joint -- put the joint back to carry them apart.
message.feedback.lift.no_room: No room to put it down here.
feedback.jei.info.voxel_case: A hinged iron case that holds one whole block of finespace. Use it empty on a finespace block and the block's voxels, skins and every machine in it go into the case, as built; use it full on a free spot and the block comes back exactly as it was. It holds one block at a time. A block with a joint or a belt cannot be carried: both are tied to something outside it.
tooltip.feedback.voxel_case.empty: Empty. Use on a finespace block to carry it.
message.feedback.voxel_case.linked: A joint or a belt ties this block to something outside it.
feedback.jei.info.tire_hub: The part that makes a turned body a wheel. Put it on the axle of a body held by a Rotary Bearing, in coarsespace or in finespace, and it declares the wheel's radius: in coarsespace a small, medium or large hub is about three quarters, one and one and a half blocks from the axle to the tread, in finespace a quarter, three eighths and a half of a block. It comes with no tire: use a tire (a rubber's tire, moulded from its ingot) on it to fit one, and the wheel grips, wears and rolls by that rubber. Sneak-use with an empty hand takes the tire off. It has no suspension of its own: the wheel is where it is mounted, so a ride is made smoother by building a slider joint into the mount. A wheel needs the hinge: a hub on a body fixed to its vehicle, with no Rotary Bearing turning it, is not a wheel, has no ring to roll on, and slides along with the body. Tire stock blocks are ordinary blocks now and no longer make a wheel by themselves.
feedback.jei.info.mote: One fine-space voxel of a block, a 64th of it: cut a whole block into 64 motes at an Engineering Table with a saw (any plain, solid, whole block can be cut). Use a mote on any block or on finespace and it goes in the voxel in front of the face you clicked; where there was empty air the click makes the finespace as well. Mining a voxel with the right tool gives the mote back. Parts that work in finespace (shafts, cogs, joints) are placed as themselves.
feedback.jei.info.micro_core: A gauge for building in finespace: hold it in either hand while placing or mining motes and it sets how they go. Sneak-use steps its mode: single, line, box, mirror or wedge. It places nothing itself.
tooltip.feedback.grapple.multi: Second hook: two lines at once
feedback.jei.info.grapple_winch: A drum on a crank in a frame. Craft it with a grapple in the crafting grid to fit it: the reel runs faster.
tooltip.feedback.grapple.barb: Barbed head: reels in lighter creatures
feedback.jei.info.grapple: A hook on a line. Use throws it; it bites a block or a creature. On a block (or a creature heavier than you) you swing from it as a pendulum; hold use to winch the line in, sneak to let go, and the speed you carry when you let go is thrown on. Fittings, each made with the grapple in the crafting grid: 4 string for a longer line, a grapple winch for a faster reel, 2 wrought iron rods for a barbed head that reels lighter creatures to you, 3 wrought iron plates for a second hook head: using the grapple again with a line out throws a second line, and both lines hold you. A line over its load strains and parts.
message.feedback.lift.balance: Mass %s, center of mass (%s) from the lift's top.
commands.feedback.space.no_body: Stand on a body or look at one.
commands.feedback.space.already_there: That body is already in the Gap.
commands.feedback.space.not_there: That body is not in the Gap.
commands.feedback.space.no_gap: The Gap dimension is not loaded.
commands.feedback.no_blueprint: Hold a printed blueprint in your main hand.
commands.feedback.charged: Charged to what the cell can hold.
commands.feedback.no_battery: Hold a battery or an electric gun with a cell in your main hand.
commands.feedback.no_material: That material has no such form.
commands.feedback.feel: Feel: flash %s, roll %s deg, fov pop %s, %s sparks, %s sound.
key.feedback.cast_radial: Cast radial (tap: cast selected, hold: choose)
screen.feedback.skills.needs_trait: Needs a weapon or armor with: %s
feedback.configuration.title: Feedback settings
feedback.configuration.reduceMotion.tool: Drops screen shake, shutters and idle life; keeps sounds and the stage lamp.
feedback.configuration.gainWisp.tooltip: A killing blow that earns skill points sends one small wisp in the tree's color from the fallen creature to you. Applies at once.
feedback.configuration.itemInfoHud.toolt: Show the instrument readout for held items. The key also toggles it.
commands.feedback.combat.parry: Parry (%3$s ticks of ping pad at most): window %1$s t, recovery %2$s t, cone %4$s deg wide, weapon %5$s Mu in %6$s.
commands.feedback.combat.roll: Roll: %1$s t of i-frames, recovery %2$s t, cooldown %3$s t, about %4$s blocks.
commands.feedback.combat.state: State: %1$s, %2$s t left, %3$s t then, %4$s t of i-frames.
commands.feedback.no_gun_skeleton: No early gun in the pool to arm it with.
commands.feedback.build: Gave the item built to the blueprint.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.suppressor: Baffles pull heat from the gas: conductivity quiets it, mass holds the heat. Soft metal softens when hot.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.muzzle_bra: Ports cut by the gas: hardness decides how fast it wears the gun.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.relief_ven: Opens where its metal yields against the barrel's; a soft seat leaks more and wears.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.barrel_shr: Fins shed heat as fast as the metal conducts it, over its mass.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.eddy_sleev: Drags a coupled bullet by how well its metal carries current.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.bayonet: Stabs with the hardness of its blade.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.bipod: Holds the gun by how stiff its legs are.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.counterwei: Cancels kick by its share of the gun's mass; brittle metal slaps worse as the bore wears.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.selector_s: A contact on the sear; it adds select fire.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.hydraulic_: Damps kick by the fluid's viscosity.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.lit_reticl: Cuts spread in the dark by how brightly its mineral glows.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.magnetic_s: Steadies the release by its magnetism, until the Curie heat.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.obturator: Seals the bore: a softer ring seals better, until it burns.
feedback.jei.gun_option.reads.thermal_sl: Fits the barrel tight when cold, binds when hot.
gun.feedback.lodged: The round did not leave the barrel.
gun.feedback.cleared: You push the round out of the bore.
modular.feedback.fig.brace_kick.tip: Share of the kick left when crouched and still: a stock's pad cushions it, a bipod's legs take it.
modular.feedback.fig.folded_brace_kick.t: Share of the kick left when crouched and still with the bipod's legs folded: the stock alone.
modular.feedback.fig.folded_brace_spread: Share of the spread left when crouched and still with the bipod's legs folded: the stock's core alone.
modular.feedback.fig.brace_spread.tip: Share of the spread left when crouched and still: a stock's core and a bipod's legs hold the aim.
modular.feedback.fig.fitting_wear.tip: Share of the gun's life a shot wears away through its fittings: a brake's ports cut by the gas, a vent's seat.
modular.feedback.fig.fitting_limit.tip: The hottest barrel the weakest fitting survives before it softens and, hotter still, runs off the gun.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_bipod: Crouched and still, the legs take the kick: %1$s%% less kick and %2$s%% tighter, by how stiff their metal is.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.counterweigh: Cancels %1$s%% of the kick and slows the cycle %2$s%%, by its share of the gun's mass; brittle metal slaps worse as the bore wears.
feedback.readout.barrel: Bore %1$s mm, wall %2$s mm, length %3$s m
feedback.workpiece.barrel_unmeasured: A bored barrel. Calipers would say how wide.
technique.feedback.heavy_punch: Heavy punch; hold the press after it for a shockwave that shoves creatures and turns projectiles
technique.feedback.punch_projectiles: Punches any projectile back at 2.5x speed
modular.feedback.desc.part.vial_body: A small hollow body, cut from crystal or pressed from paper. Made as a vial, a flask of three cells or a carboy of nine, it holds experience: a bigger one holds more, and the material sets the level it can stand at and how much a cell takes. A material that cannot hold experience makes a vial that holds none.
modular.feedback.role.vial.tip: The vessel itself. Its material sets the level it can stand at and how many points a cell of it holds; its size sets how many cells.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flask: Like a vial body, but three cells of stock: holds three times as much.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.carboy: Like a vial body, but nine cells of stock: holds nine times as much.
item.feedback.gear.joint: Weapon joint rating: +%s of the blow shared
hazard.feedback.tongs_cold: Not hot enough to need them
tooltip.feedback.modular.perk.echo: Echo (struck targets are outlined and heard by sculk)
tooltip.feedback.modular.perk.ring: Ring %s (struck targets are slowed and nearby hostile mobs turn on you)
tooltip.feedback.modular.perk.blink: Blink %s (a kill steps you into its place)
modular.feedback.role.head: head
modular.feedback.desc.part.pickaxe_head: The business end of a pick: a pointed head for breaking stone and ore.
modular.feedback.desc.part.axe_head: A wedge of metal that bites into wood. A fair weapon too.
modular.feedback.desc.part.shovel_head: A broad scoop for digging earth, sand and gravel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.hoe_head: A narrow blade for tilling soil and clearing crops and leaves.
modular.feedback.desc.part.sickle_head: A curved blade that cuts a crop and the plants around it in one sweep.
modular.feedback.desc.part.maul_head: A huge blunt head. It splits wood and staggers what it hits.
modular.feedback.desc.part.glove_body: The body of a glove, worn on the hand. Leather or cloth keeps warm work and a weak shock off the skin, as far as the material stands it. Add a metacarpal plate to fight in it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.metacarpal_pl: A plate over the metacarpal bones, the back of the hand. Hard, dense plate punches harder, guards the wearer and lets a bare hand parry; a heavy one slows the swing. It keeps no heat off the hand.
modular.feedback.desc.part.knife_blade: A thin blade for a hand knife. Its edge wears with every cut.
modular.feedback.desc.part.head_blank: A block of stock hammered to seat in a Mechanical Hammer or Press. Its material, mass and shape set how hard a blow of it can land, and it is what the machine wears.
modular.feedback.desc.part.cleaver_head: A short, heavy chopping edge: four ingots of axe.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spear_head: A long spear point for a pole: reach over damage.
modular.feedback.desc.part.sword_blade: The blade of a sword: reach and a keen edge. It needs a grip.
modular.feedback.desc.part.helmet_plate: A shell for the head. Harder, thicker plate protects more and weighs more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.chestplate_pl: A shell for the chest. Harder, thicker plate protects more and weighs more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.leggings_plat: A shell for the legs. Harder, thicker plate protects more and weighs more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.boots_plate: A shell for the feet. Harder, thicker plate protects more and weighs more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tool_tip: A hard point set into a head or blade. It bites like the tip and holds like the body.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tool_binding: Lashes or pins a head to its handle. A stronger binding holds a heavier head.
modular.feedback.desc.part.sword_guard: A crosspiece between blade and grip. It guards the hand and adds weight near it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.shield_rim: The edge that holds a shield's face together.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crossbow_prod: The bow of a crossbow. Its strength sets how hard it shoots.
modular.feedback.modifier.adjective.head: head-heavy
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.overheat: No heat governor, or a surge shunt: fired fast enough, a shot at the heat limit burns the wielder and wears the barrel. A throttle, a forced vent or a dead-man cutoff stops it.
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.shock: The receiver holds off a cell up to the %1$s band. A stronger cell shocks the wielder and wears the receiver.
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.wet_arc: Fired wet, the pulse arcs back to the wielder unless a glove rated for the cell's band insulates the hand.
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.hot_lock: A heat pellet core locks the gun hot after firing until it has vented, which it does itself after every shot.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.flurry: Every hit on the same target within %1$s s of the last adds %2$s%% damage, up to %3$s hits. A miss, a new target, or taking a hit resets it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.dash: Right click dashes up to %1$s blocks along your look, stopping at a wall, and cuts everything within %3$s blocks of the path for x%2$s your attack damage. Waits %4$s s between dashes.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.hack: Hits an unarmored target for x%1$s but an armored one for only x%2$s. Breaking a leaf, crop or plant also clears the plants within %3$s blocks, at %4$s wear a block swept.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.overhead: A fully charged swing also hits everything within %1$s blocks of the target for %2$s%% of the blow and knocks it back, at %3$s wear each time. A half-charged swing does only %4$s%% and no sweep.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.backstab: Hits x%1$s from behind (more than %2$s degrees off the target's facing) or on a mob with nothing targeted, and a further x%3$s when sneaking. Face to face it deals only x%4$s.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.flourish: A kill readies the next swing at once and grants speed for %1$s s. A hit does x%2$s when %3$s or more other hostiles stand within 3 blocks. Without a kill or a crowd it does nothing.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.timber: Breaking a log fells the connected logs, leaves stay, up to %1$s within %2$s blocks of the first, at %3$s extra wear a log. Sneak to fell just one; it stops short of breaking the tool.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.throw: Hold use to wind up and release to throw; a tap under %1$s s does nothing. The blow gains %2$s%% a block flown, up to x%3$s, and costs %4$s wear. It tumbles end over end, so it lands full only head-first, at some distances and not others, and it lies where it fell until picked up.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.hook: A blow the target blocks with a shield disables that shield for %1$s s and drags the target toward you (pull %2$s). With no shield to catch, the hook only snags and the blow lands at x%3$s.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.sounding: Right click sends a pulse that outlines every ore within %1$s blocks for each stick of the haft through the stone, each in the color of its metal or mineral, for %2$s s, to you alone (the nearest %5$s). It reads and never mines faster; %3$s s between pulses and %4$s wear each.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.vein: Breaking an ore also breaks the connected ore of the same block, up to %1$s more, at %2$s extra wear each. Sneak to switch it off; it stops short of the tool's last point.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.spear_charge: The jab cannot land within %1$s blocks. Hold use to charge: anything between %1$s and %2$s blocks ahead that you close on at %3$s blocks a second or more is hit, harder when faster and with a heavier head; from %4$s it knocks back. The charge lasts about %5$s s, shorter if the head outweighs its binding, and each hit costs more wear the faster it lands (a point per %6$s blocks a second).
modular.feedback.desc.variant.needle: Like a tool tip, but a thin point: two pieces. The edge bites more and chips sooner.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.capped: Like a tool tip, but a thick cap: three pieces. The edge resists chipping and bites less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wrapped: Like a binding, but wound twice: two lengths. Holds a head on a longer handle better.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.double: Like a binding, but wound and crossed: three lengths. The strongest joint, and the most weight at the neck.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crossguard: Like a sword guard, but a long bar: three pieces. Hold use to raise the blade and the bar takes half of a blow from the front, at a point of wear a blow.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.knuckle: Like a sword guard, but a swept hilt forged in a run of taps and heavies. Lighter, and it keeps the weight nearer the hand.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel: A broad disc: two pieces. Sits further behind the hand and lowers the blade's moment.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.counterwei: A heavy knob: three pieces. A strong counterweight, and a lot of metal for it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.banded: Like a shield rim, but a wide band: two pieces. The face holds a little more before it gives.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flanged: Like a shield rim, but an edge turned in on itself: three pieces. The face holds much more before it gives.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.war_pick: Like a pickaxe head, but forged in a run of heavy blows into a thin spike. Hits hard and digs nothing.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.blocking: Hold use to raise the blade. The crossguard takes %1$s%% of a blow from the front and the rest comes through; each blow caught costs %2$s wear. It is a bar of metal and no shield.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.knuckles: Like a metacarpal plate, but a bar across the fingers: four ingots. Punches much harder, guards the back of the hand far less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.claws: Like a metacarpal plate, but three prongs ground from six ingots, a good part lost as swarf. Light, so it slows the swing little. A bare-handed hit opens a bleed that keeps hurting for a few seconds, but the blow itself lands softer and the plate covers almost nothing.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.round: Like a helmet shell, a plain dome of five ingots.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.conical: Like a helmet shell, but forged to a cone. Lighter, thicker where a blow lands.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ridged: Like a helmet shell, but with a ridge over the crown. Heavier, much thicker along the ridge.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tailed: Like a helmet shell, but with a tail behind: six ingots, heavier.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pointed_fa: Like a helmet shell, but drawn to a point over the face. A little heavier and thicker.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.brigandine: Like a chestplate shell, but small plates riveted under cloth: seven ingots, a little lighter, less cover. Each stud set in it bites whoever strikes you in melee.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.breastplat: Like a chestplate shell, but one solid shell: nine ingots, the heaviest. Takes a share of fall and explosion damage.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.hauberk: Like a chestplate shell, but rings, forged in a run of light taps. Cuts the damage of bladed weapons, but crushing weapons go through it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.scale: Like a chestplate shell, but small plates overlapping like fish scales, forged in a quick run of taps. Lighter and thinner, and a point finds fewer gaps.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.lamellar: Like a chestplate shell, but laced rows of narrow plates, forged in triplets of taps. Close to the standard in weight, a little thinner.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.segmented: Like a chestplate shell, but banded hoops, forged in heavy blows. Heavier and thicker, and a point meets more plate.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.plain_legg: Like a leggings shell, as it comes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.articulate: Like a leggings shell, forged hard and light in turn. A sprinting kick throws hostile mobs back.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.mail_chaus: Like a leggings shell, but rings, forged in a run of light taps. Cuts the damage of bladed weapons, but crushing weapons go through it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.quilted: Like a leggings shell, but stitched padding forged flat. Light and thin.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.sabatons: Like a boots shell, but plated over the foot: six ingots, heavy. Landing from a height crushes the hostile mobs beneath, and a soft landing costs nothing.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.plain_boot: Like a boots shell, as it comes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wrapped_bo: Like a boots shell, but strips wound about the foot. Light and thin, quiet to wear.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.open_face: Arrows, bolts and thrown weapons do x%1$s of their damage to you. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.closed_visor: Projectiles do only x%1$s of their damage to you, but mobs see you x%2$s as well. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.studded: Whoever strikes you in melee takes %1$s damage for each stud set in this piece, at most %2$s, and the piece loses %3$s condition a bite. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.collar: A critical hit or a backstab does less bonus damage to you: a stiff collar takes %1$s%% of the bonus, a flexible one (chain, leather, fiber) %2$s%%. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.pauldron: An overhead blow does %1$s%% less to you, and so does a falling block, anvil or stalactite, at %2$s%% less. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.poleyn: A fall does %1$s%% less damage to you, and a kick or a leg sweep staggers you %2$s%% less. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.vambrace: With your main hand empty, or against a blow of %1$s damage or less, the forearm turns a melee blow: %2$s%% less damage and %3$s%% less shove. A disarming shot cannot pull what you hold. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.hobnails: On ice you lose %1$s%% of the speed it gives each tick, so you do not slide; but the nails ring, and mobs see you %2$s%% better. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.rigid: Fall and explosion damage to you is x%1$s. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.mail: Bladed weapons (swords, axes, blades) do x%1$s to you; crushing ones (mauls, maces) do x%2$s. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.push_through: Cobweb, powder snow and berry bushes slow you less: your mass over %5$s Mu of the slow is taken back, at most %1$s%%. Each tear costs %2$s hunger and %3$s wear, then %4$s s before the next. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.braced: Knockback pushes you only x%1$s as far, but you swim %2$s%% slower. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.trample: Landing from %1$s blocks or more lands on every creature within %2$s blocks, with %3$s Mu of shell added to your weight: each takes the fall by your share of the two masses and staggers by the drop's energy, and you take half the fall damage. A shockwave shoves everything nearby outward, at %4$s wear; landing on wool, snow or leaves costs no fall damage at all. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.spurs: Starting a sprint gives speed %2$s for %1$s s, once every %3$s s. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.scoop: Digging a shovel block also digs its neighbors across your facing, a row %1$s wide, at %2$s extra wear each. Sneak to dig one.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.quarry: Mining a pickaxe block also mines the blocks around it in the face you struck, a %1$s-wide square, at %2$s extra wear each. Sneak to mine one.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.trench: Digging a shovel block also digs the %1$s block(s) beyond it along your look, down when you look steeply down, at %2$s extra wear each. Sneak to dig one.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.kama: Tilling a block also tills the %1$s blocks beyond it, each costing the wear of a tilling, then %2$s s before the next use. Sneak to till one.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.rake: Breaking a crop draws every dropped item within %1$s blocks to your feet, at %2$s wear a stack. Sneak to leave the drops.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.scythe: Cutting a crop, leaf or plant also cuts the ring two blocks out on its level, a five-by-five with the sickle's own ring, at one wear per %1$s blocks of it. Blows on mobs land at %2$s%%. Sneak to cut one.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.billhook: A blow opens a bleed of %1$s damage a second for %2$s s that does not stack, but the blow itself lands at %3$s%%.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.reaping: Cutting a crop plants it again from its own drops, one item taken, at %1$s wear a replant. It cuts one plant at a time, no sweep. Sneak to cut without replanting.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.slam: A fully charged swing at the ground sends a shockwave: dust, a thud and a shove outward through everything within %1$s blocks, at %2$s%% strength. It spends the charge and costs %3$s wear each time.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.spring: Right click cocks the fitted spring; the next blow lets it go for the damage its volume and stiffness store, then it must be reset for %1$s s. A sword's release also lunges you forward. Armor throws the shock back into the spring (the head rates it %2$s here): worked past its rating it takes a set and stores less, far past it and it snaps, ruining part of the tool and hurting your hand. On a thrown head the spring adds to the throw instead, with almost no wind-up, and the same overload applies (rated %3$s).
modular.feedback.desc.trait.pierce: The blow ignores %1$s%% of the target's armor and toughness, and dents it: an armored target is slowed for %2$s s. Against bare flesh it is only a small hammer.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.butcher: x%1$s against animals, and each food drop of an animal it kills has a %2$s%% chance of a second helping. Against monsters it is a poor weapon, x%3$s.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.line_cut: The blow carries through the target and hits the nearest other thing in line behind it, up to %1$s blocks past, for %2$s%% of the blow; the main blow is only %3$s%%. Costs %4$s wear when the second target is struck.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.smash: A fall onto a target lands the mace's smash: bonus damage by the fall, scaled by the head's mass, and a shove around the target.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.bearded: Like an axe head, but with an extra ingot: a heavier head that hits a little harder.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.broad_face: Like a hammer head, but six cells of stock. Heavier, so it lifts the blow ceiling by half.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.narrow_fac: Like a hammer head, but two cells of stock. Concentrates the blow: three quarters of the ceiling for half the stock.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.spring_ham: Like a maul head, but with a spring cocked inside. Right click to cock it, and the next blow lands with the stored energy.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.spring_bla: Like a spear head, but a light blade thrown from a spring: quick to throw and fast, and a heavy one overloads the spring.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.war_hammer: Like a maul head, but small. Quicker and lighter, and it staggers little; it hits through armor.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.butcher: Like a cleaver head, but trimmed. A little lighter; it is made for meat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.bardiche: Like a cleaver head, but a long blade on a long edge. Reaches further and cuts through to the one behind.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.mace: Like a maul head, but a round block of stock. A fall onto a target lands a smash scaled by its mass.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.prospector: Like a pickaxe head, but thin and long. Lighter and quicker, with a keen edge that chips more easily. Right click a block with it: if the block bears metal, glints in each metal's own color fly off the face, more where more is held; a block that bears nothing puffs gray dust. A finer point shows more and wears faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.miner: Like a pickaxe head, but thick. Slower, with an edge that resists chipping.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.scoop: Like a shovel head, but wide: one more ingot of cells. Swings slower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.trench: Like a shovel head, but narrow and thick. Hits hard and the edge is tough.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.kama: Like a sickle head, but a broad blade of three cells that also tills.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rake: Like a hoe head, but light and thin. Quicker, and it hits weakly.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.billhook: Like a sickle head, but hooked and heavier at the tip. Hits a little harder.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.reaping_ho: Like a sickle head, but small and curved. Quick, and it hits lightly.
tooltip.feedback.part.worked: Worked to %s%% of the drawing (under: thick and heavy; over: thin and light)
forge.feedback.unmovable: No blow here moves this metal.
feedback.jei.info.hafted_tool: Every tool held by a haft is this one item: a haft with one to three faces (a pick, an axe, a blade, a point, a hammer, a file) on its front, back and top mounts. What it does is what its faces do: it digs what they dig, strips, tills or flattens as they do, smashes, charges or is thrown as its build allows, and works a piece held in the other hand when a face is a hammer, a file or a drill: hold use and each stroke lands one blow, cut or hole until you let go, the piece comes back as it is, and the tool wears a point per stroke. Each face wears on its own; the tool is spent only when every face is.
modular.feedback.role.casing.tip: The shell round a charge: it holds the blast in or breaks into fragments.
modular.feedback.role.module_casing.tip: The shell of a suit module: it carries the rest and sets its weight.
modular.feedback.role.launcher_seat.tip: Where the launcher stores the work that drives a shell: a spring, a pressure reservoir, a solenoid or a boiler. Its volume and its metal's stiffness set the work it holds; the receiver sets what it can take.
modular.feedback.role.filler.tip: Propellant powder packed in. The more of it, the bigger the blast, as a square root.
modular.feedback.role.filler_b.tip: A second powder in the blend. Fuel and oxidizer burn best balanced: too much fuel and the charge is weak and throws fire.
modular.feedback.fig.blast.tip: Explosion power of the packed filler in its casing. About 4 is a block of TNT.
modular.feedback.fig.swing_drag.tip: Share of attack speed the metacarpal plate's weight takes off every swing while the glove is worn.
modular.feedback.fig.fist.tip: Damage added to a swing with nothing in the hand. No effect on a weapon. Set by the metacarpal plate's hardness and density.
modular.feedback.fig.strike_st.tip: The most St a blow of this head carries in a Mechanical Hammer or Press, before wear. Set by its material, mass and shape, never the machine.
modular.feedback.fig.burned.tip: The share of the filler that burns. Under 0.9 the rest goes up as fire.
modular.feedback.fig.packed.tip: How many items of filler are in it.
modular.feedback.role.body.tip: The glove itself. Leather or cloth keeps warm work and a weak shock off the hand, as far as the material stands it.
modular.feedback.role.metacarpal.tip: A plate over the back of the hand. Harder, denser plate punches harder and guards you; a heavy one slows the swing. Lets a bare hand parry a melee blow.
modular.feedback.role.ratchet.tip: A turned pawl and toothed ring fitted to a screwdriver's handle. You wind without regripping and the green band holds steadier between pulls, but a pawl of soft or weak metal slips over its teeth under a hard pull and the torque stops climbing.
modular.feedback.role.pitch_linkage.tip: A rod linkage in the hub that turns the blades. A controller card sets the pitch as a level, from reverse through fine to coarse; without one the blades stay at their built pitch.
modular.feedback.role.edge_guard.tip: A plate strip down the haft that stiffens it. It carries part of the joint's load, and costs mass and balance.
modular.feedback.role.lanyard.tip: A chain from weapon to hand. Thrown, it reels what it hits and pulls the weapon back weakly, at a cost in throw speed. Held, a disarming shot cannot strip it from you.
modular.feedback.role.rest.tip: A padded rest for the arm or stock: steadier aim.
modular.feedback.role.stabiliser.tip: A counter-mass slug on a rod: steadier hold and less kick, slower to raise.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.steady: A rest cuts the shot's spread.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.stabiliser: A counter-mass steadies the hold and cuts the shot's spread, but the weapon is slower to bring up.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.lanyard: Thrown, it reels what it hits and pulls the weapon weakly back, at a cost in throw speed. A disarming shot cannot strip it from your hand.
modular.feedback.role.boss.tip: A metal dome on the face. It answers a turned blow with a bash and a shove, and costs mass and a weak spot.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.boss: A blow the shield turns hurts the attacker and shoves them back.
feedback.jei.info.draw_gauge: A spring balance with a hook. Hold it in one hand and a bow, a crossbow, a spring or a spring gun in the other, and use it: the draw time, launch speed and stored energy are read off the weapon and stamped on it, exact, as they were then. A stamp stays when the weapon wears; read it again to refresh it.
message.feedback.measure.nothing: Hold something made in the other hand.
feedback.readout.hardness.between: scratched by file %2$s, not by file %1$s
feedback.gloss.hint: Hold Shift: what the words mean
feedback.gloss.overloaded: load past what the run's sources can drive: the run stops
feedback.gloss.straining: load over %s%% of what the run's sources can drive
feedback.gloss.electric.live: a packet reaches this block, and every amp asked for arrives
feedback.gloss.lamp: how much of its power the panel gets, in four steps; a step changes only when the supply moves well past the boundary
feedback.gloss.lamp.burnt: the panel took far more than its rated band and is dead for good; break it and place a new one
feedback.gloss.electric.starved: fewer amps arrive than this machine asks for
feedback.gloss.seized: it ran too hot and locked up; it will not turn until it has cooled
feedback.gloss.jammed: the output is fouled; an empty hand on the cutter clears it
feedback.gloss.electric.blocked: a higher-band source on this line supplies it instead
feedback.gloss.plating.sound: coat between %1$s and %2$s Qu, one metal
feedback.gloss.plating.porous: coat under %1$s Qu: it has not closed
feedback.gloss.plating.burnt: over %4$s%% of the coat grew at more current than the piece's size takes
feedback.gloss.plating.chipped: a brittle coat loses a share to every hard hit; firing it again in a kiln restores it
feedback.gloss.plating.mixed: under %3$s%% one metal: the electrolyte let a second plate

feedback.gloss.modular.balanced: balance under %s, the moment sitting near the hand
feedback.gloss.modular.keen: edge ground to bite x%s, chipping x%s as readily
feedback.gloss.modular.blunt: edge ground to bite x%s, chipping x%s as readily
feedback.gloss.modular.brittle: edge toughness under %s of its hardness

modular.feedback.fig.balance: Balance, head's share of the swing's moment
modular.feedback.fig.joint: Joint, leverage over what it carries
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip: Every part's volume times its material's density, added up. A heavier piece hits harder and swings slower; heavy armor slows the wearer.
modular.feedback.fig.balance.tip: How much of the swing's moment sits in the head. Near 1 is head-heavy: more force at the tip, but slower to bring round.
modular.feedback.fig.swing.tip: Swings a wielder can manage each second. Falls with the mass and how far out it sits from the hand.
modular.feedback.fig.impact.tip: Energy in one blow: the striking mass at the tip's speed. Damage and dig speed both grow with its square root.
modular.feedback.fig.bite.tip: How readily the edge cuts: its hardness against its strength, as it was ground. Scales damage and dig speed.
modular.feedback.fig.reach.tip: Extra blocks of range over the hand, from how long the handle is.
modular.feedback.fig.damage.tip: Health taken off a target by one blow at full condition. Built from bite, impact and the head's shape, less wear.
modular.feedback.fig.attack_speed.tip: Swing rate as the game counts it: swings per second, less any wear.
modular.feedback.fig.dig_speed_off.tip: How fast the second head breaks the blocks it digs.
modular.feedback.fig.hardness_off.tip: The second head's edge hardness. It gates which blocks that head can dig.
How well the second head's edge resists chipping.
modular.feedback.fig.dig_speed.tip: How fast it breaks the blocks it digs. Built from bite and impact, less wear.
modular.feedback.fig.durability.tip: Uses before it is spent: the wearing edge's volume times how well its material holds its hardness.
modular.feedback.fig.enchantability.tip: How readily enchanting takes, from the main material.
modular.feedback.fig.joint.tip: The leverage the head puts on the joint, over what the handle and binding can carry. Over 1 it works loose.
modular.feedback.fig.hardness.tip: The wearing edge's hardness. It gates which blocks the item can dig.
modular.feedback.fig.edge_toughness.tip: How well the edge resists chipping. Hard, brittle edges chip on what a tough one shrugs off.
modular.feedback.fig.armour_toughness.ti: Blunts hard hits that armor points alone would let through.
modular.feedback.fig.knockback_resistanc: Share of knockback the wearer shrugs off, from the plate's density; on boots, a coat grippier than the plate adds to it and a slicker one takes from it.
modular.feedback.fig.slow.tip: Share of walking speed the wearer gives up to carry the mass past what is free.
modular.feedback.fig.capacity.tip: The most damage a shield stops outright.
modular.feedback.fig.draw.tip: Ticks to draw the bow; fewer is quicker.
modular.feedback.fig.velocity.tip: Launch speed against a vanilla bow's.
modular.feedback.fig.corrosion.tip: 0 to 1: how well it survives water, the wearing part's own and any coat's together.
