message.feedback.mixer.refused: The drum takes any material, up to a full load.
message.feedback.mixer.frozen: A molten metal in the drum has set solid: heat the drum before drawing.
message.feedback.mixer.draw_blocked: Nothing to draw, or the last draw is still waiting at the output.
feedback.jei.info.mixer: A drum on a vertical shaft. Right click with an item to pour one in; items from a hopper or the input slots go in one at a time while there is room. A fluid with a material (molten metals among them) is a part of the mixture too, from a pipe. Turning mixes them: draw too early and only the mixed share is kept; keep turning past the blend and the drum grinds it, heats it, and a powder load goes up. Draw with the button in the screen; the mixture table decides what the batch becomes, and a batch no row names comes out as a Mixture item.
feedback.jei.info.smithing_table: Where metal parts are shaped: pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of a Hand Hammer from its slot. Stock must be at its working temperature.
feedback.jei.info.anvil: The Smithing Table's upgrade: it shapes metal the same way and also forges, playing a rhythm pattern for the forged variant of a part. Set a Hearth against it on a lit fire to keep the stock hot while you play. A bloom set in the center is shingled here: strike it hot to squeeze the slag out, turn it to herd the rest. The Repair tab mends the item in its first slot with what it is made of (a foreign tool takes its own repair material, a quarter of its durability a piece, or a second damaged copy of itself) and names it from the box above; a hammer in the hammer slot takes a point of wear.
feedback.jei.info.woodworking_table: Where wood, bone, leather, fiber and paper parts are shaped. Pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of a tool from its slot. The Saw tab cuts planks with a saw, and the blade's kerf falls as wood shavings; an axe strips a log.
feedback.jei.info.stonecutter: Where stone, ceramic, glass and crystal parts are shaped. Pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of a Sawblade from its slot. A cut made with a Data Stick in the off hand is recorded for a Power Cutter.
feedback.jei.info.prep_table: Where dishes are made. Pick a dish, put food in its cells, and cut with a knife from its slot. Shape a dough on the Parts tab to choose its crust: a pie closed or lattice, a wrap rolled or flat, a bread loaf, flat or rolled. A closed or rolled crust holds more and keeps moisture in, slow to cook through; a lattice or flat one lets steam out, cooks sooner and dries out sooner.
feedback.jei.info.blueprint_table: Draw a modular item here and print it on paper. The blueprint predicts the figures the parts would give if they came out exactly to drawing; what an item really has is read off the item with an instrument. A second slot beside the paper holds a blueprint to copy: press Copy with blank paper in the paper slot and the original stays. A cartridge in the round slot reads a drawn gun against it: chamber charge against what the walls hold, muzzle speed and Work, kick, spread, heat and the damage ceiling, worked out for parts exactly to drawing.
feedback.jei.info.enchanting_table: Open it with a part to enchant. The part is held while the screen is open and handed back when it closes.
feedback.jei.info.reloading_press: Use it to open it. Seat a bullet and a charge in a case to make a cartridge. The bullet's shape is the bullet you seat. A nugget makes buckshot; birdshot, large shot and flechettes are their own items. A nugget in the core slot sits inside a bullet's jacket. A brewed potion in the payload slot is sealed in a glass vial in the bullet and let go where the round lands. A seed, a strand of string or a lump of slime also go in the payload slot. Leave the charge slots empty and it seats a shell, which a launcher's seat drives; a fuse made at the part bench goes in the fuse slot (a delay, an impact, an inertia or a proximity fuse). Grain in the charge slots with no case makes a rocket: the grain burns in flight and the shell carries on under its own thrust.
feedback.jei.info.firebox: A brick hole with a fire in it. Right-click with fuel to load it, and with an empty hand to take back fuel that has yet to catch. Set a Crucible or Boiler on top and it climbs toward the flame's temperature. Only real fuels burn here, by what they are made of.
feedback.jei.info.stockpot: A pot, made from five plates of one metal in a U; the metal sets how fast it follows its fire. It cooks a batch over a lit Firebox. Pour in up to two water buckets, add up to six foods raw or cooked, shake in salt, and ladle out bowls with a bowl in hand. Stir and skim with a spoon, and read it with an empty hand; sneak with an empty hand to tip it out, which burns if the pot is hot.
feedback.jei.info.drying_rack: A rack that dries food slowly. Right-click with a food to hang it, up to four, and right-click empty-handed to take the last one back. Dried food feeds less but keeps much longer; drying runs faster in warm air, and rain stops it, so put a roof over it.
feedback.jei.info.hearth: A brick pan that keeps an Anvil hot. Set it on a Firebox or any fire with an Anvil against one of its sides, and light the fire. The pan warms to about nine tenths of the fire's heat, so hot-working stock in the Anvil stays workable while you forge.
feedback.jei.info.ice_box: A chest that keeps food cold for as long as it has ice. Put ice in with the food; it melts away in about ten minutes. A Refrigeration Unit set against the box and wired up holds it near freezing with no ice used.
feedback.jei.info.controller: A mechanical logic box that reads sensors, compares numbers and switches things on or off. Write a program onto a Punch Card at the Programmer, then right-click the Controller with the card to load it. It is the step up from a Timer or Bimetallic Strip. Use a circuit on it for a faster clock and quieter sensor readings; an empty hand takes the card out, then the circuit.
feedback.jei.info.programmer: Where Controller programs are written onto Punch Cards. Different programmers write onto different things and make changes at different ease, but every one says the same things. Write the program, then load the printed card into a Controller.
feedback.jei.info.thermometer: Turns glowing orange into a number. Carry it and the temperature of items and blocks shows in tooltips and Jade, in steps of 25 Tu. Dipped in something too hot, or dropped from a height, it reads off afterwards; touch it to melting ice and it reads true again. A Pyrometer reads a vessel from further away.
feedback.jei.info.pyrometer: A Thermometer with a lens in it. Right-click a vessel up to 24 blocks away to read its temperature in steps of 10 Tu, whether the furnace is sealed or open.
feedback.jei.info.pressure_gauge: Turns the boiler is groaning into a number. Right-click a boiler, vessel, pipe or tank to read its pressure in steps of 0.5 Pu. A needle pushed past its spring or knocked in a fall reads off; touch it to open air and it reads true again.
feedback.jei.info.geiger_counter: Listens for radiation. It clicks a few times a second with nothing near and faster the stronger the field. Carry it to see the rate in Ru from the last five seconds of clicks; it reads the field before your armor, so it shows why to shield. A field too faint for the counter gives no reading; a circuit with gain fitted lowers that floor.
feedback.jei.info.dosimeter: Reads the dose you carry, the running total that makes you ill in steps. The dose builds while you stand in radiation and drops once you leave it.
feedback.jei.info.starter: An electric starter motor bolted onto one face of an engine. Starting the engine turns it over on the battery the starter touches, or a battery on the wire it touches. A flat battery gives no start. An engine with no starter starts with a click or a controller.
feedback.jei.info.radiator: A finned radiator bolted onto one face of an engine. It sheds the engine's heat to the air, and sheds much more with a coolant in the engine's tank: pipe a liquid in through the radiator's face. A hot engine loses power, wears above its metal's limit and seizes if it gets much hotter.
feedback.jei.info.temperature_sensor: A thermometer bolted onto a crucible or Improved Furnace. It reads the vessel's temperature all the time in steps of 10 Tu, and a Controller program can act on that reading.
feedback.jei.info.electroscope: Two thin copper foil leaves in a glass jar that spread apart when they touch something charged. It reads the band of a live line, and nothing finer; it is a deliberately rough instrument and the cheapest electrical one.
feedback.jei.info.galvanometer: A needle that swings when current runs through it. Hold it near a block in a circuit to read how much current flows through it, in steps of 0.25 A. A trickle too faint for the needle gives no reading at all; a circuit with gain fitted lowers that floor.
feedback.jei.info.current_sensor: A small galvanometer bolted onto one face of a Copper Cable. It reads the current through that cable all the time, in steps of 0.5 A, so a Controller program can act on it.
feedback.jei.info.balance_scale: Tells exactly how heavy a tool, weapon or piece of armor is, in tenths of a Mu. The tooltip gives a rough word for weight, and the scale gives the number.
feedback.jei.info.survey_meter: Shows the ore and oil within 16 blocks, so you can dig where the ground holds them. It needs no power, and its counts are rounded to 8 and wobble a little.
feedback.jei.info.xp_meter: Reads experience as numbers: the level something stands at and the points it holds. Right-click a Crystal Holder, an XP wire, a Creative XP Source, the air, a player or a villager to read it.
feedback.jei.info.burner: A burner for liquid and gas fuel, fed by a pipe or bucket. It heats whatever sits on top, a Crucible, Boiler or Reactor, toward the flame's temperature. It holds 2000 mB and burns 10 mB a second whenever it has fuel; any fluid that burns will do. Built from a nozzle part: its bore sets the fuel burned, its shape the flame; an optional flame holder runs a little hotter.
feedback.jei.info.breaker: A switch for electricity. Closed, it is a piece of wire; open, the line is split in two. Right-click to open or close it, or let a Controller switch it with a Switch card. Above 4 A it trips itself open until someone closes it by hand. Built with cables in place of the copper wire, it takes their gauge and trips at that cable's rating.
feedback.jei.info.bellows: Blows air into whatever it touches, and air makes a fire burn hotter. Drive it with a Crank Linkage, set it in front of the linkage, and touch it to a Firebox, a furnace, a valve or a Pressure Vessel. It is the only way past a fuel's normal temperature.
feedback.jei.info.bimetallic_strip: Two metals bonded together that bend when hot. Clip it to a Crucible and anything it touches switches on while the crucible is below its trip temperature and off above it. Set it against the thing to switch, such as a Clutch or Valve.
feedback.jei.info.compressor: Squeezes gas into a pipe or Gas Tank past the point where it flows by itself, raising a line's pressure. Place it against the block it draws from, with its shaft across the flow. It moves gas only, at 0.4 mB a tick for every RPM, and heats what it moves. Built from a rotor part (Chemical Treatise II): diameter and staging set flow, load and heat; an optional intercooler cools the gas.
feedback.jei.info.damper: A vent flap built against a Crucible, the opposite of the Powered Bellows. Open, it lets heat out at twice what a bare crucible loses, and up to four count. Right-click to open or close it, or let a Timer, Bimetallic Strip or Controller do it.
feedback.jei.info.hydride_bed: A box of hydrogen-absorbing metal. Use a palladium, magnesium or titanium ingot on it to load one (sneak with an empty hand to take one out). Hydrogen piped in is soaked up at low pressure while the bed is cool, a great deal for the size, and held until the bed is heated past its release temperature, when it gives the gas back faster the hotter it is. Heat it too far with gas in it and the metal cracks.
feedback.jei.info.pyro_plate: A thin plate of a pyroelectric crystal (tourmaline is the strongest) with two wires for electrodes. Set it against anything with a temperature: it answers only to change, giving a reading for a Controller (and a sneak-use) while that thing warms or cools, and nothing while it holds steady.
feedback.jei.info.levitation_plate: A slab of a diamagnetic material, two plates of it side by side. Over a powered Electromagnet it turns slick, and built into a vehicle it is lifted off the magnet. Bismuth lifts best, graphite nearly as well, gold barely.
feedback.jei.info.levitation_sleeve: A plate and a rod of a diamagnetic material. Use it on a shaft, flywheel or rotary bearing to fit it: with a powered Electromagnet touching, the drag falls. Bismuth cushions best.
feedback.jei.info.coupling_sleeve: A plate and a rod of one metal. Use it on a rotary bearing to fit it: the piece it turns is no longer a flywheel on the line but gears to the shaft. A shaft faster than the piece spins it up and is loaded by it; a piece faster than the shaft slows and drives the shaft. Only in the role that follows the shaft. Stronger metals carry more torque.
feedback.jei.info.electromagnet: The first machine that runs on electricity. While powered it pulls nearby dropped iron, steel, cast iron, hardened steel and netherite items toward itself, in any form, and pushes diamagnetic things (bismuth most, then graphite, and a little gold, silver, lead and copper) away. Eight Copper Wire wrapped around a Wrought Iron Ingot make one. Built from a core part: turns set pull and current, shape trades pull against reach; an optional yoke adds pull.
feedback.jei.info.lamp: Vanilla's redstone lamp is a block lit by a redstone signal. This one is an electroluminescent glowstone panel: a 0.5 A load on an MV power line that glows in four steps (off, dim, bright, full) by how well it is fed, and keeps its step steady near a boundary. A smaller packet (a long cable run) only dims it. A band over its rating wears it dimmer for good, and a packet far past its rating burns the panel out at once. Built from a filament part: thickness sets the draw and the life; an optional ballast rides overvoltage.
feedback.jei.info.gas_tank: A big pressure vessel for gas, a shell built like the Pressure Vessel's but many times the size. Its metal, wall and shape set how much it holds and the pressure it risks letting go at. Plain flow fills it to four fifths of its danger line and a Gas Compressor fills it higher. Right-click with an empty hand to read its contents and pressure. Optional addons: hoop bands and a relief valve, as on the Pressure Vessel.
feedback.jei.info.gas_turbine: A rotation source that burns fuel gas continuously. At full spool it turns 240 RPM and supplies up to 300 Su on its shaft. It needs blades before it runs, takes fuel from any fluid tank or pipe touching it, and a hotter fuel gives more power for less.
feedback.jei.info.heat_exchanger: A wall that carries heat from the hotter thing on one side to the cooler thing on the other, faster the bigger the difference, until they level. Built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table (Chemical Treatise II): the tube metal's conductivity and the area you give it set how fast. Finned tubes present more area. It needs no power, switch or setting: place it with a thermal block on each end of its axis. An optional fin stack of a second metal adds to the heat that crosses.
feedback.jei.info.hand_crank: The simplest source of rotation. Hold right-click to keep it turning, and it coasts down when you let go. It delivers 12 Su at 32 RPM, enough for the lightest work; the workshop machines need more than a crank can give. Built from a crank arm: a longer arm is more Su and slower; an optional flywheel steadies it.
feedback.jei.info.leyden_jar: A glass jar lined with foil that stores a charge, built at a Stonecutter from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. More plate area holds more charge; thinner glass holds more again but leaks it away much faster. The glass must insulate, and how well it insulates is the band the jar is rated: it charges when fed that band or a higher one, and gives that band back. Beside a generator of its own band it supplies only what the generator cannot carry and charges from the surplus. A band over its rating punctures the glass: the jar discharges at once as a shock to anything near it and is destroyed. It stores Eu. Optional addons: foil whose metal sets how hard it discharges, and a glass sleeve that slows the leak.
feedback.jei.info.overspeed_trip: A clutch with spinning weights inside that throws itself open if its shaft turns faster than its fitted spring allows (light 48, medium 120, heavy 300 RPM; sneak and right-click swaps the spring). Everything downstream coasts down on its own momentum, and it stays open until someone resets it. Place it inline on a shaft like any clutch.
feedback.jei.info.pressure_vessel: A sealed tank that a Powered Bellows pumps air into, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. The shape, the wall and the metal set how much pressure it holds and how much room is inside: a thicker wall holds more and leaves less, a sphere carries more than a cylinder, a flat box least. Up to its danger line it holds indefinitely; over that it may explode, and well over it certainly does. Read the gauge by using it. Optional addons: hoop bands raise the danger line; a relief valve vents air near it so a pump cannot burst the tank.
feedback.jei.info.pump: Moves fluid from its back to its front while its shaft turns: water, steam, molten metal or any other fluid. It moves 0.5 mB a tick for every RPM. Place it against the block it draws from, with its shaft across the flow. Built from an impeller part: its diameter and shape set flow, load and lift; an optional volute adds flow.
feedback.jei.info.steam_turbine: Turns hot steam into rotation at factory scale: about 64 Su at 240 RPM from 100 mB of steam a tick, which takes several boilers. Feed it steam from a Pipe or a touching Boiler; hotter steam gives more output, and its exhaust is steam a Condenser can recover. A shaft connects at either end of its axle.
feedback.jei.info.steam_engine: Turns steam into rotation. Place it touching a Boiler and it draws steam by itself, running at 16 RPM with 64 Su while it has steam. Its small store carries it over a stutter, and a shaft connects at either end of its axle.
feedback.jei.info.timer: A wind-up timer that switches the switchable blocks touching it on when started, and off when it runs out. Sneak-right-click to choose a 2, 5, 10 or 20 second wind, right-click to wind and start it, and right-click again to stop it early.
feedback.jei.info.water_wheel: Free, continuous rotation from flowing water. Built at a Woodworking Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table : a bigger wheel catches more water and turns slower for the same flow, more buckets take more of it, and a heavier rim has more momentum. It turns a few RPM for each side with moving water against it. Place it along the axis of its axle with flowing water on its sides. An optional rim ring of dense metal adds momentum.
feedback.jei.info.galvanic_cell: A zinc-copper battery giving a steady 1 A in the LV band. A close pair of metals gives LV, a wide pair MV, and a pack of cells in series raises the band a step, like a voltaic pile; the anode is eaten as it runs. Place it touching Copper Cable or a machine and it supplies power straight away, with no fuel, GUI or switch. One cell runs one Electromagnet at about three-quarters strength. Built from an anode part: its size and shape set the current and the life; an optional copper cathode adds current.
feedback.jei.info.sculk_relay: Made from a Relay Organ. Every relay within 24 blocks of another joins its run, with no wire between them and no line of sight needed, in the same dimension.
feedback.jei.info.data_sensor: Listens like a sculk sensor, within 8 blocks, and holds the last frequency it heard for two seconds. Link it to a Controller with a Data Connector and read it with a sensor card, for the frequency and for each channel's match.
feedback.jei.info.reboiler: The base of a Fractionating Column. Steam pumped into it lifts coke off the trays while it is under 420 Tu, and the heavy bottoms stay in it while only the light cuts leave.
feedback.jei.info.block_camera: A traffic camera on a steel pole, found standing in the world, most often beside a road, and never made. It watches for Bad Omen: a player carrying it who comes within sixteen blocks is turned to face, and a red light blinks for three seconds. If they still carry the omen after that, the camera reports them like a village would, their Bad Omen becomes a Raid Omen, and a raid comes to the camera. It reports once; afterwards its lens is dark. Broken, it gives up a battery, copper wire, a trace board and an optical glass lens, each only some of the time, whether it ever fired or not.
feedback.jei.info.camera_pole: One length of the steel pole a Block Camera stands on. Break one and everything standing on it comes down too, camera included.
feedback.jei.info.flare: A steel stack that burns off gas nobody wants. It is the safe vent for a line that makes more gas than you can use, since a burned gas stays out of the air.
feedback.jei.info.modular_blueprint: A design on paper, printed at the Blueprint Table. Some types, the crossbow among them, take one at a bench's blueprint slot to be made.
feedback.jei.info.magazine: Put a magazine in the crafting grid with loose cartridges of one bore to fill it, as many as it has room for. Swap it into a gun by reloading.
feedback.jade.radioactive: Gives off %s Ru at point blank
feedback.jade.shielded: Lead-lined: what it holds does not radiate
feedback.survey.none: Nothing within reach reads above the noise.
modular.feedback.desc.part.box_feed: A well under a bolt or lever action that takes a box magazine. Without it the action loads one round by hand.
message.feedback.transmission.no_design: A transmission with no design has nothing to shift.
feedback.gloss.cut: reads up to %1$s Qu, in steps of %2$s Qu
tooltip.feedback.role.substrate: The base a trace board is built on.
tooltip.feedback.role.solder: Pastes a trace board; heat the joint to set it.
tooltip.feedback.role.rectifier: A switching part: mount it on a trace board, or seat it in a cat's whisker detector.
tooltip.feedback.role.board: Mount a part, paste it with solder, then heat the joint: it becomes a circuit.
tooltip.feedback.role.circuit: Fit it on a cat's whisker detector's contact for a quieter, further-hearing report.
advancement.feedback.electronics.root.de: A circuit is a board with a switching part on it. First a base: grind a brick flat on a grinding wheel to get a substrate.
advancement.feedback.electronics.substra: Lay traces: a substrate and redstone dust in a crafting grid. Then put a coherer (no ore needed) on the board in the grid, and paste it with a tin ingot.
advancement.feedback.electronics.board.d: Heat a soldering iron at a fire. Hold the pasted board in the other hand, right-click, and drag the tip along the pads at a steady pace.
advancement.feedback.electronics.circuit: Fit it on a cat's whisker detector's contact and read it with a component tester.
feedback.circuit.lifted: Traces lifted: the circuit is dead
feedback.circuit.cooked: %s part(s) cooked: they sit on the board and switch nothing
feedback.circuit.lift.none: Nothing lifted: a part comes free only when both its pads are wet
feedback.circuit.lift.no_wick: A wick in your pack is needed to lift a part
feedback.circuit.heater: Carries a tube: it works at its best only once its heater has warmed it, and reads slow and noisy while cold.
feedback.circuit.holds: Its lattice holds what it remembers with no power
feedback.circuit.needs_supply: Its lattice needs a standing supply to remember
tooltip.feedback.circuit.has_resonator: Carries a resonator: a steadier clock and sampling, more channels and bandwidth.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.has_lattice: Carries a lattice: more variables, and it learns repeated readings. Needs power to remember.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.has_lattice_hol: Carries a lattice: more variables, and it learns repeated readings. It holds what it remembers unpowered.
tooltip.feedback.role.resonator: Solder it to a trace board as an element. A Controller or Computer takes a steadier clock and more channels from it; a Data Port a wider link.
tooltip.feedback.role.lattice: Solder it to a trace board as an element. A Controller or Computer takes more variables from it and filters repeated sensor readings.
feedback.jei.info.resonator: A crystal that rings between two electrodes, shaped at a part bench and laid together in a crafting grid. Amethyst rings; a bigger crystal is steadier and carries less, a narrower cut separates more channels and carries less. Solder it to a board as an element: a Controller or Computer with the circuit steps more evenly and reads steadier, an endernet upgrade gets as many channels as the circuit can separate, and a Data Port with the circuit seated in it carries more signals a minute.
feedback.jei.info.lattice: A living mesh in an insulating frame, shaped at a part bench and laid together in a crafting grid. The mesh must be a material that holds experience (sculk, echo shard). More cells and a finer mesh hold more extra variables for a Controller or Computer; a coarser mesh learns repeated sensor readings and holds them against noise. A lattice with a good frame and a mesh that leaks little keeps what it remembers when the host loses power; one that does not forgets the extra variables after a long dark.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.warm: Its tube is warm: it works at its best.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.warming: Its tube is warming: still slow and noisy.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.cold: Its tube is cold: slow and noisy until a heater warms it.
tooltip.feedback.circuit.gloss.warm: the bulb has come 95 per cent or more of the way to its working heat
tooltip.feedback.circuit.gloss.warming: between 40 and 95 per cent of the way to working heat: speed and noise still short of their best
tooltip.feedback.circuit.gloss.cold: under 40 per cent of the way to working heat: slow and noisy
tooltip.feedback.tube.unsealed: Open to the air. Seal it in a vacuum dryer before it goes on a board.
tooltip.feedback.role.tube: Solder it to a trace board as an element. Its heater must warm it before it works at its best.
feedback.better_combat_notice: Feedback is borrowing Better Combat's animations. If something looks wrong, report it to Feedback, never to Better Combat's author.
skill.feedback.move.wall_run.desc: Cast: with a wall beside you, run along it for most of a second; look steers, crouch drops you. Needs a wall at your side and a sprint. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.vault.desc: Cast: spring off the nearest thing in front and land behind it; it is staggered by your mass pushed off it. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.slide.desc: Cast: from a sprint, skid low along the ground; every body in the way is tripped once, staggered by your mass (armor counts). Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.smoke_step.desc: Cast: the roll kicks up a puff of the ground's own dust or snow. For two seconds anything inside loses you as a target and is blinded, unless at your elbow. Loose ground throws more than stone. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.thick_smoke.desc: Rider on Smoke step: a bigger cloud that lingers longer, most of all on loose ground.
skill.feedback.move.vanish.desc: Held cast: true invisibility while you keep still in low light. Moving, light or a blow you land ends it. Costs 5 stamina to start and a little each second.
skill.feedback.move.long_shadow.desc: Rider on Vanish: it also holds while you walk crouched.
skill.feedback.move.pocket_sand.desc: Cast: throw the ground at the eyes of a cone: loose sand blinds six seconds, dirt three, bare stone nothing. Targets lose you and flinch. Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.grit.desc: Rider on Pocket sand: blinds two seconds longer, and crushed stone underfoot works.
skill.feedback.move.challenge.desc: Cast: ring your weapon on your guard; every hostile within ten blocks turns on you. The weapon takes a point of wear. Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.advance.desc: Cast: for three seconds walk forward behind a held guard; everything in front is shoved back by your mass over its, and lighter ones are staggered. Needs a shield-type item. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.punish.desc: Cast: a heavy blow, over twice weapon damage, on the nearest thing in reach that is already staggered. Rearms on a stagger. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.rebuke.desc: Counter-strike reflex: a melee blow reaching you inside your parry window, one the parry did not catch, is answered at once with a short strike using your swing. Costs 15 stamina. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.rising_tempo.desc: Always on: with bare hands or a quick weapon (dagger tempo or faster), each blow within 1.5 s of the last is 15% harder than the one before, up to eight deep. A pause breaks the chain.
skill.feedback.move.frenzy.desc: Cast: with bare hands or a quick weapon, swing eighty percent faster for five seconds, then a third slower for three, winded. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.haymaker.desc: Cast: wind up half a second, then a punch for nine damage plus a worn plate's fist damage that shoves a body back by your mass over its. A miss staggers you. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.shoulder_charge.desc: Cast: a half-second sprint, shoulder first. A body well lighter than you flies and is staggered; one near your weight is staggered and stops you; a much heavier one stops you dead. Each body is hit once. Needs the ground. Rearms on time. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.pin.desc: Cast: kneel on the staggered or line-held body ahead. It cannot move and every blow lands harder; it struggles free after a time that grows with your mass over its (two seconds at equal weight). A much heavier body throws you off. Ends if you move, take a hard blow or recast. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.immovable.desc: Knockback does not move you: it costs stamina instead, more the lighter you are. With too little stamina you are moved as anyone is.
skill.feedback.move.stomp.desc: Cast: your whole weight on the nearest staggered thing in reach, as damage and a fresh stagger. Rearms on a stagger. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.crush.desc: Rider on Stomp: hurts half again as much.
skill.feedback.move.axe_kick.desc: Cast: an overhead heel on the nearest thing in front; a raised guard is broken and its bearer staggered by your mass. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.rending_heel.desc: Rider on Axe kick: also wears the target's armor, a heel's hardness against each piece's.
skill.feedback.move.bowling.desc: Throw upgrade: the thrown body flies as a ball for 25 ticks; everything it strikes is staggered by its mass (plus armor), and the body takes the knocks too.
skill.feedback.move.cleave.desc: Cast: bring a heavy weapon (damage 5 or more) down; the target takes the blow and a crack runs seven blocks on, staggering by weapon damage, fading with distance. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.dazzle.desc: Rider on Muzzle flash: blinds for six seconds, and the flash lights a mist of the pack's potion where the blast ends.
skill.feedback.move.concussive.desc: Rider on Muzzle flash: staggers half again as hard, and the blast drives a dose of the pack's potion into every body it staggers.
skill.feedback.move.scorch.desc: Rider on Kindle and Searing strike: targets burn twice as long.
skill.feedback.move.called_shot.desc: Cast: aim the round at where the creature under your crosshair will be on arrival. Needs line of sight, forty blocks at most. Costs a round, its heat and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.point_blank.desc: Cast: fire into a body you hold or one already staggered within reach; the round's whole impulse is stagger and, past ten Work, damage. Costs a round and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.snap_volley.desc: Cast: up to three rounds, four ticks apart, each at the next nearest living thing in the forward cone. The gun's cycle may refuse a follow-up. Each round spends ammo and adds heat. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.human_shield.desc: Cast: the body you hold takes every blow aimed at you while you hold it. If it dies, so does the cover. Needs a hold (Grab). Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.disarm_shot.desc: Cast: a round at the weapon hand of whoever you face within twenty blocks; what they held falls at their feet and they flinch by the round's impulse. Costs a round and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.field_dressing.desc: Held cast: stand still and hold the key to bind your wounds. Health returns while stamina drains 25 a second (a full bar buys about four hearts). Moving, damage, full health or an empty bar ends it. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.second_breath.desc: Cast: refill stamina to sixty and pause its regen, as a rest does. Heavy plate breathes to about forty. Costs no stamina; rearms on a landed blow.
skill.feedback.move.shake_off.desc: Cast: shake off fire, dirt in the eyes, anything sticky on the limbs, a daze, a stun. Poison, wither and the like stay. Refused with nothing to shake. Rearms on a stagger.
skill.feedback.move.wind_back.desc: A parry landed with stamina under 30 gives 15 back, without pausing regen. You must be low and still parry, and it rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.grit_teeth.desc: Always on: every blow you take lands lighter by a share read off worn armor (15% bare, up to 55% in full plate), for 10 stamina a blow. With less in the bar it lands whole.
skill.feedback.move.break_free.desc: Shake off first throws off any rope someone else has on you (a grab, a hooked weapon) and staggers the holder by their mass. Your own grapple is left alone.
skill.feedback.move.tend.desc: Held cast: stand still within two blocks of a hurt ally and hold the key to bind their wounds as fast as Field dressing, draining 25 stamina a second from you. Either moving, either taking damage, full health or an empty bar ends it. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.cut_loose.desc: Cast: free an ally within five blocks of every rope someone else has on them and break the grab, staggering the holder by their mass. Costs 20 stamina; rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.callused_hands.desc: Bare hands take the scald band: anything under 300 Tu can be held or touched unhurt. Burning and searing still hurt; gloves and tongs do better.
skill.feedback.move.sear_shut.desc: A practised hand at Cauterize: smaller burn, less heat lost from the piece, and the next one sooner.
skill.feedback.move.blood_up.desc: Three hits in a row, each within three seconds of the last, with no damage taken between, raise your stamina regain for eight seconds. Heals nothing. Taking a hit breaks the run. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.breather.desc: A kill with a modular weapon in your main hand gives back stamina by weapon mass: 10 a Mu, between 10 and 40.
skill.feedback.move.cauterize.desc: Cast: press a hot piece from either hand to the wound. A burning-hot piece heals three hearts, a searing one six; you take that band's burn and catch fire. The piece cools 200 Tu. Needs something at least burning hot.

gui.feedback.torque.title: Torque
gui.feedback.torque.hint: Hold the mouse to wind the driver. Let go inside the green band. Past it the thread strips.
gui.feedback.fitting.title: Fitting
gui.feedback.fitting.hint: Watch the bench work the part, then repeat the strokes: click the tools or press 1 to 4. A wrong stroke ends the fitting where you got to; the grade only sets how well the assembly starts.

gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.sc: A disk that shows what a scope sees, on a screen of its own. Somewhere a squirrel is being watched, and it knows.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.li: A disk that draws what is linked to what. It will not tell you why you wired it that way.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.no: A disk with a page on it. Handy for things you would otherwise forget, like where you put the disk.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.co: A disk that changes a figure from one unit into another. It has opinions about the imperial ones.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.ca: A disk that does the sums. Do not ask it about the meaning of life, it will say 42 and mean it.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.po: A disk that watches the lamp, and everything else that draws current. Nothing escapes a meter.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.ar: A disk with a game on it. The research is, regrettably, work.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.bl: A disk that holds drawings of what can be built. The drawings are better than the building, usually.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.app.ne: A disk that lets a Computer talk to others across distance. They mostly talk about the weather.
gui.feedback.research.title: Research
gui.feedback.research.shares_none: Nothing on the chain shares a trait with it yet.
gui.feedback.research.howto.1: 1. Pick a concept from the hand.
gui.feedback.research.howto.2: 2. Place it on a free hex beside one it shares a trait with.
gui.feedback.research.howto.3: 3. Link on until a hex beside the goal shares a trait with it.
gui.feedback.research.help: A link needs a shared trait. Wrong guesses cost ink.
gui.feedback.research.hand.tutorial.1: 1. Select one to five specimen cards from the hand. Record the order of selection; it is the order of testing.
gui.feedback.research.hand.tutorial.2: 2. Apply the row with Play. The cards that share a trait with another card of the row score. The most cards sharing one trait name the combo: pair, triple, quad or five. A card sharing nothing with its row is discarded and strains the specimen. A lone card is safe.
gui.feedback.research.hand.tutorial.3: 3. Each scoring card adds chips; the combo sets the multiplier. Cards carrying a trait of the goal, or of a treatise held beside, raise it. Reach the target score before the hands run out, then report the closing observation. Discard unwanted cards at no cost to the hand count.
gui.feedback.research.hand.tutorial.clos: End of protocol. Click to proceed.
gui.feedback.research.hand.goal: Reach %s. Cards with its traits add to the multiplier: %s
gui.feedback.research.hand.help: Click cards to lay a row, then Play. Cards that share a trait score.
gui.feedback.research.hand.burned: %s shares nothing with the row: it burns and counts as a bad play.
gui.feedback.research.hand.lost: The hands ran out before the target was reached.

gui.feedback.research.app.tutorial.title: > HELP
gui.feedback.research.app.tutorial.1: 1. CLICK A WORD TO TRY IT. TERMINAL REPLIES LIKENESS=N: LETTERS MATCHING THE ANSWER IN THE SAME PLACE.
gui.feedback.research.app.tutorial.2: 2. EACH WRONG WORD COSTS ONE TRY. ZERO TRIES: TERMINAL LOCKED.
gui.feedback.research.app.tutorial.3: 3. CLICK A BRACKET PAIR ON ONE ROW TO HACK. REMOVES A DUD WORD OR RESETS TRIES. ONE USE PER PAIR.
gui.feedback.research.app.help: Click a word to try it. Click a bracket pair to hack it. A word's likeness is how many letters sit where the answer's do.
gui.feedback.research.rite.tutorial.titl: Of the Purging of Murk, and the Weaving Thereof
gui.feedback.research.rite.tutorial.1: Hearken, seeker! The grid spread before thee lies clouded with murk, the raw and unwoven essence of the working. Take up a shard from the tray beneath the veil, drag it over the grid and loose it where thy heart bids; no shard may be turned, for the fates permit no turning.
gui.feedback.research.rite.tutorial.2: When a row or a column stands wholly filled, it shall blaze forth and be spent, and thine own shards within it fade to naught. Yet mark this well: murk is cleansed only where its opposite dwells in the selfsame line. Fire yearns for water, earth for air, light for dark. The anchors, steadfast stones of the working's own aspect, never fall, and count as filled.
gui.feedback.research.rite.tutorial.3: Should the shards betray thee, spend a measure of ink to draw the tray anew, or gather up the residue and close the rite in poverty. And when no murk remains, the grid is pure, and the next awaits thee.
gui.feedback.research.rite.help: Set pieces so a full row or column holds the element opposite a murk cell: it cleanses that murk. Any other full line only clears your pieces.
gui.feedback.research.found: The link holds. The notes are written up.
gui.feedback.research.lost: The ink ran out. The notes are a scrawl.

gui.feedback.engineering.tip.tool: Hand tool: a hammer, saw, file or screwdriver. Wears with use.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.fastener: Fixings: screws, machine bolts, rivets, welding rods, solder wire or glue (a slime ball is glue). Spent per assembly; better metal fits better. A weld holds best, solder less, glue least; a recipe may name the fixings it takes or refuses.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.blueprint: Blueprint: judges the fit and skips the hand work. Never required.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.blank: A blank treatise or blank paper: the specimen's volume is written onto it.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.binder: Treatise binder: its volumes count as known here.
feedback.jei.info.research_table: Where what is not yet known is found out. Put a Blank Treatise on the bench (you need the earlier treatise of its school in hand), pick a treatise volume or an attunement (for an attunement, an offering, a potion and a Blank Rite instead), and run the trials. It costs 40 experience points. On the board you link what you know to the new idea, a concept at a time: a concept that shares no trait with its neighbor fizzles and costs ink. Having done the real thing beforehand gives extra ink. A rite is not played on the board: it is a grid of murk to purify. Set pieces so a full row or column holds the element opposite a murk cell and that murk is cleansed; a better offering thins the murk and tidies the pieces, and a reagent potion leans the pieces toward the element that cleanses the thickest murk. Ink buys a fresh draw of pieces, and you can take the residue at any time for a lower grade. The notes are as good as the work was clean; a treatise carries them, and a rite is written with them: the better the notes, the higher the level it lets you attune.
gui.feedback.research_table.hint.reagent: Its potion works too, and gives more ink.
gui.feedback.research_table.note.9: Needs an offering that is good enough, or the potion it names
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.weapon: A book that holds that a sharp edge beats blunt force, with chapters on what it truly means to be sharp. Not to be confused with its rival, 'Blunt Force: A Rebuttal'.
A book that suggests that you can use a tiny explosion to shoot a piece of metal really stupid fast. The first page contains a trigger warning.
A book that suggests you can trade the explosive charge in a gun for energy itself. A robot to fire them for you, and you've got all you need for a SSShitstorm!
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.mechan: A book on the power of circles. You would think that this was already obvious.
A book on how to trade speed for torque, with a lot of nice examples. Geared to move any reader!
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.aerosp: A book on a structure you can rotate so fast it goes up! One might call this "revolutionary".
A book on burning a fuel to cause miniature explosions to send you flying. As easy as it is, it *is*, in fact, rocket science.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.roboti: A book on designing little machines small enough to wear in your clothes. It spends 200 pages talking about the size, and maybe 10 discussing real uses.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.chemic: A book on how to hold a lot of air in a comparatively small space. The book is full of words of encouragement, to avoid any pressure that comes with study.
A book on holding even more gas in an even smaller space. It contains over 5000 words, and it's not much larger than a pamphlet.
A book on how to make bombs. Do *not* cook with this, unless you take issue with hierarchical power structures.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.materi: A book on how to work a metal to draw out desirable properties. The front page warns that the instructions do not apply to the book itself.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.attune: A rite that gives a thing a pull on the animals around it. Importantly, this isn't like a "remove free will situation" so there's nothing gross about it.
A rite that scares off generally gross things. Sometimes that's zombies, sometimes that's salmonella; what matters is that they're yucky.
A rite to encourage natural processes into whatever carries it. A watched Mother Nature sometimes boils hotter, I guess.
A rite that lets a thing hold more energy than it should. The consequences of holding more than you can handle are left as an exercise for the reader.
A rite to make a thing stick to what it touches: a target, the ground, a crate, a meal. Which of you is clinging is a matter of perspective.
A rite that makes whatever carries it let electricity right on through. It's hard to *resist* an attunement this good.
A rite to give a thing a sense for conductive metal, wherever it's hiding. Take it to the beach if you feel inclined.
A rite that points toward the nearest dense block. Esoteric? Maybe. But surely there's a use to be found.
A rite to give a thing a sense for whatever could burn. Not a recommendation. Not *not* a recommendation.
A rite to give a thing a sense for the nearest magnetic block. May point north, but only when the nearest magnetic block is north.
A rite to repeat any act a moment later. A rite to repeat any act a moment later.
A rite that makes whatever happens happen just a little harder. Can't beat the classics.
A rite to light the night. What a ..shock?
A rite that lets a thing bank the damage it takes, and spend it later. There's a strategy prototyped in the text called the "Trauma Chipmunk".
A rite to put a little fire in any thing that holds still for it. Yeah, okay, you can use it on a sword, but can we get a little more creative?
A rite to stop a thing from letting go of what it holds. Whether or not that's a good thing is entirely your call.
A rite to fill your stomach. And to think, there's little kids who *wish* they had attunements like we do.
A rite to give a thing a push, and if it comes to it, perhaps even a shove.
A rite to give a thing a tug on the world's loose objects. It's not stealing if they come willingly.
A rite to broadcast a person. How would you like to doxx your enemies?
A rite to let you point your stored experience into repairing your gear. Because repairing your stuff was just *that* annoying, I guess...
A rite to let a thing build up speed and keep it. Once you start reading, it's difficult to put it down.
A rite to invoke the power of friendship. With this, you can do all things, provided you have twenty minutes of Saturday morning airtime.
A rite to squeeze every last drop of current out of an impact. The text remarks how some ancient civilizations sought to turn footsteps into electricity.
A rite that makes your thing follow boomerang rules. A great gift for the sentimental in you.
A rite to make a thing hold experience for later. It's a surprise tool that'll help us later.
A rite to make a thing announce itself with a vibration. The dinner bell in Hell.
A rite to wind a thing up. It will let go when it's ready, not when you are.
A rite to imbue your thing with water. You might expect this to break a machine. While that's wrong, it's not hard to understand how one might come to that conclusion.
A rite to play a game of chance. It might seem like an 18-carat run of bad luck, but truth is... the game was rigged from the start.
A rite to shrug off the wear of operation. This, too, shall pass.
A rite to make your item more generous. It'll take effort to not give your sword to your friend.

feedback.jei.info.engineering_table: Where parts are put together. Four tabs. Crafting: lay the parts in the 3x3 grid (positions do not matter), hand tools in the tool row (a hammer, saw, file or screwdriver; each craft wears the ones it needs a point, and a broken tool stays in its slot and blocks the craft until it is reworked) and fasteners in the fastener row (screws, machine bolts or rivets; the metal sets their quality, and better than the work asks gives a better start, worse still builds). A treatise binder in the corner counts its volumes as held. Most assemblies then ask for a hand-work game, torque or fitting, that scores the start only and never gates; a blueprint in the blueprint slot skips it. Fit: bolt several attachments onto a finished item at once. Repair: repair, swap a part or take an item apart. Treatise: copy a specimen onto a blank treatise. The part-making benches (Smithing Table, Anvil, Woodworking Table, Stonecutter) only make parts; the putting together is done here.
modular.feedback.desc.part.pry_head: A flat bar with a hooked, forked end for a pry bar. Its length is the lever: a longer bar lifts a heavier fixing but weighs more. It must be tough enough to carry what it lifts, or it bends.
feedback.jei.info.pry_head: The head of a pry bar. Right click a nailed, pinned or sealed block (rails, doors, trapdoors, ladders, signs, buttons, panes, bars) and it comes off whole, as the item it is. The bar must be tough enough for the block's hardness, and a longer bar is more lever; one that is not tough enough bends and lifts nothing. Wear follows the load it carried.
modular.feedback.desc.part.drill_tip: A fluted bit for a hand drill. A twist flute clears its chips and bites on; a spade flute takes less from each turn. It must be harder than the plate it drills, and its edge wears with the work.
feedback.jei.info.hand_drill: A hand tool that drills a plate. Hold the drill in one hand and a plate in the other, then hold use: each stroke turns the bit into the plate, so a harder plate takes more strokes, and a bit softer than the plate cuts nothing. Let go and the plate comes back as it is. The bit wears one point per stroke.
modular.feedback.desc.part.file_head: A toothed bar for a file. Its cut sets how much a stroke takes and how rough it leaves the part; its length sets the reach of a stroke. Its teeth wear with every stroke.
modular.feedback.desc.part.driver_bit: A hardened tip for a screwdriver. Its tip shape fits one kind of fastener and slips on another; a longer shank reaches the seat square but twists and wears.
feedback.jei.engineering.tool_strength: %s, wear %s, blow of %s St or more
feedback.jei.engineering.fastener_tip: Spends %s; quality %s or better builds clean, lower still builds but worse.
feedback.jei.engineering.circuit: The circuit is built in and kept
feedback.jei.engineering.blueprint: A blueprint in the blueprint slot skips the hand work.
feedback.jei.engineering.default_build: One default build; the core parts go in the grid, attachments on the Fit tab. Any fitting materials work.
feedback.jei.info.file: A hand tool for the Engineering Table's tool row (ability: file), and for filing a part down at a Part Bench. Its cut sets how much a stroke takes: a bastard cut two grains, a second cut one, a smooth cut half; a coarse stroke leaves tool marks that weaken the part until a smooth file polishes them off. A longer file takes more per stroke and wanders more. Each craft that calls for a file wears it; a broken one blocks the craft until it is reworked. In a crafting grid, a file and one rod are one stroke of filing: stroke by stroke the rod is cut into a screw, a bolt or a machine bolt, at about twice the work of the lathe or the grinding wheel, and only metal softer than the file's edge.
feedback.jei.info.screwdriver: A hand tool for the Engineering Table's tool row (ability: driver). Its tip shape moves the quality of the fasteners it drives: a cross tip suits screws, a hex tip suits machine bolts, a flat tip is middling on both. A long shank starts the fastener truer and wears the tool faster. Each craft that calls for a driver wears it; a broken one stays in its slot and blocks the craft until it is reworked. Fit a ratchet (a turned rod pawl on the handle) and the torque game needs no regrip and holds its band steadier, but a pawl of weak metal slips under a hard pull.
feedback.jei.info.fastener: A fastener for the Engineering Table's fastener row. Its quality is read from its material (1 to 5): above a recipe's floor the finished item starts better fitted, below it still builds but worse.
modular.feedback.desc.part.saw_blade: A toothed plate for a sawblade. Its edge wears with every cut.
gui.feedback.tool_table.tip.saw: A sawblade. Every act here costs it a point.
gui.feedback.tool_table.status.no_saw: Put a sawblade in the saw slot.
modular.feedback.role.container.tip: What the dish sits on, and what tells the table which dish it is: a bowl, a plate, a skewer or a baked flatbread. Its size caps how much meal there is and how long it takes to eat. Shaped at the Prep Table.
modular.feedback.role.base.tip: The bulk of the dish: a starchy food, such as a potato or bread.
modular.feedback.role.main.tip: The dense part: a protein, such as meat or fish. Every dish needs one.
modular.feedback.role.side.tip: Fiber and bulk: a plant food, such as a vegetable or fruit.
modular.feedback.role.finish.tip: A small, strong addition: a seasoning, such as honey. It moves the buff more than the hunger.
perk.feedback.settling.gloss: Eases nausea and food-poisoning sickness; strong cases are beyond it.
perk.feedback.warming.gloss: Stops the cold of powder snow from building up for a while; gives nothing against fire.
perk.feedback.cooling.gloss: Puts out burning sooner for a while; standing in lava still kills.
perk.feedback.antitoxin.gloss: Lowers the toxin in the same meal by a fraction; a deadly food stays deadly.
perk.feedback.antibiotic.gloss: Lowers the live pathogen in the same meal; rotten food is past help.
perk.feedback.antivenin.gloss: Eases poison I; stronger poison and wither are beyond it.
perk.feedback.sobering.gloss: Eases darkness, blindness and slowness up to level I.
perk.feedback.night_sight.gloss: Brief night vision, and blindness cannot land while it lasts; leaves you briefly slowed.
perk.feedback.fortifying.gloss: Lengthens the other effects of the same meal, up to double.
perk.feedback.slow_release.gloss: Stretches the meal's effects but holds them back longer.
perk.feedback.quickening.gloss: The meal's effects arrive sooner and end sooner, and a crash may follow.
perk.feedback.bracing.gloss: A small absorbing shield for a while, about one hit worth.
perk.feedback.mending.gloss: Heals you faster for a while, but only while you are fed.
perk.feedback.steadying.gloss: Blows push you less for a while; explosions still do. Slows you while it lasts.
perk.feedback.lightfoot.gloss: Brief speed and quicker stamina refill, at the price of hunger.
perk.feedback.bitter_tonic.gloss: Eases weakness and mining fatigue up to level I, then leaves a short slowness.
perk.feedback.brine_tolerance.gloss: Salt in the same dish protects it from spoiling longer; toxin is not helped.
perk.feedback.sleep_ward.gloss: Sets back the time since you last rested, so phantoms hold off; leaves you drowsy.
perk.feedback.breathing.gloss: Your air lasts longer underwater for a while; it is the air bar only.
perk.feedback.digestive.gloss: Fat and fiber hold the meal's effects back less, so they come sooner.
perk.feedback.hearth.gloss: A warm meal with this keeps you regenerating for longer; cold meals get nothing.
perk.feedback.keen_edge.gloss: Your blows land harder for a short while, but you are hurt more too.

modular.feedback.role.enrichment.tip: Worked into the dough to make it rich: an egg, sugar or honey. Optional, and a second one makes it richer still.
modular.feedback.desc.part.dough: Dough laid in a shape before it is baked. A kneaded dough keeps its knead through the shaping.

modular.feedback.desc.variant.roll: Like a loaf, but pinched small: a bread roll.

advancement.feedback.combat.rage_against: Some of those that work forces...
modular.feedback.role.top.tip: A second pastry laid over the filling, a lid or lattice. Optional.
