message.feedback.lace_refused: The potion will not mix in.
feedback.stockpot.lace_refused: The potion will not mix in.
message.feedback.rub_generator.no_rod: No rod seated: seat a rod of amber or another good insulator to rub.
message.feedback.rub_generator.full: The rod holds all the charge it can.
feedback.jei.info.rub_generator: Friction electricity by hand. Seat a rod of an insulator, amber is the classic one, by right-clicking with it (sneak with an empty hand to take it out), then rub it with an empty hand: each rub leaves charge on the rod, more for a better insulator, because only an insulator holds it. The charge leaks away slowly on its own and is drawn off into a low-voltage line as a small burst. Wire it to a Leyden jar and the rubs add up.
message.feedback.thermal_valve.fitted: Spring fitted: the valve opens when the fluid reaches the spring's temperature.
message.feedback.thermal_valve.no_memory: Spring fitted, but its metal remembers no shape: the valve stays shut.
message.feedback.thermal_valve.no_spring: No spring fitted: the valve stays shut. Right click with a coil spring.
feedback.jei.info.thermal_valve: A valve a spring works, with no power and no hand on it. Fit a coil spring: if its metal remembers a shape (void metal does), the valve opens when the fluid behind its input face reaches the temperature the spring returns to that shape at, and shuts again a little under it. A spring of a metal with no such memory, or none, leaves it shut. Right click with an empty hand takes the spring out.
feedback.jei.info.essentia_adapter: A one-way fitting from a Thaumaturge essentia store to a gas. Beside a store it draws a little essentia of the aspects it has a gas for each second (aer gives air, aqua steam, ignis hot air, forty mB for each unit) into its own tank, and leaves every other aspect where it is. Nothing goes back. A full tank spills what it cannot hold into the chunk as flux. Without Thaumaturge it does nothing.
message.feedback.essentia_vent.nothing: It touches no essentia store: it has nothing to read.
message.feedback.essentia_vent.open: Open: bleeding essentia off into the chunk as flux until the store is down.
message.feedback.essentia_vent.closed: Closed: the store beside it is below its limit.
feedback.jei.info.essentia_vent: A relief valve with its own gauge for Thaumaturge's essentia stores. Set it against a reservoir or jar. When the store is nearly full it opens and bleeds essentia out of it, and stays open until the store is well down before it reseats. Nothing it bleeds is lost: it goes into the chunk as flux, so give the flux somewhere to go, a scrubbing bed in the same chunk, or the world pays for the relief. Without that mod it does nothing.
message.feedback.taint_glaze.already: That block already wears a glaze.
feedback.jei.info.taint_glaze: A pot of glaze to brush onto one placed block (right-click it). A glazed machine does not corrode in a chunk flooded with Thaumaturge's flux, which otherwise rusts bare metal machines slowly. One block a use; a block that is replaced loses its glaze. Pick what is worth the glaze: a scrubbing bed that brings the flux down protects everything at once.
message.feedback.scrubbing_bed.empty: No bed packed in: nothing is taken out of the air.
message.feedback.scrubbing_bed.ruined: The bed has been burnt out and takes nothing.
message.feedback.scrubbing_bed.saturated: Saturated: it takes nothing and is letting some back out.
message.feedback.scrubbing_bed.fresh: Taking flux: less than half full.
feedback.jei.info.scrubbing_bed: A packed bed that takes Thaumaturge's flux out of the chunk it stands in. Pack it by right-clicking with charcoal or a molecular sieve, anything made of a material that works as a catalyst bed (sneak with an empty hand to take it out); the better the material works as a catalyst, the faster it takes flux and the more it holds. A full bed takes nothing and lets some back out. Set a fire directly beneath it, hot enough for the material to regenerate, and the load burns off; hold it in a fire hot enough to sinter and it is ruined for good.
message.feedback.laser.no_crystal: No crystal seated: nothing to lase.
message.feedback.laser.idle: Powered and ranging: the beam is only measuring.
message.feedback.laser.firing_hot: Firing, and the crystal is running hot: let it cool or it will crack.
message.feedback.laser.cooling: Not firing: the crystal is still cooling.
feedback.jei.info.laser: A pumped-crystal laser. Seat a crystal that lases (ruby, or any material with the phosphor figure) by right-clicking it; sneak with an empty hand takes it out. Powered on an MV line with a crystal it only ranges: a weak beam reads the distance to the first solid thing, which a linked Controller reads as a channel along with the crystal's heat and the cut's progress. Engaged by a Controller's Switch card or a redstone signal it fires: the beam doses the block it hits by the crystal's clarity and cuts it when the dose reaches the block's hardness, so soft stone goes in seconds and obsidian takes minutes. Anything living in the beam burns. The crystal turns what it does not emit into heat, more the less clear it is, and sheds it only while the beam is off: fire it too long and it cracks, so a hard cut is made in pulses. A band over MV cracks it at once.
feedback.jade.optical.link.2: Fiber: past its clean reach, reads to two figures
feedback.jade.optical.link.3: Fiber: far past its clean reach, reads to one figure
feedback.jade.optical.link.4: Fiber: dark (an end is dark, or the run is too long)
message.feedback.optical_terminal.no_cry: No crystal seated: this terminal gives no light.
message.feedback.optical_terminal.lit: Lit: powered, with a crystal seated.
message.feedback.optical_terminal.dark: Dark: a crystal is seated but the line gives it no power.
feedback.jei.info.optical_terminal: One end of a fiber link. Seat a crystal (any with a rectifying figure: quartz, cuprite, galena, pyrite) by right-clicking it, and a circuit the same way; sneak with an empty hand takes the circuit out, then the crystal. The crystal is the light source and the detector, and the better it rectifies the more loss the line may carry. A circuit with gain lengthens the clean reach. It draws a little current on an LV line while a crystal is seated; without power or a crystal the fiber it ends is dark, and a higher band than LV burns the crystal out. Link a sensor or machine to it with ordinary wire, then join two terminals with the Data Connector: the connector spends fiber, one piece a block, taking the poorest fiber that still reaches cleanly. Fiber is drawn from glass rods at the Wire Drawer, and its glass sets its loss: soda glass about 20 blocks, silica glass over 500. Past its clean reach a reading rounds to two figures, then one, and at eight times the reach it is lost.
feedback.jei.info.membrane_sensor: A phantom membrane film in a block. It answers to the volatiles a tired creature gives off, the same ones that draw phantoms to a sleepless player. Link it to a Controller with the Data Connector: channel 0 reads how sleepless the most tired player within about eight blocks is, rising to 1 at the sleeplessness that calls phantoms (an hour without sleep); channel 1 reads whether anyone is in reach. It also answers to the volatiles of a loose toxic gas: channel 2 reads the strongest cloud in reach (1 at the strongest a material gives off), channel 3 its kind (0.5 a gas that hangs in the air, 1 a heavy gas that has settled to the floor, 0 none). A creature that does not sleep gives it nothing. It needs no power, and measures only.
feedback.jei.info.aura_sensor: A pickup coil in a block. It reads the aura of the chunk it stands in, and gives a controller that reading: channel 0 is the vis against the chunk's base aura, channel 1 is how full of flux the chunk is, and channels 2 to 15 switch on as the flux climbs. It needs the Thaumaturge mod; without it every channel reads nothing. It only measures: what a controller does with the reading, such as scrubbing flux before it overruns, is the controller's business.
feedback.jei.info.radiation_sensor: A Geiger tube in a block. It reads the dose rate where it stands, from what radioactive material is around it, and gives a controller that reading: channel 0 is the rate against its full scale, and channels 1 to 15 switch on as the rate climbs past each fifteenth. Link it to a Controller with a Data Connector. Walls between it and the source cut what it sees.
feedback.culture.organ.2: An organ is ready to cut
feedback.rig.pendulum_broke: Impact pendulum: the specimen broke at an edge toughness of %s
feedback.rig.post: Strike post: %s J a blow, %s damage
feedback.jei.info.impact_pendulum: Right-click it with a tool or armor piece you made and the pendulum swings into the edge and reports its toughness, to the nearest 5. A twin-headed tool reports both heads. It leaves the piece unmarked. Sneak as you do it and the bob breaks the piece instead: the specimen is spent, and the reading is five times finer.
feedback.jei.info.strike_post: Swing at it with a tool you made and it reports what the blow carries in Work and the damage it deals, to the nearest half. It leaves the tool unmarked.
feedback.jei.info.sheathed_billet: Calcined redstone-chromium powder packed in a silver sheath. Draw it down in three stages (roll to a rod, draw to a wire, draw to a fine wire), annealing after every stage: a cold stage strains the metal, one with no anneal behind it will not move. Each anneal taken at the limit adds a cycle of texture; one taken early adds nothing. Then a reaction anneal at about 880 Tu in oxygen at 3.8 to 4.6 Pu makes superconducting wire: three cycles for the best, two or one for a weaker, none for nothing.
feedback.grapple.tension.exact: Line load %1$s%% of its rating, strain %2$s%%
feedback.jei.info.sheave: A pulley wheel you set in the air. A grapple line that runs through it turns on it and goes on from there, and it does not saw the line the way a block's edge does. Hang a line from a ceiling beam or a post and swing round it.
feedback.jei.info.piton: A steel spike with an eye, driven into the face of a block. Use a grapple on one piton, then on a second, to tie a fixed line between them, paid out of the grapple's line (a point of wear for every few blocks, in the line's material). Anyone off the ground who comes near the line takes hold of it: forward and back climb along it, sneak to drop off. The line is rated like a grapple's by its material and parts under too much load; a piton holds only as well as the block it is driven into, and works loose from soft ground. Sneak and use the grapple on a piton to cut its line.
feedback.jei.info.winch: A drum on a shaft, in a frame. Tie a fixed line to it with a grapple, as to a piton, and the other end to a piton or another winch. Turn it and it draws in whoever hangs on the line, at the drum's radius times its speed; turn it the other way and it pays them out. What hangs on the line is a load on the shaft, so a weak drive stalls under a heavy one and the line takes the weight. A drive that cannot carry the load strains the line hard. The winch is bolted fast and holds any load; the line is rated by its material, and a winch that goes takes its line with it.
feedback.grapple.tie.first: First piton marked: use the grapple on a second to tie the line
modular.feedback.desc.part.objective_len: The big lens at the far end of a telescope. A longer focal length with a short eyepiece magnifies more; a wider aperture gathers more light but blurs more unless the glass bends light strongly.
modular.feedback.desc.part.eyepiece_lens: The small lens you look through. A shorter focal length magnifies more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.telescope_tub: The tube that holds the two lenses where they focus. It wants to be as long as the two focal lengths together; any other length blurs the view.
modular.feedback.fig.magnification.tip: How many times larger a distant thing looks: the objective's focal length over the eyepiece's.
modular.feedback.fig.telescope_blur.tip: How soft the view is. A tube that is not as long as the two focal lengths, and a wide lens of glass that bends light weakly, both blur it.
modular.feedback.fig.tube_expansion.tip: How much longer the tube gets for each Tu it warms. Focus is set at the Overworld's ambient; a tube that is warmer or colder is the wrong length for its lenses and blurs, a steel one in the Nether or the Gap, an invar one hardly at all.
feedback.jei.info.telescope: A telescope is three parts shaped at a part bench and put together in a crafting grid: an objective lens, an eyepiece lens and a tube. The lenses must be of a material that bends light (glass, quartz, amber, a gem). Hold use to look through it: the view narrows by the magnification (objective focal length over eyepiece focal length) and softens by the blur (a tube not as long as the two focal lengths, and a weak, wide objective). On a clear night with open sky, a sharp telescope held on one of the planets that wander among the stars shows it as a disc; the farther and smaller the planet, the more magnification it takes.
modular.feedback.axis.focal.tip: How far from the lens the light comes to a point. A long objective with a short eyepiece magnifies most; the tube wants to be as long as the two focal lengths together.
modular.feedback.axis.lens_diameter.tip: How wide the lens is. A wider lens gathers more light but needs glass that bends light strongly, or it blurs.
modular.feedback.role.objective_lens.tip: The big lens at the far end. Its focal length, over the eyepiece's, is the magnification.
modular.feedback.role.eyepiece_lens.tip: The small lens you look through. A short focal length magnifies more.
modular.feedback.role.body_tube.tip: The tube that holds the lenses where they focus: as long as the two focal lengths together, or the view blurs.
feedback.jei.info.respirator: A mask worn in the Face slot, built from a face piece, a strap and one supply. With a filter cartridge it concentrates what oxygen thin air still has, down to a floor a deeper bed reaches, and cuts fume poison to a fifth; the filter wears with use. With an air cylinder it breathes its own air anywhere, and the Compressor fills it.
feedback.jei.info.shock_capsule: A steel capsule packed with graphite, set off by a blast. A blast of the right size (a creeper, TNT, a respawn anchor) squeezes the carbon into 4 Diamond Grit. Too weak a blast leaves it whole. Too strong a one (a charged creeper, an end crystal) vaporises the carbon and it comes back as graphite.
feedback.jei.info.diamond_seed: A chip of diamond for a crystal to grow on. Cut two from a Diamond, or press eight Diamond Grit into one. In a hot Reactor it grows into a Diamond two ways: with graphite on an iron, nickel or cobalt bed, held just under the vessel's burst pressure with argon; or with a thin methane and hydrogen mix at about 880 Tu, which grows two. Too hot and either turns to graphite.
feedback.jei.info.spent_blaze_rod: A blaze rod that has given up its heat. It grinds to dust with nothing left to burn. Heat it again in a hot vessel and it is a charged rod.
feedback.jei.info.inert_blaze_dust: What a spent blaze rod grinds to. It does not burn.
message.feedback.fuel_channel.rod: Rod burnt %1$s%%, condition %2$s%%. Sneak with an empty hand to take it out.
message.feedback.fuel_channel.empty: Empty channel. Put a fuel rod in.
message.feedback.control_assembly: Rods at %1$s of %2$s, set to %3$s. Click to step the target; absorber in hand loads it.
feedback.jade.fission.assembly: Rods at %1$s, set to %2$s, absorber strength %3$s%%
feedback.jei.info.reactor_core: The heart of a fission reactor. It sits at the top center of a shell seven blocks wide and seven tall: the six faces of the shell are walls of any dense material (lead, steel), the edges can stay open, and the five by five by five space under the core is the lattice. Put Fuel Channels, Control Rod Assemblies and Graphite Moderators in the lattice. The core makes heat only: put a Heat Exchanger beside it in the lid, with a Boiler on its far side, and the steam goes to a turbine. It cannot be switched off at once: decay heat keeps coming after the rods go in.
feedback.jei.info.fuel_channel: A lattice cell that holds one Fuel Rod. A rod beside a moderator or another rod runs hotter, a rod beside a control assembly cooler. Sneak with an empty hand to take the rod out.
feedback.jei.info.control_assembly: A bundle of absorber (cobalt, tungsten or lead) that sits at one of five positions, out to in. Click it to step its target, or wire it to a Controller switch. The core drops every assembly all the way in on a SCRAM.
feedback.jei.info.scram_trip: A passive safety. Built into the shell, it drops every control rod by itself once the core passes its trip temperature, with no power and no signal.
feedback.jei.info.graphite_moderator: Slows neutrons so the fuel beside it runs hotter. Read from graphite's own moderation figure, not its name.
feedback.jei.info.fuel_rod: Natural uranium clad in stainless steel. It burns for about two hours at full power, then becomes a Spent Rod.
feedback.jei.info.thorium_fuel_rod: Thorium and a little uranium. The thorium slowly breeds fissile material while it runs, so the rod lasts longer than a plain uranium rod.
feedback.jei.info.spent_fuel_rod: A burnt-out rod. Very radioactive: store it in a lead-lined chest.
feedback.jei.info.core_slag: What a breached core leaves behind. It stays radioactive for a long time and drops nothing.
message.feedback.magma_head.cold: Too cold to flow: fire %1$s Tu, bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.idle: Hot enough (fire %1$s Tu), but the shaft is still. Bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.flowing: Magma melt flowing, fire %1$s Tu, bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.blocked: Fire %1$s Tu, but nothing takes the melt. Bit %2$s%%.
feedback.jei.info.arc_hearth: A deep lined hearth: six charge slots and a 36-ingot tank, a crucible four times over. It has no fire of its own. Set an Arc Head on top of it and run an EHV line to the head; the plasma reaches about 3,500 Tu, enough to melt tungsten. Left running it boils volatile metals out of the bath, burns carbon out of steel, wears the electrodes and flashes. It also takes nitrogen or argon through its fluid face and holds it under the arc head: a sintering batch (the Heavy Core) spends that gas, and without it the batch is ruined.
feedback.jei.info.induction_coil: A coil around a crucible: a changing field heats the metal inside directly, with no flame and no smoke, up to about 1,800 Tu. It faces the way it was placed and needs a crucible holding metal (an ingot, scrap or a molten bath) in front of it; an empty crucible gets nothing. It draws 8 A at MV while there is metal to heat and follows its power with some inertia.
feedback.jei.info.induction_stove: A hob for cookware: it heats a pan or pot set on top when the cookware is made of a magnetic material (iron and steel yes, copper and aluminum no), up to about 600 Tu, with no fire and no smoke. It draws 4 A at MV only while magnetic cookware sits on it.
feedback.jei.info.preheat_coil: Right click with a piece to lay it in the coil, empty-handed to take it back. An empty hand on the empty coil, or sneaking, steps its target temperature (off, or 600 to 1,800 Tu). While powered at MV (8 A) it brings a metal piece quickly to that target; it knows nothing of the piece's forging window, so matching the two is up to you. It holds the piece there while powered, and unpowered the piece cools in the coil as it would anywhere. Only metals heat.
feedback.jei.info.heavy_core: Dense as osmium, about three times iron, and hard to melt: it is pressed from osmium powder and sintered, never cast. It is the very block found in trial chambers, which the builders made the same way. Three green compacts sinter in the Arc Hearth at 1,800 to 2,150 Tu with nitrogen or argon held in its tank. In air the powder oxidizes to osmium tetroxide: the batch is lost and a cloud of toxic fume stays, which blinds, then burns the lungs of anyone who stays in it. Too hot and the grains coarsen, a weak porous sinter. A mace or maul head reads its density.
feedback.jei.info.fission_device: A plutonium core inside a conventional explosive shell. A redstone signal sets it off: a very large blast that follows the world's game rules, and the ground around it is left as radioactive slag. It exists only where the server allows it (the nuclearArms switch in the nuclear config, off by default); where it is off the device sits inert.
feedback.jei.info.fusion_chamber: A held plasma loop. Pipe hydrogen in; helium comes out of the same port. A heat source hotter than ignition set beside it (a Star Burner) lights it while its magnet field is powered from an EHV line; once lit it gives heat to the block it faces, with no waste but the helium. Lose the field with the plasma lit and the wall wears every tick until it bursts. It faces the block it was placed against.
feedback.jei.info.star_burner: A seat for a Nether Star. Set it against a crucible or another vessel and right click with a star: the vessel is heated by it for as long as the star lasts, hotter than an arc can hold, and the star cannot be turned off or dimmed, only taken out with a bare hand, which burns. The star decays very slowly and is spent in the end.
feedback.jei.info.interferometer: Counts light fringes to read a length a hundred times finer than calipers. Carry it and every length figure a part shows prints to the finer step; it reads nothing else. Hand-held, no battery.
feedback.jei.info.cleaning_rod: A steel rod with a rag at its tip. A round too weak to leave the muzzle lodges in the bore, and the next shot into a stopped barrel is a hazard: hold the rod in one hand and the gun in the other and use it to push the round out. The hand is busy for a few seconds.
feedback.jei.info.vis_coil: A coil of fine wire wound on a steel core that holds primal vis. Where Thaumaturge is installed a recharge pedestal fills it from the aura, as it does any rechargeable thing; the finer the conductor, the more it holds. Made with the thaumaturge mod only.
feedback.jei.info.wand_part: A wand part made of one of Feedback's materials, for Thaumaturge's wand assembly. A cap's cost follows how well its metal conducts, and the aspects it is cheaper for follow its density and melting point; a rod holds vis by how well it insulates and how dense it is.
feedback.jei.info.arc_head: Three electrodes lowered into whatever it is set against: a crucible or an Arc Hearth. Right click with an electrode to fit one, empty-handed to take one back. It draws 42 A at EHV with all three fitted and burns as hot as the supply and the weakest electrode allow. The head faces the block it was placed against.
feedback.jei.info.arc_electrode: A rod of a material that can carry the arc: graphite sublimes near 3,600 Tu, a conducting metal boils. The hotter and longer the bath, the faster it wears. A worn electrode snaps and drops into the bath.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.assembly: Records an assembly of %1$s from %2$s kinds of stock.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.blank: Blank. Hold it in your off hand while you make a cut at a Stonecutter to record that cut.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.cut: Records a cut to %1$s from %2$s stock in the %3$s form.
tooltip.feedback.cutter_head: Takes stock up to hardness %1$s, condition %2$s%%
feedback.jei.info.auto_engineer: Plays back one hand assembly a recipe data stick recorded at the Engineering Table (hold a blank stick in your off hand while you take the crafted output there), on EHV. Right click with a data stick to seat it, a hand tool (hammer, saw blade, file, screwdriver) for a tool slot, fasteners for its stock, anything else to fill the parts bay; empty-handed takes the output, then the stick; sneaking takes back tools, fasteners and parts. Hoppers fill the bay and the fastener stock and empty the output. Parts that match the stick are assembled at the floor quality, never better, and each assembly wears a point of the tools it needs and spends the fasteners; it waits when a tool is missing or broken. Parts the stick does not cover become something they could legally form (the same every time in a world), or scrap nuggets of their material with mass lost. Stock too hard, a full output, scrapping and an over-rated supply wear the machine; a correct assembly never does. A circuit seated in it (use one on it) makes it assemble faster by the circuit's speed, and its noise is how often it holds off improvising or scrapping parts the stick does not cover; with none it works as it always did. A tubed circuit draws a heater from the line and runs slow and noisy until warm. Seated, the machine can be read by a Sensor card: assembly progress, condition and output fill. An empty hand takes the circuit after the stick.
feedback.jei.info.power_cutter: Cuts what is fed to it, about twice a second, on EHV. Right click with a cutter head or a recipe data stick to seat it, empty-handed to take the stick back, sneaking to take the head. Hoppers and pipes feed it and empty it. It does nothing without a head or without something to cut. Stock the stick recorded is cut the way it says; anything else gets a cut the machine could make, the same every time in a world, and what it cannot cut at all is lost. Unrecorded stock can also jam the cutter (an empty hand clears it), dull the head, or come out as scrap of its material. Stock harder than the head, a full output and an over-rated supply wear the head; correct cutting never does. A circuit seated in it (use one on it) makes it play faster by the circuit's speed, and its noise cuts how often stock the stick does not cover jams, wears the blade or comes out as scrap, and sometimes holds the machine off guessing at all; with none it works as it always did. A tubed circuit draws a heater from the line and runs slow and noisy until warm. Seated, the cutter can be read by a Sensor card: cut progress, head condition and output fill. An empty hand takes the circuit after the stick.
feedback.jei.info.sawblade: A saw blade, shaped at a part bench and used two ways. At the Stonecutter it cuts planks, slabs and the like from logs and planks. In the world, hold use while looking at a log or a plank block: each stroke takes a share of the wood, and a blade softer than the wood cuts nothing. The log becomes planks and a plank block becomes slabs, and the kerf falls as shavings. A thinner blade cuts quicker and wastes less wood. The blade wears a point per stroke.
feedback.jei.info.saw_head: The cutting element of a Power Cutter for cold stock: stone, wood, ceramic, glass, crystal and bone. What it is made of sets the hardness it can take. A worn head cuts slower and never stops.
feedback.jei.info.waterjet_head: The cutting element of a Power Cutter that cuts cold: stone, wood, ceramic and crystal as a saw does, and any metal plate without the current a plasma head needs. It cuts only with grit in it: use a gem or its dust of a hard, abrasive stuff (garnet is the one made for it) on the cutter to load it, eight cuts to a piece. Each cut spends one and wears the nozzle by how abrasive the grit is.
feedback.jei.info.plasma_head: The cutting element of a Power Cutter for conducting metal plate only: a plasma arc needs something to conduct. What it is made of sets the hardness it can take. A worn head cuts slower and never stops.
feedback.jei.info.data_stick: Blank until it records. Hold it in your off hand while you make a cut at a Stonecutter, or an assembly at the Engineering Table, and it keeps that work and the kind of stock it was made on. Seat it in a Power Cutter or an Auto Engineer to repeat it on stock of the same class. It holds one recording; making another overwrites it.
message.feedback.pipe.empty: Empty run: %s pipes, holds up to %s mB.
message.feedback.pipe.contents: %1$s: %2$s of %3$s mB at %4$s Tu, %5$s Pu, %6$s pipes.
message.feedback.seep.dry: The seep is dry for now.
message.feedback.derrick.too_soft: Bit too soft for this rock at %1$s m (%2$s%%): it is wearing, not cutting.
message.feedback.wellhead.needs_lift: Pressure is below the column's weight: turn the lift. Coning %3$s%%.
feedback.jei.info.flight_sensor: Reads altitude, airspeed, pitch, roll, climb or air density of the vehicle it is built into, for an Input card. Sneak-use steps the reading. Use opens the Contraption Diagram: the vehicle drawn as a blueprint with an arrow for every force on it (gravity, drag, levitation, buoyancy, ballast, propulsion, wing lift), from where it acts. Forces are a one second mean, in Fu; the figures are as fine as the sensor can resolve. A Computer's Diagram app shows the same page for a sensor linked to the running program. It also reads the heading (degrees round from south) and the position east and south of the world's origin, to a coarse step: what a program steers by and remembers waypoints from.
feedback.flight_sensor.heading: heading
feedback.flight_sensor.reading.heading: heading %s deg from south
feedback.jei.info.bearing_sensor: Reads how far off the End the front of the craft points, and how far away it is, for an Input card. In the Gap only: anywhere else it reads nothing. Sneak-use steps the reading: the turn to the right (yaw), the tip up (pitch) or the distance. The gas giant in the sky is the End, and it grows as the craft closes on it; this sensor makes the heading exact. It is as fine as it can resolve, and a rough heading still arrives, later and with more correction burns.
feedback.bearing_sensor.reading.yaw: turn right %s deg to face the End
feedback.bearing_sensor.reading.pitch: tip up %s deg to face the End
modular.feedback.desc.part.tray_deck: The deck of a column tray. Bubble caps hold back the most vapor and flow least; a packed bed flows most and holds back least; a sieve is between. A finer hole holds back more and cokes faster; a larger open area (hole against pitch) takes more a tick.
modular.feedback.role.tray_deck.tip: The perforated plate the vapor bubbles through. Drill finer for sharper cuts that foul faster; drill coarser for flow.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tray_bubbl: Caps over risers: the sharpest cuts, the least flow.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tray_sieve: A drilled plate: a middling cut and flow.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tray_packe: A packed bed: the most flow, the loosest cut, slow to coke.
feedback.jei.info.creative_tool_table: Makes any part of any shape from any stock, with no tool, no treatise and no working heat; forged shapes come out at once and clean. Its one Cut tab lists the saw's wood cuts and the stonecutter's cuts together. Stock is still spent.
tooltip.feedback.anvil_forge: Also forges! A Hearth beside it keeps the stock hot.
gui.feedback.tool_table.tip.axe: An axe. Each stripping or sawing costs it a point.
gui.feedback.tool_table.status.no_axe: Put an axe or a sawblade in the tool slot.
gui.feedback.tool_table.status.need_axe: Stripping a log takes an axe.
gui.feedback.tool_table.status.need_saw: Sawing planks takes a sawblade, not an axe.
gui.feedback.tool_table.list.nothing: This bench cannot make anything of that.
screen.feedback.probe.put: Put an item in the slot.
screen.feedback.probe.none: No material file lists this item.
screen.feedback.probe.row.diamagnetism.t: How hard a magnet drives it off, against bismuth, the strongest metal at it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.form.tip: What shape of the material this item is.
screen.feedback.probe.row.kind.tip: What sort of stuff the material is.
screen.feedback.probe.row.perk.tip: Given free to a weapon part made of it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.hardness.tip: Smallest blow that works it; each blow does its strength divided by this in Wu.
screen.feedback.probe.row.work_min.tip: Colder than this it cannot be worked.
screen.feedback.probe.row.work_max.tip: Hotter than this it cannot be worked.
screen.feedback.probe.row.anneal.tip: Past this it forgets being worked.
screen.feedback.probe.row.service.tip: A machine body of it softens and wears above this.
screen.feedback.probe.row.burns.tip: Held in air above this it burns.
screen.feedback.probe.row.scales.tip: Held in air above this it scales.
screen.feedback.probe.row.cooling.tip: A loose piece loses this much every tick.
screen.feedback.probe.row.conductivity.t: Heat passed by a one-block wall of it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.flame.tip: Flame temperature and how long a piece burns.
screen.feedback.probe.row.freeze.tip: A bucket of the melt holds its melting point this long as it freezes.
screen.feedback.probe.row.toughness.tip: A single blow over this cracks it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.toughness_brit: Under its hardness: anything that could move it breaks it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.ductility.tip: Cold working steps before it cracks.
screen.feedback.probe.row.work_hardening: Each cold step makes it this much harder until annealed.
screen.feedback.probe.row.yield.tip: A part of it bends under this load.
screen.feedback.probe.row.friction.tip: How hard it is to slide on.
screen.feedback.probe.row.abrasiveness.t: Cutting it spends grit at this share of the worst rate.
screen.feedback.probe.row.quench.tip: Whether plunging it in water hardens it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.viscosity.tip: How thick the melt is, against water.
screen.feedback.probe.row.melt_density.t: Weight per liter of the melt.
screen.feedback.probe.row.curie.tip: Hotter than this a magnet no longer pulls it.
screen.feedback.probe.row.reflectivity.t: Share of the light on it that it throws back.
screen.feedback.probe.row.ampacity.tip: Current a wire of it carries before it melts, against copper.
screen.feedback.probe.row.drop.tip: Eu lost from each packet per block.

feedback.jade.icebox.hold.0: Nothing holding it cold; drifting to the room
feedback.jade.icebox.hold.2: Held cold by the Refrigeration Unit
feedback.jei.info.refrigeration_unit: Against an Ice Box it holds the box cold. Against the inside of a walled room it holds the whole room cold: every Ice Box and loose item inside settles at the room's temperature. Walls leak by their material, openings (a gap, an open door, open sky) leak far more, and the unit draws more current the more the room leaks. Put a Condenser against the unit as a compressor stage and it can freeze: food held below freezing does not rot, and eats cold. Right-click with an empty hand to show where the room leaks.
feedback.jei.info.food_form: A whole block or rod of the foodstuff. It is edible (a mouthful for each raw item it holds), and it cooks, dries, chars and spoils in a furnace, a crucible or any pot the way the plain meat does.
feedback.hydride.holds_gas: It still holds too much gas to take that out
feedback.jei.info.uranium_glass_block: A block of uranium glass. It is faintly radioactive itself and fluoresces in the radiation around it: dark with nothing near, a faint glow in a small dose, brighter as the dose climbs, never brighter than a torch. A heap of it glows a little by itself. Cast it from molten uranium glass in a block mold.
feedback.jei.brewing_ingredient.note: Stirred at the Brewing Stand, it drags the marker along a curve in this direction. Cutting it at the Prep Table lengthens the curve; a hotter pot lengthens it too.
feedback.jei.brewing_ingredient.heading: Heads %s
feedback.jei.shape.line.tip: Straight to its end. The cheapest to stir for its reach.
feedback.jei.shape.arc.tip: Bows to one side on the way, then comes back to its heading.
feedback.jei.shape.wave.tip: Swings to both sides of its heading as it goes.
feedback.jei.shape.zigzag.tip: Cuts back and forth in sharp turns. Long to stir for its reach.
feedback.jei.shape.loop.tip: Doubles back on itself in a loop before running on to its end.
feedback.jei.shape.spiral.tip: Winds outward in turns and ends well off its heading. The longest to stir.
feedback.jei.shape.hook.tip: Runs straight, then bends sharply to one side at the end.
feedback.jei.info.brewing_stand: Right-click to open the stand's screen. Put a water bucket in the water slot, ingredients in the six slots and set it over a fire. Stir by circling the mouse over the map to walk the flask along the path the ingredients drew; the Pour button ladles water over the brew and sends the flask a step back toward the center. The compass trim shows each class's direction, and hovering an ingredient draws a ghost of its line. Cook ends the brew where the flask is: inside a node's ring a potion, anywhere else a dud draught.
feedback.jei.info.vacuum_dryer: Use a potion bottle on it to load it. It sits over a fire with a vacuum pump on a shaft: the faster the shaft turns, the deeper the vacuum. The potion dries once the chamber is warm enough and deep enough for a while, and stalls when either lapses. Too hot scorches away strength, far too hot cracks the bottle. An empty hand takes the salts out. Use salts on a water source to turn them back into a bottle, a little weaker. It also evacuates and seals a built vacuum tube: use the tube on it and it comes out sealed once the chamber has been warm and thin for a while. The deeper the vacuum, the hotter the bake (short of what the glass takes) and the tighter the glass, the harder the seal; a shallow, cool seal leaves gas in, which turns a gridded tube into a thyratron, and glass taken past its service temperature slumps and holds none.
feedback.jei.info.vacuum_tube: An envelope, a cathode, a plate and any grids, shaped at a part bench and laid together in a crafting grid. It is full of air until a vacuum dryer evacuates and seals it. A sealed tube mounts on a trace board as a switching element and sets the circuit's gain, speed and noise. Its character is computed from what you built: no grid is a diode, one to three grids a triode, tetrode or pentode, and a gridded tube sealed with gas left in is a thyratron. The cathode metal sets emission against warm-up and heater power, the grid and plate metals set gain and speed, the glass sets how good a vacuum it holds and how hot it may be baked. A circuit with a tube reads slow and noisy while cold and works at its best once warm: a powered Electric Controller or Computer warms it with a heater it pays for, a fire warms it too.
feedback.jei.info.potion: Drink it for its effect, at the level and length it was brewed with; its potency fades with time, faster when warm. Sneak and use to throw it at a spot, where it splashes every creature nearby. Every potion can be drunk: fire sets the drinker alight and explosion bursts into heat on them.
feedback.jei.info.potion_use: Sneak and use with the bottle in one hand and a finished tool in the other to imbue it; its next few hits carry a short rider of the potion. Sneak and use a dish or serving with the bottle in the other hand, or pour it into a stockpot, to lace the food: the eater gets the effect without being told. A taste far from the food's own gives it away, and a nibble reports what it leans on.
feedback.jei.info.potion_salts: A bottle dried at the Vacuum Dryer. The salts never fade and keep the effect, level and strength they had when dried. Use them on a water source to reconstitute a bottle at a reduced strength.
feedback.jei.info.potion_salts_use: Salts cannot be imbued or poured into food; reconstitute them first.
feedback.jei.info.jar: Put one jar and one food, or one ladled serving, in the crafting grid in any arrangement to fill it. Then seal it in a Pressure Vessel over a hot fire.
feedback.jei.info.jarred_food: Made by filling a jar in the crafting grid. Heat above plain boiling, which only pressure reaches, seals it and kills what is live in it. Kept hot after sealing it goes mushy. Eating it returns the jar.
feedback.jei.info.salt: Left behind when a Stockpot of sea water boils dry beside the ocean or a beach, or dug from salt deposits crusted on the sand of ocean floors. Put one salt and one food in the crafting grid to salt the food: it keeps longer, is drier, and shrugs off more of what is live or toxic in it.
feedback.jei.info.dough: Three wheat and a water bucket. Knead it on the Prep Table, then bake it. Add an egg for pastry dough, or lay it out on the Prep Table for flatbread.

skill.feedback.move.running_start.desc: A straight sprint builds speed, up to a quarter faster after three seconds. A hard turn or a stop lets it go.
skill.feedback.move.fleet.desc: Cast: a burst of speed for two and a half seconds, trailing dust: sixty percent faster, but worn armor's speed cost cuts the gain down to a fifth. Costs 20 stamina; rearms on a landed blow.
skill.feedback.move.quick_draw.desc: Cast: the first gun in your hotbar comes up and fires on the same tick, and stays in hand. If it cannot fire, nothing is spent. Spread grows with gun weight against your mass, plus barrel heat. Costs 20 stamina; rearms on a landed blow.
skill.feedback.figure.fume_soften: Poison from a fume dose %s (fraction off)
feedback.fume_cloud.1: Your eyes sting and your head swims. Get out of the fumes.
feedback.fume_cloud.2: Your sight is going. Get out of the fumes.
feedback.fume_cloud.3: Your lungs burn. Get out of the fumes.

skill.feedback.figure.hand_ease: Food a stroke of hand work costs %s (fraction off)
feedback.thresher.unjammed: Jam cleared; the stuck piece comes out
feedback.jei.info.thresher: A drum on a shaft under a hopper. Put a grain plant in the hopper (wheat) and turn the shaft at 16 RPM or more: the drum beats the grain loose, and the seed, the straw and the chaff drop into three trays. An empty hand takes them out; a hopper can too. Turned faster than 64 RPM it throws the seed onto the ground instead. Anything soft that is not a grain is shredded to nothing; anything harder than the drum's teeth jams it and wears them, and an empty hand clears the jam and gets the stuck piece back. Worn teeth work slower, never stop. It is a 40 Su load.
tooltip.feedback.potion_salts: Dissolve in a water source to restore a bottle, weaker than it was
feedback.jei.kind.metalloid.tip: An element between metal and salt. Cast like a metal, but brittle and a poor conductor.
message.feedback.creeper.sac_empty: Too little in the sac to cut a charge.
message.feedback.creeper.wont_eat: The creeper will not eat that.

tooltip.feedback.tasting.title: You taste %s:
modular.feedback.desc.part.spoon_bowl: The bowl of a spoon. A bigger bowl stirs a stockpot harder and skims more off the top; a deep bowl lifts more and a shallow one pushes the pot about better; a ladle reaches further from a hot pot.
feedback.jei.info.spoon: Hold a dish in the other hand and use the spoon to taste it: it names how hearty, rich, moist, done, salty, smoky, fresh and warm the dish is, as a villager judges it (with a figure at the truth tier). A bowl smaller than the reference takes a small mouthful and tells only the two axes that stand furthest from the middle; a dish hotter than the handle can be held over burns the hand. Each tasting wears the spoon a point. Aim at a stockpot and hold use to stir; tap use to skim the scum off the top. Stirring keeps the bottom from scorching and mixes the pot, but stirring with scum on top folds it in for good, so skim first. A bigger bowl does more per stroke; a deep bowl skims more and stirs less, a shallow one the other way. A ladle skims more and stirs less than a spoon, and its long reach keeps the hand off a hotter pot. Every skim and a long stir wear the spoon, and stirring a pot hotter than the handle stands burns your hand.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spatula_blade: A broad flat blade for a spatula. Flips a piece in a skillet; held on the pan it lifts it off the fire.
feedback.jade.skillet.piece: Piece: %s Tu, cooked %s%%, moisture %s%%, char %s%% down, %s%% up
feedback.jade.stockpot.figures: Cooked %s%%, scum %s%%, mixed %s%%, water %s mB, solids %s mB
feedback.jei.info.skillet: A pan for cooking by hand, made from three plates of one metal over a stick; the metal sets how fast the pan follows the fire. Lay up to four pieces of food in it, one per quarter, and set it on a fire. Take a piece off with a bowl or plate to keep your hand safe. Grip it with tongs to lift it off the fire.
feedback.jei.info.spatula: Right-click a piece in a skillet to flip it. Only the face down chars, so turning evenly gives an even result. Each flip wears the spatula.

feedback.jei.info.commissions: Villagers wanting a finished tool, weapon or armor piece of a type and quality post commissions each day. Put the piece in the delivery slot and press Deliver: the villager grades it on its true figures against what they asked, pays emeralds by class, and a slip tells you the one thing furthest off. Some wants are never said. Many deliveries of the same kind of piece in the same sort of material pay less for a few days.
gui.feedback.villager.sell_hint: Put what you want to sell in the slot.
village.feedback.speech.not_wanted: I am not buying that today.
village.feedback.speech.full: I have enough of those for today.
feedback.jei.research.reagent: Its potion works too, and gives more ink.
gui.feedback.mortar.hint: Grinding bowl: drop a plant in, then grab the pestle. Pound it to smash, rub it side to side to grind. Drag a plant out when it is as fine as you want.
feedback.jei.info.mortar: The heart of the Brewing Stand's grinding bowl, and an ingredient of the stand itself. At the stand, drop plants into the bowl and work them with the pestle: a plant ground finer gives the water more surface, so its compound comes out faster. Hard things need smashing; soft herbs grind easily.
gui.feedback.recipe.title: Recipe
gui.feedback.recipe.name_hint: Name it, or let it be named

message.feedback.arc_welder.no_power: No charged battery in your pack.
message.feedback.arc_welder.no_filler: No %s ingot in your pack for filler.
feedback.jei.info.arc_welder: Needs a charged battery and a filler ingot of the part's own material in your pack. Hold a worn tool, weapon, armor piece, gun or machine head in the other hand and hold right click to weld it; or right-click a worn machine with the welder. A weld restores the part to its best remaining condition, but each weld lowers that best by a step, down to a floor: a welded part is never as good as new. The electrode wears a little with every weld and keeps working.
modular.feedback.desc.part.backpack_shel: The body of a pack, worn on the back. Leather, cloth or sheet metal; its shape sets the slots: one cell a pouch, three a satchel, nine a pack. Add a strap to carry it.
modular.feedback.role.shell.tip: The bag body. Its shape fixes how many slots it holds; its material only decides how heavy it is.
modular.feedback.role.strap.tip: Carries the load. On a backpack its strength sets how much the wearer can carry before being slowed, and it is the part that wears and lets go. On a shield it carries the weight of the face, so the face holds a little more of a blow.
modular.feedback.fig.carry.tip: Mass of the pack and its contents the strap carries before the wearer is slowed and cannot sprint. Set by the strap's strength; falls as it wears.
modular.feedback.fig.slots.tip: Item slots of the bag, fixed by the shell's shape.
modular.feedback.role.hard_liner.tip: Two plates sewn inside the shell. The shell wears half as fast under an overload. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.fire_patch.tip: A plate over the shell's back. A burning wearer's cloth shell scorches without it, and wears; with it, not. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.oiled_coat.tip: A hide soaked in oil and laid over the shell. A cloth shell without one soaks in water or rain and weighs half as much again. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.warm_liner.tip: Three carpets quilted inside against the back: chill from powder snow leaves the wearer faster. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.buckle.tip: A metal clasp on the chest strap. Its key drops the pack at once, contents and all. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.lamp_bracket.tip: A rod hook above the pack: one slot that takes only a lantern. A lantern in it lights the way around the wearer. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.sheet.tip: What you lie on. Softer cloth or hide gives more comfort.
modular.feedback.role.fill.tip: Fibrous stuffing between the sheet and the shell. The softer it is, the better the sleep.
modular.feedback.role.pack_frame.tip: Four rods lashed to the shell. Rigid stock takes load off the strap and gives the pack more mounting points; it never wears.
modular.feedback.role.holster.tip: Two hides cut into a sleeve strapped outside: one tool or weapon, drawn without opening the pack. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.bottle_loops.tip: A bundle of leather cut into loops: three small vessels (potions, flasks, fluid containers). Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.bandolier.tip: Two bundles of leather straps with loops: three slots for rounds and arrows. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.hip_belt.tip: Three hides cut into bands that move the load to the hips; needs a frame to hang from. Its strength adds to the carry rating; it wears with the strap. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.lashing.tip: Two sticks and a cord that tie a bedroll on top of the pack: one slot that takes only a bedroll. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.panel.tip: Two carpets against the back. The softer the cloth the more it raises the carry rating. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.pad.tip: Two boards that fold out into a bench: its key opens a 3x3 crafting grid while you stand on firm ground. Heavy, and takes two mounting points.
modular.feedback.fig.points.tip: Fittings take points from the shell (a pouch has the fewest, a pack the most); a frame gives more.
modular.feedback.fig.stores.tip: Typed slots the fittings add beside the fixed ones: holster, bottle loops, bedroll lashing, bandolier.
modular.feedback.fig.comfort.tip: How soft the padding and cover are, thicker and lifted off the ground. Half of it is the share of your health a night's sleep gives back (see Heals).
message.feedback.pack_pad_ground: The pad needs firm ground under your feet.
message.feedback.pack_strap_broke: The strap lets go and the pack falls away.
feedback.jei.info.backpack: Worn in the back slot; press the pack key to open it. The shell's shape fixes the slots (pouch 9, satchel 18, pack 27) and the strap's strength fixes how much the pack and its contents may weigh. Over that the wearer is slowed and cannot sprint, and the strap wears until it lets go and the pack falls off with everything in it. A pack cannot hold a pack. Rework the strap to mend it. Fittings are added at a Woodworking Table (a Smithing Table for plate fittings) by reworking a finished pack, and take mounting points from the shell (pouch 1, satchel 2, pack 4): a frame (four rods, gives 2 points, raises the rating), a hip belt (three hides, needs a frame, raises the rating), a padded panel (two carpets, softer is better), a side holster (two hides, one tool), bottle loops (a leather bundle, three vessels), a bandolier (two leather bundles, three slots for rounds and arrows), a bedroll lashing (two sticks, one bedroll; its key beds you down without taking the roll out), a crafting pad (two boards, two points, its own key opens a 3x3 grid on firm ground), a hard liner (two plates, the shell wears half as fast overloaded), a fire patch (a plate, keeps a burning wearer's cloth shell from scorching), an oiled coat (a hide, keeps a cloth shell from soaking), a warm liner (three carpets, thaws powder-snow chill), a quick-release buckle (a metal nugget; its key drops the pack at once), a battery fitting (two plates, one slot that takes only a battery, which a tethered pulse gun draws from) and a lamp bracket (a rod, one lantern slot that lights the wearer). Take a pack apart to remove a fitting.
tooltip.feedback.endernet_upgrade.bonded: Bonded under a pair id. Use it on an Electric Controller or Computer to make it one end of a data pair.
message.feedback.data_port: Teleportant %1$s mB. Chunk %2$s. Pair %3$s. Click to retune: %4$s
message.feedback.data_port.away: far end not loaded or not powered
feedback.jei.info.data_port: One end of an entangled data pair, made with a pearl, two plates and a length of fine wire: it gives two ports bonded under one pair id, the way ender ports are. Link a sensor, machine or computer to a port with the Data Connector and it can be read from the far port (or from an Electric Controller or Computer fitted with the bonded endernet upgrade) as if it were wired to it. Each end draws standing power and the pair carries only while both ends are powered and loaded; an unloaded end pauses it, and an ender anchor used on a port keeps its chunk loaded. Each signal across costs a little teleportant, poured into the port's tank, and uses up a share of its bandwidth; a dry or saturated port is dark until it recovers. One end of every pair must be a port. Both ends must be in one dimension. An empty hand reads the tank and the pair; the Tuned Eye finds the far end. A circuit seated in it (use one on it, sneak with an empty hand takes it out) widens its bandwidth by the circuit's resonator. With a robot's endernet upgrade bonded to it, the port is that robot's base station: Sensor and Actuator cards linked to it read and hold the robot's senses and actions. Click it to step its bus channel (off, then 1 up to what a resonator on the circuit in it separates): ports tuned to one channel share its bandwidth, a program writes four signal slots with an Actuator card and any port on the channel hears them with a Sensor card, and anyone tuned to it can listen.
feedback.jei.info.endernet_upgrade: An antenna bonded under a pair id, made from a bonded Data Port and a metal plate (the port's partner stays a port). Use it on an Electric Controller or Computer to make that block one end of the pair: it then reads what is linked to the far port as though linked to itself, and draws standing power. One per block; a Crowbar takes it off. A Computer with it can list and switch the far side in the Network app. The channels it offers follow the resonator of the circuit in its host. Used in the air by the wearer of a suit, it bonds the suit: each scan pulse is then posted under the pair, and the Data Port at the other end offers the last scan (creatures, hostile, nearest, reach) as channels, paying teleportant and bandwidth for each signal read, in the same dimension only. On a Computer with the Network disk it is also tuned: a channel (1 with no circuit, more for a resonator) and an address, so the Computer can send short messages and programs to other addressed Computers on its channel, each paid for by the pair and by the channel's shared bandwidth; anyone on the channel overhears messages.
message.feedback.tube.run: Tube run of %1$s blocks: %2$s of %3$s mB air, %4$s Pu
message.feedback.station: Address %1$s. Capsules %2$s, pods %3$s. Sort: %4$s. In bands: %5$s. Rejects: %6$s
feedback.jei.info.tube: A sealed pneumatic tube. A run of tubes shares one air ledger, and air pressure moves the capsules in it: a Compressor or the Creative Air Source pressurises the run, each hop spends a little air, and under a third of a Pu a capsule sits still until pressure returns. A heavy load slows a capsule, a bend slows it more, and a capsule too heavy for the bore stalls. Right-click to read the run's pressure. Over 5 Pu the run can burst.
feedback.jei.info.lined_tube: A tube with a smooth liner: less wall friction, so capsules move half as fast again at the same pressure.
feedback.jei.info.wide_tube: A wide-bore tube. Passes pods and far heavier capsules than the narrow tube. It joins narrow tubes freely, but a pod cannot enter a narrow one.
feedback.jei.info.evacuated_tube: A wide-bore tube sealed for vacuum. While its run is pumped down by a Vacuum Pump (under 0.05 Pu) capsules coast through at three times the plain speed with no air spent. Seals leak, so the pump must keep running; with the vacuum lost the tube behaves like a lined wide tube.
feedback.jei.info.tube_junction: Routes capsules by address, never by contents. Use a dye on a face to name the color that leaves that way (the same dye again clears it); sneak with an empty hand to clear all. A capsule with no matching color leaves by the first open face.
feedback.jei.info.programmed_junction: A junction that returns what it cannot place. Dye a face to name its color; click a face with an empty hand to make it the return line. A capsule with no matching color goes to the return line, and waits while that line is full rather than going astray.
feedback.jei.info.tube_station: The door of a tube run. Items fed in (by hopper or belt) are packed into a stocked capsule when the buffer is full or has stood idle, stamped with the station's address color, and sent into the tube it faces. Arriving capsules are emptied into an output buffer that pushes into neighboring inventories. Dye sets the address; sneak with an empty hand clears it. Use a capsule on the station to stock it. With the Sort Gauge it sorts at the door: each unit is read once and sent to one address if it is in the band, another if not. Sneak with a dye sets the in-band address.
feedback.jei.info.sorting_station: A tube station with up to three sort stages, each a separate reader (a magnet, an optical head or a weigher) that a unit must pass. Cargo it cannot place goes to the reject address (an off-hand dye sets it) instead of through. It runs at the pace of its slowest stage. The Sort Gauge adds and steps stages.
feedback.jei.info.sort_gauge: Use on a tube station to step the last sort stage through its bands and then its property; sneak to add a stage, or clear them when full.
feedback.jei.info.vacuum_pump: A shaft-driven pump that draws air out of the tube run it faces, with its shaft across the flow. An evacuated tube keeps its vacuum only while this keeps up with the seals' leak.
feedback.jei.info.linear_motor: A coil ring placed against a tube block. Fed with current it drives capsules that carry a magnetic plate through that block at twice the speed; plain capsules ignore it.
feedback.jei.info.carrier: A capsule that rides a tube. Holds four stacks and an address color; a heavy load slows it.
feedback.jei.info.magnetic_carrier: A capsule with a magnetic plate, the kind a linear-motor ring can drive.
feedback.jei.info.pod: A one-seat capsule for a wide-bore tube. Stock it in a tube station and right-click the station with an empty hand to board. Sneak to leave in an emergency: you step out at the tube. Pods are slower than capsules at the same pressure and slow down further in bends and vertical runs. Only players ride; a pod needs a wide-bore run all the way. If a chunk on the path is not loaded the pod waits for it.
feedback.jei.info.creative_air: Operator tab only. Compresses air at a set temperature, flow and pressure into any tube run, pipe run or gas tank beside it.
feedback.jei.info.ender_port: One end of a bonded pair: one pearl and two plates make two ports with the same bond. Items put in one cross to the other when the pair's per-minute mass allowance covers them and the tank holds enough liquid teleportant, which costs more for heavier items and longer distances. Both ends must be loaded; chunks are not loaded for it unless a Chunk Anchor is fitted. A shulker box next to the port seals it, and shulker boxes, fluid-holding items and pods never cross.
feedback.jei.info.ender_anchor: Use on an Ender Port to keep its chunk loaded so the pair works while nobody is near. Without it the pair pauses whenever an end is unloaded.
modular.feedback.desc.part.belt_band: The flexible strip a belt runs on. Its material sets how well cargo grips it and how hot the cargo may be; leather and rubber grip, a steel link band takes the heat. A textured face grips harder and a link band bends round hot cargo that would char a hide.
modular.feedback.role.band.tip: The strip cargo rides on. Its material sets the grip on a slope and the heat it takes.
modular.feedback.role.cleat.tip: Optional bars across the band. They roughen the face, so the belt holds cargo on a steeper slope.
feedback.jei.info.conveyor_belt: A belt cell built at a Woodworking Table (a Smithing Table for a steel link strip) from a band (leather, rubber or a steel link strip) with an optional cleat. Place cells end to end facing the same way, finish the run with a head roller, and turn the head's shaft: the run moves cargo at the shaft's speed. Sneak-click a cell with a belt in hand to make it climb or fall by one block; an empty hand sneak-clicks turns it. Cargo holds on a rise only while the belt's grip times the cargo's grip is enough, so a cleated or rubber band climbs where leather slips and a wet belt slips sooner. Hot cargo above the band's limit wears the band; a worn band slips but never fails. Dropped items that land on a belt ride it, and so do creatures. A coil block set on a belt heats what passes under it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_head: The driven roller at the exit end of a belt run; every other cell is an idler. Feed it a shaft from either side across the belt. The shaft's speed sets the belt's, and the load on the shaft is the roller's own plus the weight of the cargo on the run: an undersized shaft slows the whole belt.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_funnel_in: Fits into a belt cell and pulls items from the container on the side it was placed against, one unit at a time, as fast as the belt has room. It reads nothing about what it pulls.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_funnel_out: Fits into a belt cell and pushes passing cargo into the container on its side. At the end of a run a full container leaves the cargo queued on the belt.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_chute: Drops cargo off the belt, down the column below its side or into what is there: a container, a lower belt or the floor. Brittle cargo (low toughness for its hardness) breaks on a long drop.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_diverter: A plow that sweeps every unit that reaches it to its side. Empty-hand click engages or releases it; a controller can too.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_splitter: Sends passing cargo to alternate sides of the belt. If one side is full the other takes it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_magnet: A permanent magnet over the belt. It sweeps magnetic cargo to its side and misses cargo above its Curie temperature or made of a non-magnetic metal; it will pull iron junk just as readily. Cargo it cannot place passes by.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_electromag: A switchable magnet drawing a little current. Stronger than a permanent one, it can be released by hand or by a controller. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_screen: A mesh the cargo passes over. Units lighter than the aperture fall through; click to choose fine, medium or coarse. Fines clog the mesh and blind it until it is wiped by hand.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_air_jet: A nozzle blowing light, dry cargo off the belt. It needs a gas pipe with pressure beside it and takes a little air with each puff; the pressure sets how dense a unit it can lift. Damp or sticky cargo stays put.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_optical: Reads the sheen of passing cargo and sweeps one band (dull, mid or bright) to its side. Click to choose the band. Glowing-hot cargo reads bright, and a dirty head reads everything duller until wiped. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_weigher: Reads the weight of passing cargo: density bands and size bands. A stack blurs the reading because it weighs the pile. Click to choose the band. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_counter: Counts what passes and reports the count and rate to a linked controller. It controls nothing and reads nothing about the cargo.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_cooler: A cold plate under which cargo cools toward a window, as a hot ingot must before it meets a leather band.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_gate: Holds cargo at its cell until released. Empty-hand click or a controller releases it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_hood: A cover over a belt cell. Rain and fluid above no longer wet the band there, so a rise holds its grip; a unit carrying fluid still wets it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_linear: A coil in place of a roller. While it has current it drives the whole run at a fixed speed, with or without a head roller or shaft. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_fan: Blows air over passing cargo and cools it. Draws a little current.
jade.feedback.pen.stomach.both: Stomach holds an oxidiser and a fuel
jade.feedback.attune.1: Attunement quiet: no experience reaches it
jade.feedback.attune.2: Attunement quiet: the run stands too low
jade.feedback.echo.1: The crude is ringing under the lift
jade.feedback.echo.2: The crude is shrieking: slow the lift or add flywheel
feedback.jei.ore_processing.separate: Separate: wash, magnet or optical sorter
feedback.jei.ore_processing.leach: Leach in the Reactor, then win the metal
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.0: Clean: hardly any slag left in it.
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.1: A little slag in the iron.
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.2: Plenty of slag in the iron.
feedback.jei.info.puddling_furnace: A reverberatory hearth with a rabble turned by a shaft into its back. Load cast iron and an oxidiser (hematite, magnetite, limonite or burnt iron scale), light it and keep it between 1250 and 1450 Tu while the shaft turns it at 20 to 60 RPM. Stalled or racing, the charge crusts and the hold falls back. Past 1500 the oxidiser eats the iron and leaves burnt iron. The ball it gives is a bloom with little slag in it: shingle it at an Anvil or under a Mechanical Hammer.
feedback.jei.info.iron_bloom: Spongy iron with slag trapped between its grains, made by heating iron ore with charcoal between 1000 and 1350 Tu (above that it carburises into cast iron) or by puddling cast iron. Put it hot in the center of an Anvil with a hammer and shingle it: strike to squeeze the slag out through the edges before the piece cools, and turn it to herd the rest. A Mechanical Hammer beating a bloom hot drives the slag out unattended.
feedback.jei.info.bloomery_slag: The slag a bloom gives up when it is worked. It still holds some iron: crush and melt it for pig iron.
screen.feedback.shingle.hint: Click to strike (right click for a heavy blow), R turns the piece, Space puts the hammer down. Squeeze the slag out to the edges while it is runny.
forge.feedback.shingle.done: The slag is out: wrought iron.
forge.feedback.shingle.left: Slag still in it. Reheat the bloom and work it again.
feedback.jei.info.redstone_receiver: Turns redstone into a data reading. Any redstone signal reaching it is read by a Sensor card on the control signal linked to it, as a number from 0 (none) to 15 (full strength), so a program can follow a vanilla lever, plate or detector.
feedback.jei.info.redstone_emitter: Turns a data signal into redstone. A controller, timer or sensor program switches it like any actuator; engaged, it puts a full-strength redstone signal out of every face, so a vanilla piston, lamp or door can follow a Feedback sensor.
feedback.jei.info.analog_adapter: A fitting for a machine with a variable setting, such as a valve's opening or an engine's throttle. Right-click a face of the machine with it; redstone power arriving at that face then sets the setting from none to full in fifteen even steps: power 15 is full, power 0 is none. Take it off with a crowbar, and the machine returns to full. Any machine with a switch also starts and stops from redstone directly, with no adapter.
feedback.jei.info.ripeness_probe: Reads how grown the crop in front of it is, in quarters, from the crop's own age. A row of them sees a field. It reads any block that has an age, so a modded crop works too.
feedback.jei.info.photocell: Reads the light at the block in front of it, in fifths: the brighter of daylight and block light. It reads its own lamp as well, so a lamp it switches can switch it back.
feedback.jei.info.presence_plate: Reads whether a creature or a dropped item stands in the block in front of it: full when one does, nothing when not.
feedback.jei.info.fill_gauge: Reads how full the inventory or tank in front of it is, in eighths.
feedback.jei.info.tension_gauge: Reads how taut the fixed line is that runs through its own block, in sixths: the load hanging on the line over what its material is rated for. A slack line, or none, reads nothing; a line over its rating reads full and is already straining. Set it where a fixed line crosses, and a controller card reads it.
feedback.jei.info.note_block: Built from a body cut to a pitch and one or two noisemakers: each noisemaker's shape is an instrument, its material sets how loud and how high it rings. It makes no sound without one. An empty hand steps the note and plays it; a rising signal or a punch plays it. Needs the cell above it clear.
feedback.jei.info.dropper: A spring pushes the item out, not the signal: a redstone signal only releases a cocked spring, and the spring stays spent afterwards. Cock it again by sneaking and using it with an empty hand, or by touching a turning shaft. A signal on a spent spring only clicks.
feedback.jei.info.dispenser: A dropper with a fitting that uses the item: arrows are fired, buckets emptied, fire charges lit, as in vanilla. Like the dropper, a signal only releases a cocked spring. Cock it by hand (sneak and use with an empty hand) or with a turning shaft.
feedback.jei.info.hopper: Carries one item at a time from the container above (or an item lying on it) into the block it faces, and holds nothing itself: if the block it faces cannot take the item, nothing moves. A chain of hoppers is a conveyor, not a store or a sorter. A redstone signal switches it off.
feedback.jei.info.observer: Reads high for half a second after the block in front of it changes state, such as a crop growing a stage or a door opening. It reports the change a tick late.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_mast: A vertical shaft whose arm sweeps a circle. Seat an arm (its length is the field's radius), a tip, and for the cutting, breaking and striking tips a machine head from a Smithing Table; put seed or feed in by hand or hopper and take what the collecting tip gathers from the other slots. The tip works every cell the arm crosses, along its whole length, and knows nothing about the job: a cutting tip cuts green crop as readily as ripe, so switch the drive with a ripeness probe. A long arm with a heavy head asks for more Su than a weak drive gives. Sneak with an empty hand to take parts back; an empty hand reads the arm and the head's condition.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_arm: An arm for the pivot mast. Its length in blocks (short 3, medium 5, long 8) is the radius of the field it sweeps, and the drive load grows with it.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_cut: Cuts plants, leaves, cane, kelp and the wool of sheep along the pivot arm. Needs a machine head seated in the mast; one too soft for the target cuts nothing.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_break: Breaks blocks along the pivot arm that the seated head can overcome. A block too hard for the head does not break, and the head wears by the difference. Machines and chests are left standing.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_plant: Places a block item from the mast's input slot, such as a seed or a sapling, in every empty cell it can stand in. It plants wherever the item can survive, wanted or not.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_feed: Uses the item in the mast's input slot on whatever is in each cell: feed on an animal, bone meal on a crop, shears on a sheep. It does not choose; a wrong item is spent as readily as a right one.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_strike: Strikes creatures in the cells it crosses, with the weight of the seated machine head. Hurts anything living, including a player.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_collect: Sweeps dropped items into the mast's output slots, which a hopper or belt can empty.
feedback.jei.info.dark_cell: The controller of a mob farm, set in the wall of a sealed room. The room is the cell: if it is closed and dark inside, hostile mobs gather there as a count, not as creatures, up to the room's capacity. Kill-method blocks set in the wall (fall, fire, crush, fume, shock, radiation) work on what has gathered, and the drops come out of the cell into a chest, hopper or belt beside the controller. Mobs the walls do not hold back wear the shield down once the room is crowded; mend it by hand with building blocks. At nothing left, the mobs spill out. A Catalyst Tap in reach takes the XP of zombies and skeletons at a loss. Empty hand reads the cell.
feedback.jei.info.fall_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Drops what stands on it; the height (small, medium, large) is stepped with an empty hand. Harms only mobs that take fall damage.
feedback.jei.info.fire_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Burns what stands on it, as hot as the heat pointed at it. Mobs that do not burn are untouched. Food drops come out cooked; left in the output, food chars.
feedback.jei.info.crush_head: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. A hammer on a vertical shaft: put a machine head in it and turn it. Its harm is the head's strength; a head too light for the mobs wears.
feedback.jei.info.fume_port: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Takes a toxic gas by pipe or bucket and lets it into the room. Harms only mobs that breathe; the worse the gas, the worse the harm. A full tank with nothing to do seeps into the room outside.
feedback.jei.info.shock_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Passes the current it is given through what stands on it. Big bodies are scorched, so their drops are charred. A few mobs shrug off a shock.
feedback.jei.info.radiation_source: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Holds one radioactive item and kills everything alive in the room with it. The drops come out contaminated and give off radiation themselves, and so does the source: stand clear.
feedback.darkcell.report: Cell of %s blocks, %s mobs, shield %s%%, %s kill methods
feedback.jei.info.stoker: A screw feed that pushes solid fuel into the firebox in front of it, driven by a vertical shaft. Three drum sizes, stepped with an empty hand, set how much each turn moves. A hopper or belt fills it from any side but the front. It does not look at the fire: a full firebox refuses the fuel and the feed stalls.
feedback.jei.info.creel: A basket trap for water. Set it where it is under water in a pond, river or sea; a puddle catches nothing. Every couple of minutes it draws a catch from the same fish and junk the water gives a rod, never treasure; bait in the top slot shortens the wait and is spent. An empty hand empties the basket, and a hopper can take from it. A full basket stops.
feedback.jei.info.fish_wheel: A water wheel with baskets on its blades. It turns in a current like any wheel but gives half the power, and while it turns it draws a catch from the same fish the water gives a rod, never treasure; more blades in the current catch faster. An empty hand empties the baskets, and a hopper can take from them. A full basket stops the catch, not the wheel.
feedback.jei.info.kiln_zone: A tunnel kiln zone. Ware goes in at the back from a hopper or belt, rides a car through four positions of heat (a cool start, two hot, a cool finish) and comes out the front into whatever takes items. Heat comes from a firebox or burner pointed at it; the car is driven by a vertical shaft, and its speed sets how long ware stays: slow gives a clean result, fast leaves ware raw, a stopped car leaves it in the fire to char, crack or spoil. It runs food by its cooking ladder and anything else by the same rows a furnace uses, but does not melt metal.
gui.feedback.depot.linked: Linked. Parcels on the road here: %s
gui.feedback.depot.unlinked: Not linked: use a link card on this and another depot.
feedback.depot.recorded: Depot recorded on the card. Use it on another depot to link them.
feedback.depot.same: That is the depot already recorded.
feedback.depot.unreachable: The recorded depot is gone or too far to reach: the card keeps what it recorded.
feedback.jei.info.depot: One end of a trade road. Link it to a depot in another village with a link card, put goods on the outgoing shelf, and lay a road (path, gravel, stone, brick or planks) leaving it. On the next market day a convoy carries the outgoing goods to the other depot, which carries its own to yours; the trip takes longer the farther apart the depots are. Raiders take some stacks on the road, fewer when a bell stands near either end. A donkey courier is seen setting out when a player is there. The incoming shelf is taken from, not put on. Villages pay differently for the same goods: carry what the other village wants.
feedback.jei.info.depot_link_card: Use it on a depot to record that depot, then on another depot to link the two. The link is wiped from the card when made.
feedback.jei.reach.flow: moves %s mB per tick for each RPM
feedback.jei.reach.gears: gears %s to %s input turns per output turn, torque multiplied by the same
village.feedback.cross.inactive: This square is too small or not paved: the cross needs a wide, open, paved square.
village.feedback.cross.today: Market day. The trader is in.
village.feedback.cross.in: The next market is in %s days.
village.feedback.board.raid: A raid is on. Stocked shelves draw raiders: guard them.
village.feedback.board.bounty: A banner bounty stands: %s emeralds for an illager banner (%s owed). Put one in the slot on the Contracts tab and press Banner.
village.feedback.board.market_none: No market square stands near the board.
village.feedback.board.market_today: Market day today at the cross.
feedback.jei.info.market_cross: A pillar for a paved square. Pave a wide, open square (path, gravel, stone, brick or planks, with sky above) and set the cross on it: when the square is big enough the cross is active, and every eighth day the wandering trader sets up at it for the day. Villagers near an active cross want more things and make another errand that day, and shops near it restock. A village that honors you brings a second trader selling goods of its region. Right-click it to read whether the square counts and when the next market is.
gui.feedback.board.no_orders: No villager in range has an order.
gui.feedback.board.no_contracts: The village has posted no contracts.
village.feedback.board.contract_line: %s of %s delivered, at least %s, %s days left, %s each
village.feedback.board.standing.0: The village does not know you.
village.feedback.board.next.1: Next: yet more contracts each day, and a bigger bonus for finishing.
village.feedback.board.next.2: Next: honored standing earns a blueprint for every contract finished.
feedback.jei.info.ledger_board: The village's notice board. Place it near the bell. Right-click it to read, in one place, every open order of the villagers around it grouped by what is asked, the contracts the village has posted, and the notices. A contract asks several pieces of one kind, each at least Good; put a piece in the slot and deliver it, or let a Counter within twelve blocks of the board fill contracts from what reaches it. Each piece pays by its class, and finishing a contract adds a bonus and raises the village's regard of you; an Exceptional run, or an honored village, earns a blueprint. The board stores nothing about a player: it reads the villagers' own gossip.
