feedback.counter.catchment: In reach %s, want something here %s, errands pending %s, out of reach %s. Today: walk-in sales %s, hand-over sales %s.
gui.feedback.counter.hint: Click to buy one, Shift-click a stack. Prices are emeralds each.
feedback.jei.info.counter: A shop counter with a nine-slot shelf. The front is the customer side: right-click the front or top to buy from the shelf with emeralds, which go into the till. The back is the keeper side: stock the shelf, set a price on each slot and take the till. A stocked shelf draws villagers: one that is idle or meeting, has no errand left to run and wants something on the shelf, and has a way to walk to the front, comes and buys at your price. A villager sealed in a cell has no way and never comes. Roads of path, gravel, stone or planks carry the reach farther down the street. A villager buys above market up to a ceiling, and gossips against the keeper for it. Hand-over still works: goods fed into the intake from the sides are handed to a villager within 8 blocks as a delivery would be, and a want sold this way pays three quarters of its line. Emeralds come out of the till slots and whatever was not taken comes out of the returns. Hoppers fill the shelf from the back and top. Right-click a side to read the catchment.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.textured: A broad belt with a ribbed face. Grips better.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.link: Linked plates. Grips less and takes far more heat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pack: A big pack: 27 slots, and it weighs on the wearer.
modular.feedback.role.bowl.tip: The scoop. Its material sets how much it holds and how it takes heat.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_buffer: A hydraulic buffer behind the bolt: it slows the cycle %2$s%% and takes %1$s%% of the kick (the fluid's viscosity, at its thickest: a cold barrel).
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_obturato: A seal that stops gas slipping past the round: %1$s%% less kick and %2$s%% tighter (the softer the metal, the better), until it burns through.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_reticle: A lit sight picture: %1$s%% tighter spread (the mineral's glow), visible only in low light.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_fire_con: A circuit reads the shot: the group tightens by up to 45%% for a silent circuit, less as it gets noisy, and the card shows range, lead and drop.
message.feedback.suit_endernet_fitted: Endernet upgrade fitted to the suit: its scans now reach the bonded Data Port.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_sear: A magnet holds the sear: %1$s%% tighter spread and a %2$s%% quicker cycle while the barrel is cool (a non-magnetic metal does nothing).
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.cell: What the stack weighs. Swung as a club it hits harder for it; the charge it holds does not change.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.charge: What the charge weighs, filler and casing.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.gun: What the gun weighs unloaded. A heavier gun kicks less and swings slower as a bludgeon.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.shield: Every part's volume times its material's density. A heavier shield swings and raises slower.
commands.feedback.blueprint: Gave a blueprint of the held item.
commands.feedback.no_modular: Hold a modular item (not a blueprint).
advancement.feedback.combat.this_is_very: Fire an assault rifle with a pistol grip.
advancement.feedback.combat.big_iron.des: A big iron on your hip: fire a revolver with the longest barrel there is.
advancement.feedback.combat.long_ass_gun: A Gun, of the Long-Ass Variety
I shot Darnell with a long-ass gun then tossed it in the aquarium!
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.conflict: Cannot go on with what is fitted now.
modular.feedback.desc.part.engine_block: The block the cylinders are bored in. Its layout sets how the engine runs: inline is plain, a V is compact and light but revs lower, a boxer is heavier and revs higher.
modular.feedback.desc.part.piston_set: The pistons, one per cylinder. Their count is the cylinders; their metal sets how fast they may move, and so the redline.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crankshaft: Turns the pistons' stroke into rotation. A forged crank revs higher than a cast one; a crank of a weaker metal than the pistons holds the revs down.
modular.feedback.desc.part.cylinder_head: Closes the cylinders. Its compression ratio decides which fuels it runs well on: low misfires on nothing and knocks on nothing, high makes more torque and knocks on low-ignition fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spark_plug: Lights the charge in each cylinder. The electrode's metal sets how long it lasts (a metal that melts hotter erodes slower) and how readily it fouls (a metal that carries heat away runs cold). Running in a vehicle wears it; a worn plug makes the engine stumble.
modular.feedback.desc.part.gear_set: The gear wheels of a gearbox. Their count is the number of forward gears; their metal sets how fast a shift at speed wears them.
modular.feedback.desc.part.synchro_ring: Matches the speed of a gear to the shaft before it engages.
modular.feedback.desc.part.gearbox_case: Holds the gears and what keeps them oiled.
modular.feedback.role.engine_block.tip: The engine block. Its layout sets torque per liter, how high the engine revs and how heavy it is.
modular.feedback.role.pistons.tip: The pistons. Their shape is the number of cylinders, the bore you set is their width, and their metal is the engine's: it must be a metal with a measured yield strength, and sets the redline.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tube_envelope: The glass bulb of a vacuum tube. Its glass sets how good a vacuum it can hold and how hot it may be baked; its diameter sets how fast it warms: a wide bulb needs more heater.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tube_cathode: The emitter, heated until it gives off electrons. A metal that melts before it glows enough gives next to nothing; a long emitter gives more current and drinks more heater power.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tube_grid: The grid wires between cathode and plate. More grids and a finer pitch make a stronger amplifier; a grid with none makes a diode; a seal with gas left in turns a gridded tube into a thyratron.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tube_plate: The plate the electrons land on. A large plate takes more power and slows the tube; a metal that sheds heat poorly slows it further.
modular.feedback.role.tube_envelope.tip: The glass bulb. It must insulate and take heat; its tightness sets the best vacuum a seal can reach.
modular.feedback.role.tube_cathode.tip: The emitter. A high-melting metal that gives up electrons readily emits fully at a lower heat; a longer one gives more current for more heater power.
modular.feedback.role.tube_grid.tip: Optional. One to three grids make a triode, tetrode or pentode; a good conductor holds its potential and keeps the gain.
modular.feedback.role.tube_plate.tip: The plate. Wider is more power and less speed; a metal that sheds heat poorly slows it.
modular.feedback.axis.bulb.tip: How wide the glass bulb is. A wider bulb warms slower.
modular.feedback.axis.emitter.tip: How long the cathode is. A longer emitter gives more current and amplifies more, and costs more heater power.
modular.feedback.axis.grids.tip: How many grids. None is a diode; one a triode, then a tetrode, then a pentode, each stronger. A little slower with each.
modular.feedback.desc.part.resonator_cry: The crystal of a resonator. It must ring (a piezo coupling): amethyst does. A bigger crystal is steadier and carries less; a narrower cut separates more channels and carries less.
modular.feedback.desc.part.resonator_ele: The electrodes the crystal rings between. A better conductor couples the crystal to its wire better.
modular.feedback.desc.part.lattice_body: The living mesh of a sculk lattice. Its material must hold experience; more cells and a finer mesh hold more variables and learn less.
modular.feedback.desc.part.lattice_frame: The frame the mesh sits in. A better insulator keeps what the mesh holds when the host loses power.
The ringing crystal: its piezo coupling, size and cut set stability, channels and bandwidth.
modular.feedback.role.lattice_body.tip: The living mesh. It must be a material that holds experience; how much, how fast and how well it keeps it set the figures.
modular.feedback.axis.cells.tip: How many cells of mesh. More hold more variables.
modular.feedback.axis.mesh.tip: How fine the mesh is. Finer holds more and learns less.
modular.feedback.axis.cut.tip: How narrow the cut is. Narrower separates more channels and carries less.
modular.feedback.role.crankshaft.tip: The crank. The stroke you set is how far a piston travels: a short stroke revs higher, a long one makes more torque. A cast crank revs lower than a forged one.
modular.feedback.role.cylinder_head.tip: The head. Its compression ratio sets which fuels the engine runs well on, and a little of its torque.
modular.feedback.role.spark_plug.tip: The spark plug. Its electrode metal sets how long it lasts and how readily it fouls. A plug wears only while the engine runs in a vehicle, and a worn one misses; swap it at the Engineering Table.
modular.feedback.role.gear_set.tip: The gears. Their shape is how many forward gears there are, and you set the ratio of each: input turns per output turn, so 3.5 is a low gear and 0.8 an overdrive. Their metal sets how fast a shift at speed wears the box.
modular.feedback.role.synchro.tip: A dog clutch is plain and wears the box most when shifted at speed; a synchromesh matches speeds first and wears it far less, for a little weight.
modular.feedback.role.gearbox_case.tip: The case. Dry, splash or pressure oiling: the more oil reaches the gears, the less a shift at speed wears them and the heavier the case.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.inline_blo: Cylinders in a row: the plain layout.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.v_block: Two banks at an angle: a short, light block that revs a little lower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.boxer_bloc: Opposed banks that cancel each other's shake: revs higher, but a heavier block with a touch less torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_cylind: Six cylinders: twice the swept volume of three, and the ingots to match.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.eight_cyli: Eight cylinders: the most torque, and the most metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cast_crank: A poured crank: cheap, but it will not rev as high.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.forged_cra: A hammered crank: stronger, so the engine revs higher, for more metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.low_compre: Runs on fuels that ignite easily without knocking, and makes a little less torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.high_compr: More torque, but a fuel that ignites easily knocks and wears the engine.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_speed: Six forward gears: the widest spread, and the most metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dog_clutch: Plain dogs that mesh as they are: a shift at speed wears the box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.synchromes: Rings that match the gear's speed before it meshes: a shift at speed wears the box about two fifths less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dry_case: Grease only: the lightest case, and the gears wear most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.splash_cas: The gears dip in an oil bath: a quarter less wear on shifts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pressure_c: An oil pump feeds the gears: half the wear, and the heaviest case.
modular.feedback.axis.orifice.tip: How wide the pilot's jet opens. A wider orifice burns more of the tank's fluid for the same flame.
feedback.jei.info.engine: A piston engine: block, pistons, crank, head and spark plug, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you also set the bore and stroke. Place it against the end of a shaft; it burns fuel from its own tank and turns the shaft like a Steam Engine. In a vehicle the spark plug wears with running time and a worn one makes it stumble; swap it at the Engineering Table.
modular.feedback.desc.part.vessel_shell: The wall of a pressure vessel. Its shape and thickness, and its metal's strength, set the pressure it holds and the room inside.
modular.feedback.role.vessel_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure and leaves less room. A sphere carries a load best, a flat box worst but fills the block. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.exchanger_cor: The tubes of a heat exchanger. Their metal's conductivity and the area they present set how fast heat crosses.
modular.feedback.role.exchanger_core.tip: The tubes. A metal that conducts heat well and more area move heat faster. The metal needs a stated conductivity.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tank_shell: The wall of a gas tank. Its shape and thickness, and its metal's strength, set the pressure it holds and the room inside.
modular.feedback.role.tank_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure and leaves less room. A sphere carries a load best, a flat box worst but holds most. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
figure.feedback.block.Relief: Vents %s mB a tick near the danger line
modular.feedback.desc.part.wheel_rim: The rim and buckets of a water wheel. Its size and bucket count set the power it makes and how slowly it turns; its wood sets its momentum.
modular.feedback.role.wheel_rim.tip: The rim. A bigger wheel and more buckets give more power; a bigger wheel turns slower for the same flow; a heavier rim holds more momentum.
modular.feedback.desc.part.motor_winding: The winding of a linear motor ring. More turns pull a magnetic capsule harder and draw more current; a thicker wire draws more still.
modular.feedback.role.motor_winding.tip: The coil wound round the tube. More turns push harder and draw more; a thicker wire draws more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.coil_element: The wire of a heating coil. A thicker wire draws more current, more turns draw less; a metal that resists current turns more of it to heat (nichrome heats well, copper hardly), and the coil holds as hot as its metal before it wears.
modular.feedback.role.coil_element.tip: The wire wound into the coil. Thicker draws more; more turns draw less and weigh more; a resistive metal heats best.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crucible_shel: The wall of a crucible. More slots make a bigger vessel that takes more heat to warm; a thicker wall holds heat longer and takes longer to warm. The wall wears when it runs hotter than its own material holds.
modular.feedback.role.crucible_shell.tip: The wall. A metal wall takes up and gives off heat quickly; brick holds it and warms slowly. Run it hotter than the wall material holds and the wall wears thin.
feedback.jei.info.heating_coil: Eu to heat: set it under a vessel, or against one. A coil is wound from a wire at the Blueprint Table: a thicker wire draws more current, more turns draw less, and a metal that resists current (nichrome) turns more of it to heat than one that does not (copper). It holds as hot as its wire metal before it wears.
feedback.jei.info.data_connector: Joins data nodes with wire. Use it on one node, then another, to link them; the wire is paid for by its length and has a reach. Shift-scroll changes what a use does: link, unlink a pair, clear every wire on a node, or paint a controller link with the dye in the other hand (no dye clears it).
feedback.cable.coat_live: A live cable cannot be coated
feedback.cable.strip_live: A live cable cannot be stripped
feedback.jei.info.crucible: A vessel for melting, built at a Stonecutter from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. Its wall is brick or metal plate: more slots make a bigger vessel that is slower to warm, a thicker wall is slower still, and the wall's own material sets how much heat that is. Held above the temperature its wall material holds, the wall wears and leaks more heat, and a spent wall gives way.
modular.feedback.desc.part.store_core: The wall of a thermal store. A thick wall has more to heat and loses less; its material's conductivity sets the loss.
modular.feedback.role.store_core.tip: The wall. Thicker holds heat longer and takes longer to charge. Ceramic keeps heat; metal gives it away.
figure.feedback.block.Leak: Loses %s Work a tick per Tu
modular.feedback.desc.part.jar_glass: The glass of a Leyden jar. More plate area holds more charge, thinner glass more again, and thinner glass leaks it faster.
modular.feedback.role.jar_glass.tip: The glass. It must insulate. Thin glass stores more and leaks much faster; more area stores more.
Hoop bands round the shell. A strong band metal against the shell's raises the pressure it carries.
modular.feedback.role.relief_valve.tip: A valve that opens near the danger line and lets air out, so a pump that outruns the leak still cannot burst it.
modular.feedback.role.fin_stack.tip: A second metal bonded to the tubes. Its conductivity adds to the heat that crosses.
modular.feedback.role.rim_ring.tip: A ring of dense metal round the rim. More momentum, and slower to spin up.
modular.feedback.role.lagging.tip: A poor conductor wrapped round the outside. The poorer, the less heat the store loses.
modular.feedback.role.salt_fill.tip: Salt packed inside: more stuff to heat, so the store holds more.
modular.feedback.role.foil.tip: Foil lining the jar. The more current its metal carries, the harder the jar discharges.
modular.feedback.role.outer_sleeve.tip: A glass sleeve over the jar. A second insulator: the charge leaks away more slowly.
modular.feedback.desc.part.pump_impeller: The impeller of a pump. Its diameter and shape set how much it moves and how hard it is to turn.
modular.feedback.role.pump_impeller.tip: The impeller. A bigger one moves more and is harder to turn. Axial moves the most and lifts poorly; a screw moves little and lifts well.
modular.feedback.role.volute.tip: A casing that turns speed into flow: a pump moves a little more for a little more load.
modular.feedback.desc.part.compressor_ro: The rotor of a compressor. Its size and staging set how much it moves, how hard it is to turn, and how hot it heats the gas.
modular.feedback.role.compressor_rotor.t: The rotor. A bigger one moves more and is harder to turn. Staging moves more and heats the gas less, at more load.
modular.feedback.role.intercooler.tip: Takes heat out of the gas between stages, so it leaves cooler.
modular.feedback.desc.part.thruster_nozz: The nozzle of a thruster. Its bore sets how hard it pushes and how much fuel it burns; its shape trades push against fuel.
modular.feedback.role.thruster_nozzle.ti: The nozzle. A wider bore pushes harder and burns more fuel. A cone pushes hardest and burns most; a throat pushes least and sips fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_bel: A bell that expands the jet: the baseline push and the baseline burn.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_con: A wide cone: pushes 30% harder, and burns 50% more fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_thr: A bare throat: pushes 30% less, and burns half the fuel.
modular.feedback.role.regen_jacket.tip: A plate wrapped round the nozzle that the fuel runs through first. The fuel arrives warm, so 15% less of it burns for the same push.
feedback.jei.info.thruster: Pushes the body it is part of along its facing, burning liquid fuel from a pipe or bucket; right-click to switch it on. It needs air to burn (not in the End, not underwater) unless the fuel carries its own oxygen. Built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table (Aerospace Treatise II): the nozzle's bore and shape set the push and the fuel it burns, a regen jacket saves fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.burner_nozzle: The nozzle of a burner. Its bore sets how much fuel it burns; its shape trades burn against flame temperature.
modular.feedback.role.burner_nozzle.tip: The nozzle. A wider bore burns more fuel. A jet burns more and hotter; a wick burns little and cooler.
modular.feedback.role.flame_holder.tip: A small metal piece that steadies the flame, which burns a little hotter.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crank_arm: The arm of a hand crank. A long arm is more lever and a slower hand.
modular.feedback.role.crank_arm.tip: The arm. Longer is more Su and fewer RPM. An offset crank has more lever for a little less speed.
modular.feedback.role.crank_flywheel.tip: A small disc on the crank: it carries the turn through the dead spot, and is slower to start.
modular.feedback.desc.part.magnet_core: The core of an electromagnet. More turns pull harder and draw more current; the shape trades pull against reach.
modular.feedback.role.magnet_core.tip: The core. More turns pull harder and draw more current. A horseshoe pulls harder and reaches less; a pot core pulls hardest and barely reaches.
modular.feedback.role.yoke.tip: Closes the magnetic path: a little more pull for the same current.
modular.feedback.desc.part.thermo_wire: The wire pair of a thermocouple probe: two metals joined at a tip. The gap between their Seebeck figures sets how finely it reads; the weaker metal's service temperature is the top of its scale.
modular.feedback.role.thermo_wire.tip: The two wires. Pick two different metals: the further apart they sit in Seebeck figure, the finer the probe reads; a metal that melts low caps the top of the scale.
feedback.jei.info.thermocouple_probe: Two wires of different metals joined at a tip, placed against a block: it reads that block's temperature as a banded signal for a controller card, with no power. The gap between the metals' Seebeck figures sets how many bands it reads in; the weaker metal's service temperature is the top of its scale, so a copper wire melts before a hot furnace is read and a hotter pair reads more coarsely. Use it with an empty hand to see the reading.
modular.feedback.desc.part.thermo_leg: The legs of a thermoelectric generator: two metals joined at the hot end. The gap between their Seebeck figures sets the voltage a degree of difference drives (the same metal twice drives none); the section sets the current; the weaker metal's service temperature is the hottest the pair stands.
modular.feedback.role.thermo_leg.tip: The two legs. Pick two different metals: the further apart they sit in Seebeck figure, the more a degree of difference gives. A wider section gives more current.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.stubby_leg: Short, thick legs: more current for the section, but they conduct the heat straight through and hold less of the temperature difference.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.slender_le: Long, thin legs: less current for the section, but they hold more of the temperature difference.
figure.feedback.block.Gap.label: Seebeck gap
feedback.jei.info.thermoelectric_generat: Two legs of different metals, a hot side and a cold side: a trickle of LV current from the temperature difference. Put it against a heat source (a fire, a hot vessel, a coil) and let its other side shed to the air, to water or ice touching it, or to a cryocooler's cold head. The voltage a degree drives is the gap between the metals' Seebeck figures, so the pair is the design; the same metal twice gives nothing. Current goes with the square of the voltage, up to what the legs' section carries. Past the weaker leg's service temperature the legs fail and it gives nothing.
modular.feedback.desc.part.cell_anode: The anode of a galvanic cell. A bigger one feeds more current and lasts longer; the shape trades current against life.
modular.feedback.role.cell_anode.tip: The anode. A bigger one gives more current and lasts longer. A plate gives more current for a shorter life; a block lasts longest.
modular.feedback.desc.part.lamp_filament: The filament of a lamp. A thicker one draws more current and lasts longer.
modular.feedback.role.lamp_filament.tip: The filament, which must conduct. Thicker draws more and lasts longer. Carbon draws more and is tougher; a fine one draws little and burns out sooner.
modular.feedback.role.ballast.tip: A small resistor in line: the lamp rides a little overvoltage before it burns out.
figure.feedback.block.Burnout: Burns out at %s times the rated packet
modular.feedback.desc.part.boiler_shell: The shell of a boiler. Its wall, shape and metal set the pressure it risks letting go at; the valve and seams follow it.
modular.feedback.role.boiler_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure. A water-tube shell carries more than a fire-tube one; a flat box least. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.flywheel_disc: The disc of a flywheel. Radius and thickness set its momentum; its metal's strength over its weight sets how fast it can spin before the rim strains.
modular.feedback.role.flywheel_disc.tip: The disc. Momentum rises steeply with radius, but a bigger disc strains at fewer RPM. Dense metal holds more momentum; strong, light metal spins faster.
modular.feedback.role.rim_band.tip: Hoop bands round the rim. A strong band metal lets the disc spin faster before the rim strains.
modular.feedback.role.flywheel_bearing.t: A better bearing: less drag for carrying the disc.
modular.feedback.desc.part.prop_hub: The center the blades bolt to. Its shape is the number of blades.
modular.feedback.desc.part.prop_blades: The blades. Their pitch and diameter set the thrust and the speed it pulls to, and their metal sets the tip speed they survive.
modular.feedback.role.prop_hub.tip: The hub. Its shape is the number of blades: more blades pull harder for the same diameter and weigh more.
modular.feedback.role.prop_blades.tip: The blades. The diameter you set is the disc they sweep; pitch is their angle. Their metal, which needs a measured yield strength, sets the tip speed they survive.
feedback.jei.info.sculk_grower: A node on the XP wire that works a ripe Culture Dish beside it without a hand: in the dark, between 10 and 30 Tu, once the run it sits on stands at level 10 or higher it spends 20 points to harvest the dish. The harvest pops above the dish, as a hoe's would. It holds no experience of its own, and the dish's own growth is its pace.
feedback.jei.info.culture_dish: A living sculk culture, fed XP and air from the network. A full culture left in the dark (light level 3 or less), between 10 and 30 Tu, breathing and fed grows a Relay Organ in about five minutes; cut it with a hoe in the three minutes after, or it overgrows and is spent. Left ripe longer it clots, then calls a warden.
feedback.jei.info.gas_cell: One cell of an airship's envelope. It holds a lift gas (hydrogen, wisp gas or helium) from a pipe or bucket, and cells that touch share it. The air it pushes aside weighs more than the gas, and the difference lifts the cell where it sits, so how a ship is loaded decides how it trims; thin air at height lifts less. A bladder skin is the lightest and gas-tight; a skin of cloth coated in slime is heavier and seeps gas slowly. A cell stretches as the air thins: climb with a full cell past what its skin takes and it weeps gas until a Vent Valve lets some out first. An arrow or bullet leaves a hole that leaks until you patch it by hand with cloth, rubber or a plate. Hydrogen and wisp gas burn, and a flame, lava or a running thruster beside a cell lights the whole envelope; helium never does. Cloth and rubber skins burn away with their gas.
feedback.jei.info.vent_valve: Lets gas out of the gas cells beside it, to come down or to relieve a full cell on the climb. Use it to open or shut it by hand, or set it from a Controller card.
feedback.jei.info.ballast_tank: A tank of water that weighs the craft down. Fill it with a bucket or a pipe; use it to dump the water by hand, or set the dump from a Controller card. Dumping lightens the craft, so it rises.
feedback.jei.info.propeller: An aircraft propeller: hub and blades, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you also set the diameter. Place it on the end of a shaft; it pulls the vehicle when turned, and tears itself apart if its tips are driven faster than the metal holds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.two_blade: Two blades: light and cheap, and the least thrust for the disc.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.four_blade: Four blades: more thrust for the same diameter, and heavier.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fine_pitch: Shallow blade angle: a climb prop, strong at low airspeed and soon out of bite at speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.medium_pit: Middling blade angle: a fair thrust and top speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coarse_pit: Steep blade angle: a cruise prop, weak at low airspeed and fast once moving.
feedback.jei.info.transmission: A gearbox: gear set, synchro and case, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you set the ratio of each gear. Place it in a drivetrain; a shifter picks neutral, a forward gear or reverse.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.smoothbore: A plain tube, one cell of stock. A chamber gun's barrel: the round is thrown by burning charge. Bullets scatter more than from a rifled bore.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rifled: Two cells of stock, cut with spiral grooves that spin the bullet. A chamber gun's barrel; a single bullet flies much truer than from a smoothbore.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_rifling: Spiral grooves spin the bullet: its spread is %1$s%% of a plain bore's.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_gun: A longer receiver for a long barrel to steady the bullet. It takes a stock to brace against the shoulder. What it is called follows from the barrel: rifled and narrow a rifle, smooth and wide a shotgun, smooth and narrow a musket, rifled and wide a slug gun.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flintlock: A hammer holding a flint, over a pan of priming powder. Slow to prime and cock between shots, and about one pull in eight flashes in the pan without firing.
advancement.feedback.progress.root.title: Technology
advancement.feedback.progress.root.descr: Stone and wood tools, and no fire you control. Everything starts there.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat_roo: Guns, blades and the skills that make you good with them.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.first: Stone and wood only. Make a fire that stays where you put it.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.reada: A fire has a temperature, and a number beats a guess. Find something that reads it.
Copper melts in a fire you can build. Find a vessel that holds the melt.
Make your first tool or part of stone, wood or bone. A tool you find does not count.
advancement.feedback.progress.age.bronze: Make your first tool or part of copper, tin, bronze or brass.
advancement.feedback.progress.age.iron.d: Make your first tool or part of wrought or cast iron. The prologue ends here; the sciences open.
Make your first tool or part of steel, with the carbon under control.
advancement.feedback.progress.age.machin: Cut a part to size on a lathe, drill press or grinding wheel. The first thing made by a machine to a measure.
Make your first tool or part of stainless steel, nickel, chromium, aluminum, titanium, tungsten, a carbide or netherite.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.iron_: Iron wants a hotter fire that also strips the oxygen from the ore. Push more air, hold more heat.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.steel: Iron with a little carbon, melted clean.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tempe: Fresh steel is brittle or soft. Heat and cooling decide which.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.hard_: Steel fails at heat and wear. Press and sinter something harder.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.hotte: A fuel fire tops out and makes smoke. Find a heat that does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.c: All of this is hand work and your arm is the only power. Turn it into a shaft.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.w: A crank needs a person. A river does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.s: Rivers stay put. Make a shaft turn on fire, anywhere.
Hand-made parts are loose and rough. Make a machine cut to size.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.e: Steam is heavy for its power. Burn something refined inside the machine.
advancement.feedback.progress.electricit: Rub something and hear it snap. Make it repeatable.
Two metals and a wet gap. A steady push with nothing moving.
A shaft only carries work as far as the gears go. Turn rotation into something that travels.
Run a wire to a machine no shaft can reach.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.ti: Machines run until told to stop, and the output suffers. Make one stop on its own.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.co: Reflexes are fixed. Build something you can tell what to do, then give it something to read.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.me: One program fills a controller. Store more than it holds.
Plain rock and water hide a lot. Start with salt.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.elect: Drive current through water or brine and see what comes apart.
Metals will not dissolve in water. A reactor and an acid might.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.oil.d: Fuel is wood and coal. The ground has more.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.press: Some reactions only go when squeezed. Contain it, and leave it a way out.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.alumi: Some ores will not smelt. Electricity can reduce them.
Cooking is hand work too. Find a table to prepare things on.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.skill: Heat a pan and watch it. Food does not wait for you.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.pot.d: Some food wants hours and more than one ingredient.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.arm: Powder, a barrel and a steady hand. Shape its parts at a Smithing Table, Woodworking Table or Stonecutter and assemble a gun at the Engineering Table.
advancement.feedback.progress.nether.net: What the Nether gives is not yet usable. Melt it down and cast it.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.x: Experience can be held, if you find something to hold it.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.e: Write an effect in a script that is not yours.
Some rocks give off more than heat. Find a way to hear it.
A heat source is only a heat source. Make one that sustains itself, and keep it cooled.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.port: The End is out of reach by hand. Send something there anyway.
advancement.feedback.progress.vehicles.s: An engine on a stand goes nowhere. Sit on something that does.
advancement.feedback.combat.dodge_this.d: Shoot an Enderman with a bullet. It dodges arrows, not this.
advancement.feedback.combat.newton_was_r: Fire until the recoil throws you, or the gun.
advancement.feedback.combat.remember_rem: Fire a flintlock. Treason and plot optional.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.press: Let a boiler find out where the pressure goes.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.told_: Let an overspeed trip save a shaft from itself.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.skill: Feed a machine more force than the work can take, and wear it.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.hot_t: Meet something hot with your bare skin.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.aw_ma: Carry a creeper charge into a fire, a fall or an explosion.
Put a phosphor screen on it. Surely.
feedback.jei.info.converter: Steps a line's band by a named step: down one band, down two or up one (click it with an empty hand to pick). Wire the line you step from to the converter and set a Converter Tap against it; the tap is where the stepped line starts, and the two never share a run. Nearly all the power comes out, but the loss is heat in the block: set aluminum Heatsinks against it, because a hot converter loses condition and wastes more. It passes a fixed amount of power, so a lower band out is more amps.
feedback.jei.info.converter_tap: The output side of a Solid-State Converter. Set it against the converter; wire the line you step to onto the tap. Alone it supplies nothing.
feedback.jei.info.heatsink: Finned aluminum. Set against a Solid-State Converter (up to four), it sheds the converter's heat to the air faster.
feedback.jei.info.thermal_store: A tank that holds heat, not electricity, built at a Stonecutter from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. A thick wall has more to heat, so it charges slowly, but it loses less; a thin one charges fast and cools fast. The wall's own conductivity sets the loss, so ceramic keeps heat and metal gives it away. Optional addons: a lagging of poorly conducting stuff cuts the loss, and a salt fill adds heat mass.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.tuned: The eye tunes to this pair.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.untuned: The eye points nowhere. Use it on a port first.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.none: The other end is not placed anywhere.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.elsewhere: The other end is in another dimension.
feedback.jei.info.tuned_eye: A pearl tuned to a bonded pair. Use it on a port to tune it; use it in the air to read how far the other end is and which way, even when that end is far away or unloaded. Crafted from a pearl and redstone dust.
feedback.jei.info.synthetic_pearl: Pressed from silica glass, redstone chromium and teleportant at high heat. It does everything a pearl does: it makes a bonded pair, tunes an eye and blinks. Endermen drop real pearls the cheap way.
feedback.jei.info.porous_aggregate: What end stone leaves after its trapped hydrogen is driven off in a Reactor: a porous, very light rock that barely conducts heat.
gui.feedback.reloading_press.idle: Seat a case and a charge to read the round.
message.feedback.disenchant_stone: An attunement ground off the part.
feedback.jei.info.orb_absorber: Pulls loose experience orbs within a few blocks into the XP wire it sits on, once a second. What the run cannot hold stays in the world as orbs. A lever on the block opens and shuts the draw; a redstone signal holds it shut.
feedback.jei.info.ore_tap: Takes the experience of ore (or any block that pays it) broken within eight blocks into its XP run. Mining machines pay XP the same as a pickaxe. A lever on the block opens and shuts the draw; a redstone signal holds it shut.
feedback.jei.info.trade_tap: Takes the experience a villager trade pays, when the villager is within eight blocks, into its XP run. A Counter sale or purchase pays it too, only into a tap: no orbs drop. A lever on the block opens and shuts the draw; a redstone signal holds it shut.
feedback.jei.info.smelter_tap: Drains the experience a vessel beside it banked from cooking recipes into its XP run, twenty points a second. A vessel with no tap holds its bank until broken, then spills it as orbs. A lever on the block opens and shuts the draw; a redstone signal holds it shut.
feedback.jei.info.disenchant_stone: Right-click with an attuned part: one attunement is ground off, and half of what the session cost comes back as XP into a run beside the stone, or as orbs if there is none.
feedback.jei.info.crystal_bank: Seats up to four XP containers as one node on the XP wire. The bank stands at the containers' common level and holds the sum of their points; the containers settle to one level, so a vial that is fuller gives to one that is emptier. Use with a container to seat it, empty-handed to take the last one out.
feedback.jei.info.crystal_holder: Seats one XP container (an XP container tool or a Reservoir-attuned tool) and shows its store on the XP wire next to it. Take the stack out to take its XP.
feedback.jei.info.coolant_port: A wall cell of the reactor shell. Water goes in by pipe or bucket; the core feeds it to its coolant channels, and the steam they make comes out the same block. With no water the channels carry nothing away and the core climbs.
feedback.jei.info.coolant_channel: A lattice cell that carries heat off the core as water boiling to steam in the Coolant Port. The water slows neutrons a little for the fuel cells beside it, so a channel run dry costs the core some reactivity.
feedback.jei.info.neutron_reflector: A shell wall cell that sends neutrons back into the fuel cells it touches, raising their multiplication. Counts as a sound wall.
feedback.jei.info.star_seat: A lattice cell that seats one Nether star. The star is never used up: it adds reactivity to every live fuel cell, delays the core's temperature feedback, and holds a core with no fuel at a low idle.
feedback.jei.info.flux_meter: Reads a reactor core's neutron flux as a fraction of full power. Use it on the core.
feedback.jei.info.spent_fuel_pool: Holds up to nine spent fuel rods under water. A freshly discharged rod keeps making decay heat for days; the water takes it, boiling away over 100 Tu, so keep the pool topped up. A pool run dry heats its rods until they slump into radioactive slag, and gives off a dose while it is dry. Put a rod in with the rod in hand, fill with a bucket, sneak with an empty hand to take one out.
modular.feedback.desc.part.centrifuge_ro: The rotor of a gas centrifuge. A wider rotor separates at a lower speed but weighs more on the shaft, and its rim holds only as fast as its metal's strength over density allows, less the wider it is; spun past that it tears apart.
modular.feedback.role.centrifuge_rotor.t: The spinning drum. Wider starts at a lower speed and loads the shaft more; a stronger, lighter metal holds a faster rim.
feedback.jei.info.gas_centrifuge: Put it on a shaft. Natural uranium ingots go in by hand (four to a batch), hydrofluoric acid by bucket or pipe (50 mB a batch). Above 24 RPM it spins out a batch: one Enriched Uranium ingot and three Depleted Uranium ingots, faster the faster the shaft turns (by the square). Right-click with an empty hand to take what it made, or to read it.
feedback.jei.info.plutonium_fuel_rod: Plutonium clad in stainless steel: the strongest fuel rod, bred from spent fuel. Plutonium is a toxic heavy metal as well as a radioactive one.
feedback.jei.info.enriched_fuel_rod: Enriched uranium clad in stainless steel: much stronger than a natural Fuel Rod, so a core runs hotter on fewer rods.
feedback.jei.info.breeder_rod: Depleted uranium around thorium. It breeds fissile fuel fast, but only in a hard spectrum: put it where no moderator or flowing coolant touches it.
gui.feedback.computer.text_refused: The text does not compile: nothing was changed
gui.feedback.computer.text_discarded: The text did not compile and was dropped: the program is as it was
gui.feedback.computer.text_printed: A printed card: shown, not editable
gui.feedback.computer.network_none: No endernet upgrade is fitted to this Computer. Fit one bonded to a Data Port to see the far side.
gui.feedback.computer.network_empty: Nothing is linked to the far end.
gui.feedback.computer.network_tune_help: A channel is a number you tune: everything on it shares one bandwidth and hears every message sent on it. A circuit with a resonator separates more channels. An address is how others on the channel pick you out; with none you neither send nor are listed.
gui.feedback.computer.network_need_addre: Give this Computer an address first.
gui.feedback.computer.network_nobody: Nobody else is on this channel.
gui.feedback.computer.network_heard_file: Heard %1$s send %2$s a program of %3$s nodes
gui.feedback.computer.app_hint: Runs while this disk is in a drive.
feedback.programmer.erased: Erased. The program is back in the editor.
feedback.programmer.function_bad: That selection cannot be saved as a function.
feedback.jei.info.memory_board: A program medium of remanent traces: write it at an electric Programmer, then press Erase to bring the program back into the editor and print the next one onto the same board. An Electric Controller and an Electric Programmer take it; a mechanical host takes the Punch Card alone and a Computer takes no board.
feedback.jei.info.usb_port: A socket fitted to a Computer (use it on the block). With one fitted, the Computer's bays take USB Drives as well as Floppy Disks. One per Computer.
feedback.jei.info.floppy_disk: A program medium you can rewrite. Put a printed disk in a Programmer and press Erase: the program comes back into the editor, and Print writes the new one onto the same disk. A blank Floppy Disk is also what an app is researched onto at a Research Table, with the thing the app is about (a spyglass for Scope, a compass for Link Map, a book for Notes, a clock for Converter, redstone for Calculator, a bookshelf for Library, a redstone lamp for Power, a note block for Arcade, paper for Blueprint, a spatial anchor for Network): its app runs on a Computer while the disk is in one of its drives.
feedback.jei.info.usb_drive: A program medium you can rewrite, like a Floppy Disk. Only a Computer with a fitted USB Port takes it; a Controller and a Programmer do not.
feedback.jei.info.function_card: Saves a selection of cards from a Programmer. Hold a blank one, select cards, press Save fn. Hold a saved one and press Stamp to drop its cards into the editor as plain cards with their inputs unwired; Print flattens them into the program. Needs no Controller support: a function is a convenience, not a new kind of card.
feedback.controller.wrong_medium: This block does not take that medium.
feedback.controller.circuit_needed: The program needs the variables this circuit's lattice gives: take the card out first
feedback.jei.info.electric_controller: A Controller powered from a cable, not a shaft. It takes the Memory Board and the Floppy Disk, not a Punch Card or a USB Drive. It runs while the line delivers at least half of what it wants. A circuit in its slot sets the clock and the sensor noise, and a tube on it draws heater power from the line. Riding in a vehicle it is an autopilot host: a program on it reads the flight sensors and drives the vehicle's analog parts through its cards; with no circuit it holds only a few cards, and each element on a circuit seated in it allows more. Its circuit sets the clock and sensor noise as ever, the heater draws from the vehicle's line, and a sculk lattice's extra variables are where a program keeps its waypoints.
feedback.jei.info.electric_programmer: A Programmer that takes the Memory Board and the Floppy Disk. The mechanical Programmer takes the Punch Card only. Erase works on a printed Memory Board or Floppy Disk.
feedback.jei.info.computer: An Electric Programmer and an Electric Controller in one block. Its bays take Floppy Disks, and USB Drives once a USB Port is fitted; never a Punch Card or a Memory Board. Right-click for its desktop: four drive bays and a running slot are icons you drag media onto, your hotbar sits in a dock, widgets show the time, a scope of the running program's first sensor and each drive's memory, and the apps open as windows from the Menu or the icons. Open a drive to Edit it (the node editor opens in its own resizable window), Run it or Eject it; the Monitor shows the running program's variables and sensor readings, Links lists the blocks its cards are linked to, and Settings changes the phosphor color, wallpaper, screen effects and widgets, which are kept on the block. Sneak with an empty hand to take the running medium out. The editor works without power; the program runs only while the cable delivers. Use a circuit on it to fit one; sneak with an empty hand takes the medium out, then the circuit. It sets the clock and sensor noise as for a Controller. A Network App Disk adds the Network app: with an endernet upgrade fitted it lists what is linked to the far end of the pair and flips switches there. The Editor window has a Text view: the program as text (one statement per card, named values, delay(x, 5s), sensor(link, quantity)), edited with completion; Apply takes it when it compiles, and a text that does not compile never changes the program. Riding in a vehicle it is an autopilot host the same way (see the Electric Controller).
gui.feedback.computer.editor_empty: Nothing is open. Pick a drive, then Edit.
gui.feedback.computer.files.hint: Drag a program onto another drive to copy it onto a blank Floppy or USB drive, or onto the trash to erase it. Right-click a drive for more.
gui.feedback.computer.no_blank_there: %s: is not a blank Floppy or USB drive.
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_no_address: Not sent: this Computer has no address
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_no_pair: Not sent: the pair is not carrying
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_no_row: Not sent: that address is no longer listed
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_too_big: Not sent: that program is too big for a packet
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_lost_band: Packet lost: the channel is saturated
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_lost_pay: Packet lost: the port could not pay for the crossing
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_lost_full: Packet lost: the far inbox is full
gui.feedback.computer.log.net_lost_no_ro: Packet lost: no blank medium to land the program on
gui.feedback.computer.notes_hint: Type here. Saved on this Computer.
gui.feedback.computer.group.metal.note: One Qu is a nugget. Molten metal is 16 mB per Qu.
gui.feedback.computer.group.volume.note: 1 mB is a liter. 1000 mB fills a block.
gui.feedback.computer.group.time.note: 20 ticks to the second, 24000 to a day.
gui.feedback.computer.copy_note: Copy needs a blank Floppy or USB drive, alone in another bay.
gui.feedback.computer.no_blank: No blank Floppy or USB drive in another bay.
gui.feedback.computer.icons_note: Icon side applies when the desktop is opened again.
gui.feedback.computer.no_links: Nothing is linked to this Computer.
message.feedback.enchant.no_rite: No rite of this effect stands by the table.
tooltip.feedback.rite: The notes on one attunement. Shelve it in a chiseled bookshelf by an Enchanting Table; it is never used up.
tooltip.feedback.rite.notes.1: Guessed notes: attune up to level 1
tooltip.feedback.rite.notes.2: Rough notes: attune up to level 2
tooltip.feedback.rite.notes.3: Fair notes: attune up to level 3
tooltip.feedback.rite.notes.4: Clean notes: attune up to level 4
tooltip.feedback.rite.notes.5: Exact notes: attune up to level 5
feedback.jei.info.rite: The notes on one attunement. Stand a chiseled bookshelf holding it where a bookshelf would go around an Enchanting Table, and that attunement can be written there; the better the notes, the higher the level. Write one at the Research Table, buy one from a cleric, or find an enchanted book (it becomes a rite).
feedback.jei.info.blank_rite: Paper to write a rite on. Put it in the Research Table's third slot on the Attunements tab and research an attunement.
gui.feedback.enchant.unknown_tip: No rite of this effect stands on a shelf by the table. Shelve one in a chiseled bookshelf where a bookshelf would go.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.siz: Look a creature over until it gives something away.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.exp: Spend a read on one large blow and land it.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.sof: Pick the worn piece under your crosshair and strike through it.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.rea: Watch a creature take aim at you, and be somewhere else when it lets go.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.wro: Hit armor with something softer than it. It will not go well.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.rig: Hit armor with a weapon harder than what it wears, and let it show.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.hot: Finish a fight with a blade or barrel whose edge runs hot.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.spe: Land a hit with a spear while the use key is held.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.arm: Be hit while wearing armor you built, and take less for it.
Take a blow wearing a full outfit of armor you built.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.fir: Cast a technique from any skill tree.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.cas: Use a technique from the Anchor tree. Stand your ground.
Use a technique from the Veil tree. Be elsewhere.
Use a technique from the Brute tree. Put your weight in it.
Use a technique from the Onslaught tree. Keep the rhythm.
Use a technique from the Observation tree. Read first, then act.
Use a technique from the Proficiency tree. Get out of trouble.
Use a technique from the Chaos tree. Leave them with what you did.
advancement.feedback.combat.overrun.desc: Fire a round the chamber was never built to hold.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tongs: Lift or carry something too hot for bare skin, with tongs or gloves between you and it.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.ste: Stand in the steam a weeping boiler seam gives off, and live. The sound comes before the pain.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.bac: Bring a boiler that has started to weep back under its seam line before it lets go.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.rad: Carry a counter or dosimeter through a dose sick enough to make you hungry, and come out the other side.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.overd: Leave a batch in the heat long past done. It is done.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tin.d: Some metal melts in a cooler fire than copper and stays bright. Find it in the ground.
A dense gray ore melts at a fire you can already build. It is soft, and it is poison to handle carelessly.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.brass: Copper takes a second metal and turns the color of gold. Not tin this time.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.glass: Sand melts, if the fire is hot and the vessel holds. What it gives is clear.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.quart: Plain glass softens early. Pure silica holds its shape much hotter, and wants a much hotter fire.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.fireb: Ordinary brick cracks in a hot fire. A particular clay, fired hard, does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.graph: Carbon comes in a form that marks paper and does not burn in a fire you can build.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.lava_: Fire That Does Not Go Out
Some fires need no fuel and have no gap. Set a vessel where one burns.
advancement.feedback.progress.nether.arr: The ground itself is hot here, and there is no water. Go and see what a fire can do with it.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.arri: Mail is not the same as being there. Go to where the port sends.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.void: Nothing grows in the void, but something lives there. Dark and sealed works anywhere.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.l: The deep dark answers to vibration. Set something to hear it, and keep what it heard.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.just_: Raw is no good and black is worse. Take it off at the moment between.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.dried: Water is what spoils food. Take enough of it away and the food outlasts the season.
key.feedback.suit_wheel: Suit ability wheel (hold, release over a segment)
screen.feedback.suit.node.head: Helmet
modular.feedback.role.servo.tip: A winding that drives the piece: the conductor sets how hard it pulls and how much of what it draws is lost as heat.
modular.feedback.role.gauge.tip: A lens over the suit's dials. Without one the suit tells you in words; with one, in figures, finer the clearer the glass.
modular.feedback.role.sensor_head.tip: A bundle of fiber that gives the helmet night sight and thermal sight; more fiber sees further.
modular.feedback.role.battery_bay.tip: A plate cradle in the chest that holds the battery the whole suit runs on.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_drive.tip: Amps the servo winding can carry: the piece's muscle. The suit draws a share of it for each ability.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_loss.tip: The share of what the servo draws that leaves as heat in the suit.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_gauge.tip: How finely the suit's dials read: lower is finer, from the clarity of the lens.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_sense.tip: Cells of fiber in the sensor head.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_bay.tip: Whether the piece holds the suit's battery.
feedback.jei.info.charging_gantry: A frame on an electrical line that charges the battery in the suit of whoever stands in it. Only the floor plate is solid: walk in. It asks for the battery's own charge current while the line is in a band above the battery's own, and a line in a band over the battery's case wears the cells. Wire it like any sink.
feedback.jei.info.vis_tap: A coil on a Thaumaturge vis relay network that gives current. Within reach of a linked relay it draws a little vis every second and keeps five Eu of the buffer for each hundredth of vis (a buffer of four hundred Eu), offering it to a line at its band, two amps at most. With no load the buffer fills and the tap cannot stop what the network pushes at it: the surplus backs up as flux in the chunk. Without Thaumaturge it does nothing.
feedback.jei.info.energy_fitting: The one place another mod's energy meets a line. It takes current from a line at its band or higher, turns four FE out of each Eu and keeps four fifths of that (the rest is lost as heat), and offers it to any touching block that takes FE, or to anything that draws from it. A full buffer stops it asking the line for current, so a load that stops leaves the line unharmed.
feedback.jei.info.charger: A clip on an electrical line. Right click with one battery to put it in, empty-handed to take it out. A battery charges as a placed one does when fed its band or a higher one, wearing if the line is over its case.
feedback.jei.info.exosuit: A powered suit is ordinary modular armor with fittings added at the bench: a servo (a winding part of any conductor, on any piece), a gauge (a lens), a sensor head (fiber, on the helmet) and a battery bay (plate, on the chestplate) that holds the battery everything runs on. Wear the pieces, fit a charged battery in the bay from the suit screen (J), and hold V for the ability wheel: strength, jump and dash (hold B), plating, night sight and thermal sight. Servos make heat; past the limit the suit cuts out until it cools. Each piece also takes one upgrade module, a finished item of its own (see Suit Module): some tune the suit, and a few give the wheel a segment of its own: cloak, jet (hold G), shockwave, scan ping and EMP.
modular.feedback.role.upgrade.tip: A finished suit module, fitted whole. What it is and how strongly it works come from the module itself; it only works while the suit is powered.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_casing: The shell of a suit module. It carries the module's weight and keeps its core off the wearer.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_wiring: The leads that feed a module's attachments. A heavier conductor wastes less of what the module draws and can feed more attachments.
modular.feedback.role.wiring.tip: The leads of a suit module. Its material must conduct: more current means more attachments fed and less of the draw lost as heat.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_wiring.tip: How well the module is wired: heavier conductors waste less of what it draws.
feedback.jei.info.suit_module: A suit module is built at the bench from a casing (plate), wiring (wire) and one to four attachments, each a part of one kind of mechanism: a lens, filter, heat exchanger plate, armor plate, spring, actuator, tread, thruster nozzle, field coil or dosing pump. There is no list of upgrades to pick from: each part has one measurement to set (focal length, bed depth, thickness, stroke, span, bore, core length, dose) that trades two effects, and its material's figures set how hard it works. Support parts held in the module (a circuit, a power cell, a motor) let a part do more: a motor makes a heat plate a pump, a circuit lets it mask the thermal view, a power cell lets a coil pulse. The thruster burns fuel from a bucket in your pack, and the dispenser doses from a potion bottle in it. Heavier wiring feeds more attachments and wastes less. Fit the finished module into a suit piece; taking the piece apart gives the module back whole. Parts that are plain physics (plates, springs, treads, filters) work unpowered; the rest work while the suit is powered. Drawing a suit module takes a treatise on robotics; building one takes its blueprint.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_optic: A lens set in a casing. A short focal length reaches what you look at; a long one reaches further and sharpens the thermal sight. The glass sets how clearly it sees and how much glare it turns back; a flash from a held circuit lights every living thing near. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_optic.tip: An attachment of one kind: a lens. Its focal length and its glass decide what it does. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_filter: A cartridge of loose, open media packed in a housing, such as charcoal: the lighter it packs, the more surface the air crosses. A thin bed passes the air easily and the breath lasts longer; a deep bed cleans it, and poison, nausea and hunger are cleared as they land, at a small draw. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_filter.tip: An attachment of one kind: a filter cartridge. Its bed depth and its media decide what it does. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_therma: A conductive plate or fin set bolted between the suit and the air. A thin one spreads the suit's heat to the air and sheds it faster; a thick one holds the cold and fire off the wearer, so fire hurts less and frost does not settle. The better the metal conducts heat, the harder it works, and it needs no power. With a motor held in the module it is a pump: the wheel can vent most of the suit's heat at once. With a circuit held it can follow the ambient: switch it on and a thermal view sees the wearer at the temperature of the air, at a steady draw.
modular.feedback.role.module_thermal.tip: An attachment of one kind: a heat exchanger plate. Its thickness decides whether it sheds heat or shields. A held motor makes it a pump, a held circuit a thermal mask. A coolant in a carried fluid container runs through a thin plate and carries off more heat; some of it is used up with every bit of heat it takes. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_platin: An armored insert for a suit piece, read off its material's hardness and toughness. A thin plate turns a shot, an arrow or a thrown thing aside; a thick one soaks a blast, takes a blow without moving you, and, run down the leg, is a frame that carries a pack's weight to the ground. A harder, tougher metal works better. It needs no power.
modular.feedback.role.module_plating.tip: An attachment of one kind: an armored insert. Its thickness decides whether it turns shots or takes blasts and blows. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_actuat: A linear actuator on a leg or heel, driven by a held motor. A short stroke strides fast, a long one lifts the foot over a step; the bore it is cut to sets how hard it pushes. A heel ram can strike from the wheel. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_actuator.ti: An attachment of one kind: a piston on a held motor. Its stroke and its bore decide what it does. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_spring: A coiled or bent spring for a leg. A short stroke is stiff and throws the jump; a long one is soft and takes the landing, handing a hard one back to the ground. A stiffer material works harder. It needs no power.
modular.feedback.role.module_spring.tip: An attachment of one kind: a leg spring. Its stroke decides whether it kicks or cushions. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_tread: A pad for the sole or the shin. A narrow pad bites the ground and keeps the footing on slow surfaces; a wide one pushes water like a fin. The stickier its material, the better it works. It needs no power.
modular.feedback.role.module_tread.tip: An attachment of one kind: a pad. Its span decides whether it grips or paddles. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_thrust: A nozzle that burns fuel carried on the body, as the thruster block does: it draws the fuel from a bucket or other fluid container in your pack, whatever burns, and the hotter the flame the harder it pushes. Hold the jet key to lift, or fire a single burst along your look from the wheel. A wide bore pushes harder and burns fuel faster; the nozzle's metal must stand the flame, so a higher melting point works better. It burns in air or on the oxygen the fuel carries, so it gives nothing in thin air with a plain fuel, and nothing when the pack holds none.
modular.feedback.role.module_thruster.ti: An attachment of one kind: a thrust nozzle. Its bore decides how hard it pushes and how much it burns. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_coil: A core with a coil wound round it: an electromagnet. Switched on at the wheel it pulls dropped magnetic things (iron, steel, anything the material says is magnetic) in to you; a long core reaches farther, a short one pulls harder. A ferromagnetic core carries the field; any other is weak. With a power cell held in the module as its capacitor, the wheel can dump the field as a pulse that slows, weakens and blinds the creatures near you, and makes them lose you. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_coil.tip: An attachment of one kind: a field coil on a core. Its core length decides whether it reaches or pulls hard. A held power cell lets it pulse; a charged Leyden jar on a handle carried in the pack is dumped into the pulse and makes it stronger. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.role.controller.tip: A circuit the module is run by. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a faster, quieter circuit makes them work harder. Read off the circuit itself.
modular.feedback.role.cell.tip: A battery the module carries for itself. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a bigger cell makes them work harder.
modular.feedback.role.motor.tip: A motor or dynamo built into the module. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a higher-rated one makes them work harder.
message.feedback.plan.measured: You measure it as you take it apart: the paper becomes a blueprint.
feedback.jei.info.blueprint_book: Holds blueprints like a bundle. Click a blueprint onto it to put it in, click it on an empty slot to take one out. A bench that wants a blueprint reads the blueprints in a book in its blueprint slot.
item.feedback.treatise_weapons_1: Weapons Treatise I: Blades and Heads
item.feedback.treatise_mechanical_1: Mechanical Treatise I: Engines, Flywheels and Dynamotors
item.feedback.treatise_chemical_2: Chemical Treatise II: Heat and Compression
item.feedback.treatise_materials_2: Materials Treatise II: Metallurgy and Heat Treatment
item.feedback.treatise_electrical_1: Electrical Treatise I: Cells and Static Charge
item.feedback.treatise_electrical_2: Electrical Treatise II: Coils and Magnets
item.feedback.treatise_nuclear_1: Nuclear Treatise I: Reactors and Fuel
item.feedback.treatise_experience_1: Experience Treatise I: Orbs and Vessels
tooltip.feedback.treatise_age: Its specimen is the work of the %s.
tooltip.feedback.treatise: Hold it, in a binder or on a shelf against a Blueprint Table, to draw blueprints of the types below. Each volume is its own subject.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.no_trea: Drawing this takes %s: carry it, in a binder, or keep it on a shelf against the table.
message.feedback.treatise.written: Taking it apart, you write down what you learn: %s.
feedback.jei.info.treatise_binder: Holds treatises like a bundle; click a treatise onto it to put it in. The Blueprint Table counts the treatises inside as held.
feedback.jei.info.treatise_shelf: A shelf for treatises and binders. Put it against a Blueprint Table: what it holds counts as held by whoever draws there.
feedback.jei.info.blank_treatise: Take a machine, gun or powered-suit module apart at a bench with this in the blueprint slot and it becomes the volume of that school's treatise the item belongs to. A volume lets the Blueprint Table draw blueprints of the types it covers.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.cannot_: Put a blueprint in the left slot and blank paper in the right to copy it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_rod: A plain rod: the baseline current and the baseline life.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_plat: A broad plate: 60% more current, but it lasts 56% less long.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_bloc: A thick block: 20% less current, but it lasts about 2.4 times as long.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_bar: A straight bar: the baseline pull and the baseline reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_horse: Bent so both poles face the work: 40% more pull, 30% less reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_pot: Wrapped round the coil: 80% more pull, but half the reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_shor: A short arm: 30% less lever, but it spins 40% faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_stra: A plain arm: the baseline lever and the baseline speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_long: A long arm: 40% more lever, but 25% slower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_offs: A jogged arm: 30% more lever for only 10% less speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.filament_c: A coiled wire: the baseline current and the baseline toughness.
A baked carbon thread: draws 40% more and burns out only at a 30% bigger packet.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.filament_f: A hair-thin wire: draws 40% less, and burns out at a 20% smaller packet.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flywheel_s: Spokes to a rim: 40% less momentum, and the rim bursts at 20% fewer RPM.
A full disc: the baseline mass and the baseline rim strain.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flywheel_r: A heavy rim on a web: 30% more momentum, but the rim bursts at 10% fewer RPM.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_c: Vanes flung outward: the baseline flow and the baseline lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_a: A propeller in the pipe: 60% more flow and 60% more load to turn, but half the lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_s: A screw in a barrel: 30% less flow and load, but 60% more lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_flat: A flat sheet of glass: 30% less area, and half the leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_lined: A foil-lined jar: the baseline area and the baseline leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_rolled: Glass and foil rolled up tight: 50% more area, but 50% more leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_rin: A ring of ports: the baseline burn and the baseline flame.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_jet: A single hard jet: burns 50% more fuel, and the flame is 8% hotter.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_wic: A wick fed by capillary: burns 40% less fuel, and the flame is 8% cooler.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.plate_fram: Plates stacked in a frame: moves twice the heat of plain tubes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_scre: Meshed screws: 30% more flow, 40% less heating, 20% more load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_sing: One rotor: the baseline flow, the baseline heating and the baseline load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_twin: Two rotors in stages: 80% more flow, 20% less heating, 70% more load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_fire: Flame passes through tubes in the water: the baseline pressure rating, 20% less room for water.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_flat: A flat box: holds only 35% of the pressure of a fire-tube shell, but has the most room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_wate: Water runs through tubes in the flame: 40% more rating than a fire-tube shell, 30% less room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_slab: A low slab: leaks 30% more heat and holds 20% less of it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_towe: A tall tower: leaks 30% less heat and holds 30% more of it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_wall: A plain walled block: the baseline leak and the baseline mass.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_box: A flat-sided box: holds only 35% of a cylinder's pressure, but has the most room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_capsu: A cylinder with domed ends: 40% more rating than a cylinder, but 12% less room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_cylin: A plain cylinder: the baseline pressure rating, with 20% less room than a box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_spher: A sphere carries load evenly: twice the rating of a cylinder, but only about half the room of a box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tubes_coil: Tubes wound into a coil: moves 30% more heat than plain tubes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tubes_plai: Bare straight tubes: the baseline heat moved.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_buck: Buckets that hold the water: 50% more power, but 30% slower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_padd: Flat paddles in the stream: 30% less power, but 40% faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_slat: Slatted blades: the baseline power and the baseline speed.
modular.feedback.role.core.tip: The core the winding is wound on. Its material sets the core loss: the share of the power through it that turns to heat.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.cramped: While you crouch, your movement is %1$s%% of normal. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.crown_lever: Knockback on you is %1$s%% of its strength while this is worn on the head. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.leg_drag: Sprinting costs %1$s extra exhaustion a tick, and in water you move at %2$s%% of normal speed. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.shaft_seal: Powder snow does not freeze you, but in water you move at %1$s%% of normal speed. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.cushion_sole: Fall damage is %1$s%% of what it would be. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.fig.pierce_resist.tip: Share of arrow and bolt damage the piece turns aside, from the plate's competence, its cover and how its shape meets a point. Worn pieces add by slot: chest most, boots least.
modular.feedback.fig.fire_conduct.tip: How readily the plate carries fire's heat in to the wearer: the material's thermal conductivity times the plate's volume. Metal conducts, cloth and leather do not. Burning or standing in lava, each worn piece heats and the wearer takes extra heat damage.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.title: Title this blueprint
modular.feedback.axis.width.tip: How wide the part is across. A wider one covers more and hits with more of its face, and takes more stock and weighs more.
modular.feedback.axis.torso_length.tip: How far down the body the plate runs. Longer covers more and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.face_opening.tip: How much of the face the helmet leaves open. Wider sees better and guards less.
modular.feedback.axis.crown.tip: How tall the helmet rises over the head. Taller takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.length.tip: How long the part runs. A longer one reaches or covers further, and takes more stock and weighs more.
modular.feedback.axis.shaft.tip: How high the boot rises up the leg. Higher covers more and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.sole.tip: How thick the sole is under the foot. Thicker wears longer and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.thickness.tip: How thick the part is. A thick one resists chipping and weighs more; a thin one bites deeper and is quicker.
modular.feedback.axis.head_size.tip: How big the head is. A big head weighs more, so it hits harder and swings slower; a small one is quick to swing and to throw.
modular.feedback.axis.edge_length.tip: How long the working edge, face or point is. A longer one takes more stock and weight for the work it spans.
modular.feedback.axis.face_size.tip: How big the shield's face is. A large face guards more and weighs more and slows you; a small one is quick and parries.
modular.feedback.axis.prod_length.tip: How long the crossbow's prod is. A long prod draws very heavy and hits hard but loads slowly; a short one loads fast and shoots light.
modular.feedback.axis.limb_length.tip: How long the bow's limbs are. Long limbs draw heavy and shoot fast but slow; short limbs draw quick and shoot light.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.curved: Like a sword blade, but forged with a bend along its length in a run of taps and heavy blows. It cuts on the draw and hits a little harder, and carries a dash.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tapered: Like a sword blade, but drawn down to a point in a run of taps. Light, with its mass near the hand and the best reach for its length; it hits lightly and the fine edge chips. Quick thrusts build into a flurry.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.skinning: Like a knife blade, but belly-curved and thin at the edge. A little lighter; it is made for hides and carcasses. Livestock and wildlife take more from it and drop a second helping more often; monsters take a little less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.utility: Like a knife blade, but thin and straight. Light, with a longer reach for its size; it hits lightly and the fine edge chips. Quick cuts build into a flurry.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tanto: Like a knife blade, but thick through the point. Heavier and a little shorter; it hits harder, and the point goes through part of a target's armor and slows it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.serrated: Like a sword blade, but with teeth ground along the edge in a run of heavy blows. It saws through the unarmored and hits hard, but turns on armor.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fullered: Like a sword blade, but with a groove ground down its length in taps and heavy blows. Lighter for its stiffness and a little quicker, with a slightly weaker edge.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.leaf: Like a sword blade, but swelling toward the tip in a run of taps. Its weight sits forward, so it hits well, and it sweeps a crowd with a flourish.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heater: Like a shield face, but a flat top tapering to a point: five lengths of stock. Lighter than a round face of the same size.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rectangula: Like a shield face, but a square-cornered slab: eight lengths of stock. Holds a fifth more, and the corners are weight to carry.
message.feedback.electric_gun.too_big: This receiver takes a battery of at most %s cells.
tooltip.feedback.electric_gun.no_cell: No battery. Click the gun with one to load it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spring_gun_ba: The tube a spring gun's pellet runs down. A longer barrel keeps the piston's push longer; a wider bore cuts a heavier pellet from each nugget and wastes more of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spring_gun_re: The body a spring gun's barrel, piston and spring are fixed to. It is what the spring is rated against: a spring stronger than the receiver holds takes a set each time it is cocked.
modular.feedback.role.piston.tip: The small metal plunger the spring drives. It moves with the pellet, so a heavy piston takes a share of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_standa: One cell of stock, an 8 mm bore: pellets of middling weight, a few dozen to a nugget.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_pellet: One cell of stock, a 5 mm bore: tiny pellets, many to a nugget, and little of the spring's energy is wasted. Each pellet hits lightly.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_slug: Two cells of stock, a 12 mm bore: a heavy slug, only a few to a nugget, that hits hard, but the wide bore wastes much of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.axis.barrel_length.tip: How long the barrel is. A longer barrel keeps the piston's push going and shoots truer, and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.fig.spring_energy.tip: What the cocked spring stores: its volume times the stiffness of its metal.
modular.feedback.fig.air_efficiency.tip: The share of the spring's energy that reaches the pellet. A longer barrel keeps more; a wider bore wastes more.
modular.feedback.fig.draw.tip.air_gun: Ticks to cock the spring by hand, for a wielder of ordinary strength. A stiffer or bigger spring takes longer.
modular.feedback.fig.velocity.tip.air_gu: Muzzle speed of an iron pellet of this bore, against a vanilla bow's arrow.
