modular.feedback.fig.joint.tip.air_gun: The spring's energy over what the receiver holds. Over 1 the spring takes a set each time it is cocked; far over, it snaps.
cartridge.feedback.rocket: A rocket: %s grain burns in flight. The tube only ejects it.
cartridge.feedback.shell: A shell: no powder. A launcher's seat drives it.
feedback.jei.info.launcher: A launcher drives a shell with work stored in its seat. The reload key loads a round of the bore with no powder in it, then cocks the spring: the time is the spring's energy over your strength. Left click fires. A denser shell hits harder. The spring's stored energy is its volume times its metal's stiffness; a longer barrel keeps more of it and a lighter piston wastes less. A spring stronger than the receiver is rated for takes a set each cocking, and far past it snaps and hurts you. The release is nearly silent.
modular.feedback.desc.part.electric_gun_: The barrel of a pulse gun, a tube the pulse is guided down. Its length sets how far the pulse holds its damage; its bore, how wide it runs. A conductor takes energy out of the pulse and turns it to heat, so the best barrel is one that hardly conducts.
modular.feedback.desc.part.pulse_seat: The battery seat of a pulse gun, set inside the receiver: a frame of contact bars and a bank of capacitors, the conductor, packed in a dielectric. Its shape is the gun's heat cycle; its conductor is the ceiling on the energy of one pulse; the dielectric sets what a capacitor bank holds; its power tier takes Light, Standard or Heavy of that ceiling.
modular.feedback.role.seat.tip: Where the battery meets the barrel. The shape of the seat is how the gun fires and cools; the conductor of the seat caps what one pulse can hold, and the power tier (Light, Standard, Heavy) is how much of that cap a shot takes, at the cost of more heat, recharge, drain, recoil and strain. Banks and flywheels need a long gun or machine gun frame. A thermopile's two metals are the conductor and the dielectric slot.
modular.feedback.desc.part.heat_governor: A heat governor for a pulse gun, clipped to the receiver with a bimetal strip or a thermistor bead pressed against the barrel and a relay in the firing circuit. The strip curls as the barrel heats and the relay follows it. A strip of poor heat conductor lags the barrel, so the governor acts late.
modular.feedback.role.heat_governor.tip: One governor on the receiver (a throttle, a forced vent, a dead-man cutoff or a surge shunt), a strip against the barrel working a relay. With none, a shot at the heat limit burns you and wears the barrel. A throttle never lets the gun reach that limit; a forced vent locks out for longer the further over it ran and scalds whatever stands in its steam, you and friends too; a dead-man cutoff holds fire until the barrel has cooled; a surge shunt, closed on the reload key, doubles the rate of fire for a window and then locks the gun until the barrel is back under the limit. The strip's material is how fast it follows the barrel: a poor conductor reads low, the throttle slows late and a cutoff can let a shot through past the limit, which burns you.
modular.feedback.desc.part.hold_trigger: A long-travel trigger lever on a leaf spring. While it is held down it keeps a charging switch closed on the seat's capacitor, and the pulse goes when the lever is let go. For a pulse gun whose seat fires one shot a pull: a cylinder, a capacitor bank or a burst bank.
modular.feedback.role.hold_charge.tip: A spring-loaded lever that keeps the charging switch closed. Hold to build a stronger shot that goes through more; let go early for an ordinary one. Only a seat that fires one shot a pull takes it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.pump_charge: A pump lever geared by a rack and a ratchet pawl to a small hand magneto, whose winding tops up the seat's capacitor with every stroke. The pawl lets it turn one way only. For a pulse gun whose seat fires one shot a pull.
modular.feedback.role.pump_charge.tip: A lever on a rack and a ratchet turning a magneto that tops up the seat. Press the pump key to pump. Each of the first two pumps widens and strengthens the next shot, and a beam splitter throws more beams; the third arms a blast that replaces the shot, hurting everything close and you. Only a seat that fires one shot a pull takes it. The reload key works one fitting, so no hold charge, surge shunt or shock lead beside it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.beam_lens: A fitting for the muzzle of a pulse gun, a housing round a glass lens or a pair of spark-gap electrodes: a splitter's cut facets share one pulse among several beams, a fork's electrodes ionise a path in the air that the shock follows to the nearest body.
modular.feedback.role.beam_lens.tip: One lens on the muzzle. A beam splitter turns a pulse into three, five or seven weaker beams in a spread, strongest up close. An arc fork carries a hit on to the nearest conductive body, then any; fired in water it shocks everything wet in reach, you included unless you are insulated. A coherence lens bounces the pulse off what it strikes and sets off projectiles it crosses. A malefic lens stops the pulse at the first thing it meets and blows there.
modular.feedback.desc.part.zoom_coil: A solenoid on the rail of a pulse gun: a winding of wire round an iron core that builds a magnetic field while the sight is held up. The field pulls the pulse into a tighter beam. A better conductor in the winding builds a stronger field.
modular.feedback.role.zoom_charge.tip: A solenoid on the rail. Zoom builds while you aim: the shot tightens and the pulse holds its damage further. It starts over after each shot. A winding of a better conductor builds more of both; a poor one builds half.
modular.feedback.desc.part.heat_gauge: A thermistor bead pressed on the barrel, wired to a moving-coil needle meter in a plate case: a needle on the gun and a finer heat bar on the HUD.
modular.feedback.role.heat_gauge.tip: A thermistor against the barrel feeding a moving-coil meter: a needle on the gun that swings with the barrel's heat, and a finer heat bar with a scale on the HUD.
modular.feedback.role.battery_fitting.ti: A cradle for a battery in the pack's row of fittings: one slot that takes only a battery. A tethered pulse gun draws from it. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cylinder: Three cells of stock: six small capacitors that trickle-charge from the battery. Each shot spends one and the drum turns; the wait for the next is a capacitor filling. A faster battery and a better conductor fill them sooner. Single shots.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flux_cycle: Two cells of stock with fins: the heat dump bus. There is no capacitor to wait for; every shot draws from the battery and the heat goes into the barrel, which limits how long fire can be held. Automatic and single.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.capacitor_: Four cells of stock: every capacitor discharges at once into one very large pulse that goes through every body in line, then a long recharge that grows with the tier and the cells in the battery. The dielectric between the plates sets what the bank holds. Needs a long gun or machine gun frame. Single shots.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_breec: Four cells of stock: one very large shot of slow heat, then the cores are too hot to fire until the gun has broken itself open and vented, which it does after every shot. Needs a long gun or machine gun frame. Single shots.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.burst_bank: Four cells of stock: a bank spent as a fixed burst of three shots, then recharged. Needs a long gun or machine gun frame. Burst and single shots.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flywheel: Three cells of stock: a wheel on a generator that spins up while the trigger is held, so the first shot waits, and spins down quickly after. A denser wheel holds more and spins up slower. The sound rises with the spin. Needs a long gun or machine gun frame. Automatic and single.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.recoil_dyn: Two cells of stock: a small coil and magnet that the recoil drives through each other, returning a tenth of each shot's energy to the cells. Automatic, single and burst.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fire_rate_: A bimetal strip curls with the barrel's heat and pinches the firing relay's timing, so the rate of fire falls smoothly as the barrel heats, to 40% at the limit, and the gun never reaches the limit that burns.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.forced_ven: Two cells of stock: a bimetal strip lifts a spring-loaded poppet valve at the heat limit. The gun locks out, for longer the further over it ran, and lets go a cloud of steam in front that scalds whatever stays in it for about a second, the wielder and friends too.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dead_man_c: A thermistor bead against the barrel opens a latching relay on barrel heat alone, and holds it open until the barrel has cooled.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.beam_split: Two cells of stock: a ring of cut glass facets in a housing, each facet taking a share of the pulse. One pulse into three, five or seven weaker beams in a spread, strongest up close.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.arc_fork: Two cells of stock: a pair of spark-gap electrodes that ionise the air in front of the muzzle, a path a gas-discharge tube would carry the current down. The shock of a hit arcs to the nearest conductive body within reach, then to any. Fired wet it hurts everything wet in reach.
modular.feedback.axis.tier.tip: Light, Standard or Heavy: how much of the seat's conductor ceiling a pulse takes. Heavier pulses go through more bodies and hold their damage further, and cost more heat, recharge, battery, recoil and strain.
modular.feedback.axis.beams.tip: How many beams the splitter makes: three, five or seven. More beams are weaker each and wider.
modular.feedback.fig.shot_energy.tip: What an ordinary pulse takes from the battery: the seat's ceiling, times its tier and what the seat does to it.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.fault.p: A capacitor bank, a burst bank and a flywheel need a long gun or machine gun frame.
A hold-charge trigger and a pump charge need a seat that fires one shot a pull: a cylinder, a capacitor bank or a burst bank.
tooltip.feedback.electric_gun.tether: No battery in the gun. The tether lead draws from a battery in a pack's battery fitting or a suit's bay.
feedback.jei.info.electric_gun: A pulse gun: a pulse of electrical energy, no bullet. Load a battery by clicking the gun with it in your inventory, and take it out with an empty cursor; charge it at a Charger. The seat sets the heat cycle (cylinder, flux cycler, capacitor bank, burst bank, flywheel, recoil dynamo or pack tether) and the power tier; the barrel should hardly conduct, or it takes energy out of the pulse and heats. A pulse is instant, holds its damage out to a range that grows with the barrel and the tier, goes through a few bodies and through glass, and shocks the wet and the metal-armored harder. A shot at the heat limit burns you and wears the barrel unless a heat governor is fitted. Firing wet arcs to you; only insulating gear stops it.
modular.feedback.axis.bore.tip: How wide the bore runs. A wide bore delivers a little more of the pulse in a wider cone; a narrow one tightens the beam.
modular.feedback.axis.tines.tip: How many points the head splits into. More tines spread the thrust: a wider cone that can catch several things at once, but each point is thinner, so it pierces armor less and every blow is a little weaker.
modular.feedback.axis.barb.tip: How hard the head resists being withdrawn. A barbed hit pulls the target toward you and tears the wound, so a pulled target takes more damage, and the weapon is held up while you work it free. On a thrown head with a lanyard, the barb is what wounds the target you reel in.
modular.feedback.axis.zoom.tip: How far the scope closes the view in. A stronger scope narrows the field and takes longer to find a target in; the lens loses a little of the light it passes.
gui.feedback.bench.slot_hint: A second material in the same part: it is set in the stock slot beside the first, and the part is made of both.
modular.feedback.role.thermal_fitting.ti: A live circuit clipped onto the scope's mount. It is a finished item of its own and comes off whole.
modular.feedback.role.fire_control.tip: A live circuit clipped onto the receiver. It reads the shot: a quiet one tightens the group, its gain lengthens the rangefinder, and the gun card shows range, lead and drop to what the crosshair is on. A tube on a gun has no heater, so it reads cold: slower and noisier, never refused. With no circuit the gun shoots as it was built.
modular.feedback.role.fuse_control.tip: A live circuit clipped onto the launcher. Sneak and press the fire-mode key to switch what fuses the round: its own, proximity, a short count or a long count. Proximity senses wider with the circuit gain and a little off with its noise; the counts are steps of the circuit clock, so a slow circuit gives a long fuse. With no circuit the round keeps the fuse it was pressed with.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.jacket_dampi: The jacket stores the barrel's vibration: %1$s%% tighter while the barrel is cold, worse than bare once it is hot.
modular.feedback.slot.head: Head
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.egun.sink: Sink holds %s%% of a copper kilo
modular.feedback.desc.part.shears_blade: The cutting part of a pair of shears: two blades on a pivot, or one bent bar that springs open. Its length sets the bite.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pivot_scis: Two blades crossed on a pin. It bears as much as the pin through it does and snaps at an ordinary pace; with no pin it hardly holds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.spring_bow: One bar bent on itself, springing open after every snap: quick, but it bears little and tires soon.
feedback.jei.info.shears: Shear sheep and cut cobweb, leaves, wool and vines. The blade's length takes a bigger bite of wool and leaves and reaches further, but loses the control that cobweb and vines want. A spring bow snaps quickly and bears little; a pivot scissor bears what its pin does, the weaker of pin and blade.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flat_tip: A blade ground square across: it turns a slotted screw and, with some slipping, a bolt head.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cross_tip: Four wings that center in a screw's cross; it rounds a bolt's head.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.hex_tip: Six flats that grip a bolt's head square; it slips in a screw's slot.
modular.feedback.axis.shank.tip: How long the shank is between the grip and the tip. A longer one reaches the seat square and starts the fastener truer, but twists under load and wears faster; a short one is stiff and lasts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.bastard_cu: Coarse teeth: two grains off a stroke, and a stroke leaves tool marks that, left unpolished, weaken the part.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.second_cut: Medium teeth: a grain a stroke and few marks.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.smooth_cut: Fine teeth: half a grain a stroke, and each stroke burnishes the marks of a coarser file away.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.short_spoo: An ordinary spoon bowl on a short handle: stirs and skims as well as each other.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ladle: A big bowl on a long reach: it lifts more and keeps the hand off a hotter pot, but is clumsy at stirring.
modular.feedback.axis.depth.tip: How deep the bowl is. A deep bowl holds what it lifts and skims more; a shallow one stirs the pot better. A deeper bowl takes more stock.
modular.feedback.desc.part.bed_mattress: The cover, padding and shell of a bed. Two cells rolled up as a bedroll, three flat as a mattress. Add a fibrous padding and a leather shell.
modular.feedback.desc.part.bed_frame: The frame a mattress lies on, off the cold ground. Four cells as a bedstead, three as a cot. It weighs, so a bed with a frame does not go on a pack.
modular.feedback.role.mattress.tip: What you lie on: cover, padding and shell. Softer padding gives more comfort, and padding that passes less heat keeps you warm.
modular.feedback.role.bed_frame.tip: Lifts the mattress off the ground: more comfort and warmth, and the weight of the frame. Leave it off and the bed is a bedroll.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.bedroll: The mattress rolled: two cells, light, a little less comfortable. Built with no frame it can be lashed on a pack.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.mattress: The mattress laid flat: three cells, thicker, so softer and warmer, and heavier to carry.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.bedstead: A tall frame that lifts the sleeper well off the ground.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cot: A low light frame: it lifts the sleeper a little and weighs little.
message.feedback.bed.worn_out: This bed is worn through; take it up and rework it.
message.feedback.bed.no_sleep: You can only bed down on firm ground at night or in a storm.
message.feedback.bed.not_safe: You cannot rest with monsters nearby.
feedback.jei.info.bed: A bed built with a frame is set down as a two-block bed: sleep in it at night like any bed, it skips the night and sets your respawn point, and it keeps its parts and materials when you break it and pick it up. You wake healed by its comfort (the softness of padding and cover, the thickness of the mattress, the frame's lift off the ground), less in cold country by how little its padding keeps the heat in. Each night wears it. Built with no frame it is a bedroll, not placed: use it from the hand on firm ground at night, or in a storm, with nothing hostile near, and it skips to morning wherever you are; it is light enough to lash on a pack. Fill the padding with anything fibrous: wool, hide, or the lightest and warmest, feather down.
modular.feedback.fig.warmth.tip: How little heat the bed passes: padding that insulates, thick, lifted off the cold ground. In cold country, comfort is scaled by it.
modular.feedback.fig.clip.tip: How fast the shears take wool and leaves: a quicker snap and a longer blade.
modular.feedback.fig.clip_fine.tip: How fast the shears take cobweb and vines: a quicker snap, held back by a long blade's lack of control.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crock: A deep lidded pot of clay: it holds more than a bowl and its lid keeps the soup in, so a stew stays moist and does not slop.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shish_skew: A long skewer: room for a full run of meat and vegetables.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.satay_stic: A short thin stick: a bite or two of meat, quick to cook.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_dispen: A metered pump and nozzle that doses the wearer from a bottle of brewed potion carried in the pack: it takes the first live one and gives the effect drinking it would, then the empty bottle comes back. A small dose lasts a short while; a large one lasts longer. A metal that resists corrosion keeps the dose clean. It draws a little charge, and has nothing to give when the pack holds no potion.
modular.feedback.role.module_dispenser.t: An attachment of one kind: a dosing pump. The dose axis sets how long the effect it gives lasts. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_pad: the mattress is softer: a night's rest heals more.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_snug: the frame holds you snug: a night's rest heals more.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_slip: the frame lets you slide about: a night's rest heals less.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_warm: the bed keeps more heat in: more warmth against cold country, and it thaws frost sooner.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_cool: the bed lets heat out: less warmth, but waking puts out fire on you and leaves you fire resistant a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_echo: a night's rest heals more, as if the rest were heard twice.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_gamble: a night's rest heals double or nothing.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_fortun: a night in the bed sometimes leaves it unworn.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_feed: you wake with more food points.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_drain: you wake with fewer food points.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_mend: what you wear is repaired while you sleep.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_tithe: waking drops experience for the wear the night took.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_swift: you wake quicker on your feet for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_brace: you wake with resistance to blows for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_douse: waking puts out fire on you and leaves you fire resistant a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_pulse: your weight on the frame charges a battery or Leyden jar beside the bed when you wake.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_draw: items lying near are drawn to you as you wake.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_fling: items lying near are flung away as you wake.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_launch: waking throws you up off the bed.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bayonet_pa: the bayonet thrust does less damage.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pulse_bank: the electric gun's seat holds a bigger pulse.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.blast_arc: when the charge goes off, everything the blast reaches takes an electric shock.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.blast_shov: the blast throws what it reaches away from it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.blast_pull: Casing draws in with the blast (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.blast_pull: the blast pulls what it reaches toward it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.blast_hold: the casing holds the gas in longer: the blast is stronger.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.xp_bank: the vial holds more experience, like a capacitor's plates around the same store.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_grow: eaten, you regenerate for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_reap: eaten, you grow hungry for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_slick: eaten, it slips by: less saturation.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_echo: eaten, the effects you have run longer.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_lag: eaten, the effects you have run shorter.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_edge: eaten, you hit harder for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_pad: eaten, you take on a padding of absorption.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_grudg: eaten, you dig faster for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_calm: eaten, it settles the stomach: poison, nausea, weakness and hunger leave you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_draw: eaten, items lying near are drawn to you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_fling: eaten, items lying near are flung away.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_taunt: eaten, hostile creatures near turn on you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_swift: eaten, you run faster for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_brace: eaten, you take less from blows for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_share: eaten, players near you are fed too.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_alone: eaten with no other player near, it fills more food points.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_pulse: eaten, a battery or Leyden jar beside you is charged.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_ring: eaten, it rings out and wandering hostiles come to see.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_sprin: eaten, you jump higher for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_gambl: eaten, it fills more food points half the time.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_fortu: eaten, it sometimes fills more food points.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_charge: waking leaves static in the bed: every Charge tool you carry takes some charge.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_ground: waking, the bed earths you: every Charge tool you carry bleeds some of its charge.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_stick: a placed bed slows the hostile creatures beside it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_slick: a placed bed throws the hostile creatures beside it off.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_pack: a night's rest heals more for each ally near the bed (team, tamed by you, or a guardian of the village).
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_lone: a night's rest heals more when no ally is near the bed.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_recall: a placed bed with a magnetic recall part returns to your inventory when you break it, instead of dropping.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_anchor: a placed bed is slow to pull up.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_dim: after waking, hostile mobs beyond a short range do not take you up as a target while you stand in low light, for a while.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_keen: a placed bed cuts the hostile creatures beside it, and sleeps harder (less comfort).
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_damp: a placed bed takes a share off the fall of whatever lands on it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_pull: a placed bed draws the hostile creatures beside it toward itself.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bed_lag: a night's rest heals in parts, a second apart, instead of at once.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_sense: eaten, tells you in words how heavy the meal was.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_intac: eaten, the dish sometimes stays in your hand uneaten.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_hold: the food in it rots more slowly (a tight grip keeps it from coming apart).
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_slip: the food in it rots faster (the loose fit lets it work loose).
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_shove: eaten, hostile creatures near you are thrown back.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.meal_pull: eaten, hostile creatures near you are drawn in.
feedback.jei.material.specific_heat.tip: Work to warm one Mu of it by one Tu. High means it soaks up a lot of heat before it gets hot.
feedback.jei.material.latent_fusion.tip: Work to melt one Mu at its melting point, with no change in temperature.
feedback.jei.material.latent_vaporisatio: Work to boil one Mu at its boiling point, with no change in temperature.
feedback.jei.material.ph.tip: Which way a water solution leans: under 7 an acid, over 7 a base. A battery takes any ion-carrying liquid its plates are not eaten by.
feedback.jei.material.corrosivity.tip: How hard it burns flesh and eats metal on contact: how far its pH is from neutral. 0 is neutral; a strong acid or a strong base is about 7.
feedback.jei.material.toxicity.tip: How harmful it is swallowed: a log scale of the real lethal dose. 0 is harmless; each step is ten times deadlier.
feedback.jei.material.shear_thickening.t: How much thicker it gets the faster it is pushed. A pump turned fast on it moves less and labors.
Work to warm one Mu by one Tu.
Work to melt one Mu; the temperature holds while it does.
screen.feedback.probe.row.latent_vaporis: Work to boil one Mu; the temperature holds while it does.
screen.feedback.probe.row.ph.tip: Under 7 an acid, over 7 a base.
screen.feedback.probe.row.corrosivity.ti: On contact: how far its pH is from neutral. A strong acid or base is about 7.
screen.feedback.probe.row.toxicity.tip: Swallowed: a log scale of the real lethal dose, each step ten times deadlier.
screen.feedback.probe.row.shear_thickeni: Pushed fast it stiffens by this much.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coherence_: Three cells of stock: a tube lined with polished mirror and a focusing stack that keeps a pulse coherent enough to bounce. The pulse bounces off what it strikes, keeping the share the struck surface reflects: metal blocks and polished stone keep a lot, dark stone and dirt almost nothing, so a wall of dirt ends the beam. The lining's own reflectivity sets how many bounces it survives, and a held charge buys more. A beam that crosses a projectile in flight, an arrow or a fireball, sets it off where it is.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.malefic_le: Three cells of stock: a tight focusing stack that dumps the whole pulse into one spot. The first body or block it meets flash-boils and blows, and the beam goes no further; the blast's reach and hit come from the energy that went in, more against a wet or metal-armored body. Blocks break by the world's rules. Stand inside the blast and you take it too, capped at three quarters of your health.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.laser_rod: Three cells of stock: a rod of a stuff that lases, ground flat at both ends and set in a steel housing. Chromium in corundum, ruby, is the one that does it here: the pulse leaves as a narrow, parallel beam instead of a cone. The clearer the stuff and the longer the rod, the tighter the beam. A rod of glass or of a gem that does not lase is only a lens.
modular.feedback.axis.rod_length.tip: How long the lasing rod is. A longer rod gives a tighter beam, up to a hundred millimetres.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.surge_shun: Two cells of stock: a hand-closed shunt that bypasses the relay. Press the reload key and for a window the rate of fire doubles and every pulse is stronger, and the barrel heats faster; when the window ends the gun locks until the barrel is back under the limit. Hit the limit inside the window and you burn, as with no governor. The contacts' metal sets the window: one that welds or softens at a lower temperature shortens it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.thermopile: Four cells of stock: a ring of two joined metals between the barrel and a heat sink clamped to it, turning the barrel's heat back into charge. A hot barrel is fuel and a cold one is a plain gun. The conductor and the second slot are the two metals; the further apart their Seebeck figures, the more each shot returns. The sink fills as it soaks, and a full sink returns nothing until it has given its heat up. Needs a heat sink on the barrel, and a long gun or machine gun frame. Automatic and single.
modular.feedback.axis.line_length.tip: How much line the reel holds, in meters. A longer line reaches further and snaps when it is pulled past its length.
modular.feedback.desc.part.shock_lead: A shock lead for a pulse gun: a reel of line on a rod and a plug on its end, the wire probes of a taser. The line is a conductor, and the charge it can carry is capped by its ampacity.
modular.feedback.role.shock_lead.tip: A reel and a plug on a line from the gun. The reload key throws the plug at the body in front of you; from then the battery drains down the line into it, and the shock builds the longer the plug stays in, faster in a wet or metal-armored body. Press the key again to discharge, or let it fill to what the line can carry. The shock arcs on from the body to wet or conductive ones near it. A line pulled past its length or round a corner breaks; one trailed through your own water shorts to you. The reload key works one fitting.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tether_lead: A tether lead for a pulse gun: a socket in the receiver and a cable run to a battery worn on the back. The cable is a conductor in a sheath; a poor or thin one wastes more of every shot on the way.
modular.feedback.role.tether_lead.tip: A cable from the gun to a battery in a pack's battery fitting or a suit's bay. The gun has no cell of its own: it draws from the worn battery, and the cable costs a share of every shot as heat in the line. A better conductor that carries more current loses less.
modular.feedback.desc.part.heat_sink: A block of metal clamped to the barrel of a pulse gun, finned to give its heat to the air. It soaks the barrel's heat; the bigger it is, and the more heat a kilogram of its metal takes, the more shots it takes to fill.
modular.feedback.role.heat_sink.tip: A block clamped to the barrel that a thermopile seat needs. Its mass times its metal's specific heat sets how many returning shots it takes before it is full and the thermopile stops helping; copper and aluminum take a lot, lead little.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.fault.p: The reload key works one fitting: a pump charge, a hold-charge trigger, a surge shunt or a shock lead, not two.
A thermopile seat needs a heat sink on the barrel.
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.malefic_bla: The malefic lens blows at the first thing the pulse meets. Stand inside the blast and you take it, capped at three quarters of your health.
modular.feedback.desc.hazard.wet_line: A shock lead trailed through your own water shorts to you unless a glove rated for the cell's band insulates the hand, and the line goes dead.
item.feedback.whiplash.flavor.1: = You're not getting away this time.
technique.feedback.whiplash: Whiplash; press its key to throw a barbed spear on a lanyard that reels at once: a light creature, an item or a projectile comes to you, a heavy creature or a block pulls you; press again to retrieve it
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.b: Build a bedroll: a mattress with no frame, light enough to lash to a pack.
Build a bed: a mattress on a frame, set down as a place you can respawn.
Some might say that that phrase isn't to be taken literally. Some might say that.
Hold or touch something too hot for bare skin, and take the hit.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.l: Touch a live conductor, and walk away from it.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.c: Breathe air a hot toxic metal has fouled.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.h: Hold something glowing, and pay nothing for it.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.c: Put food to a fire in the open.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.w: Stand within reach of a Hearth that is lit and holding heat.
Eat food that was kept cold and is still sound.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.s: Wake in a bed you set down.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.h: Fit a head to a handle and build a tool.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.l: Fix a grapple line on something and let it bite.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.h: Wear a pack heavier than it is rated for, and feel it.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.r: Break a block that needs the right tool, with a hafted tool that is one.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.p: Have a villager accept a commission.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.m: Deliver work a villager calls exceptional.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.f: Buy from a villager, or sell it something.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.o: Have a villager buy from a Counter you keep.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.m: Be at a Market Cross when the market opens.
advancement.feedback.progress.survival.r: Take back goods a raider carried off.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.own_g: Be killed by your own heat, steam or wire.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.bad_r: Have the same villager reject your work three times running.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.custo: Sell a villager something from its own shelf.
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_chassis: The frame of a robot. It carries the drive, the battery and the program, and sets how much the robot weighs.
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_drive: What moves a robot. Wheels roll it over flat ground, legs step it up a block and over rubble more slowly, a rotor lifts it off the ground if it is light enough, at the cost of a steady draw to hover.
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_head: The working end: it breaks blocks. Its material decides what it can break and how fast.
modular.feedback.role.robot_chassis.tip: The frame of a robot: it carries everything and sets its weight.
modular.feedback.role.robot_drive.tip: The wheels and gearing: with the weight, they set how fast the robot moves.
modular.feedback.role.robot_head.tip: What the robot digs with: its material sets what it can break and how much charge a block costs.
feedback.jei.info.robot: A robot is built at the bench from a chassis, a drive and a tool head, then set down from the hand as a small machine that acts on its own. It has no program until you slide a Punch Card into it, and no power until you give it a battery: right-click it with each. Sneak-use a Punch Card on it to take its program back out. Its program is an ordinary Controller program, but its cards name the robot's own senses and actions instead of blocks: select one with the Data Connector (each click on the robot steps to the next) and link it from the Programmer. It stops where it stands when the battery is flat; a robot that is picked up keeps its parts, charge and card. The brain circuit (a circuit in its K slot) decides far more than its hand: a robot with none holds a program of only a few cards, reads numeric sensors with wobble and has no leash; each element on the circuit allows more cards, gain lengthens what its rangefinder and beacon reach and steadies readings with a lower noise, a lattice lets it remember places (remember, choose the next, and read the east, south and distance of the chosen one), and an endernet upgrade used on the robot is its leash: the Data Port it is bonded to becomes its base station, read and driven by cards or from the Network app, as far as the circuit's selectivity lets it carry. A tubed brain draws its heater from the pack. A gas-cell drive makes a drone that floats on its own.
gui.feedback.robot_channels.title: Channels
feedback.jei.info.robot_dock: A pad on an electrical line. A robot standing on it has its battery charged as a Charger charges one: it asks for the battery's charge current while the line is at its band or above.
feedback.jei.info.robot_reel: A reel on an electrical line that feeds a robot tied to it by a Tether Cable, for as long as the robot stays within the cable's length. Use the cable on the reel, then on the robot; sneak-use on the robot unties it. A removed reel leaves the robot untied.
feedback.jei.info.robot_tether: The cable between a Tether Reel and a robot. Use it on a reel to take that end, then on a robot to tie it. The robot may roam only so far from the reel.
robot.feedback.tether_none: Use the cable on a reel first
robot.feedback.leash_fitted: The endernet upgrade is fitted: the Data Port it is bonded to is this robot's base
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_sensor: A sense for a robot. A probe reads what the block ahead is, a rangefinder how far the first solid thing is, an inertial unit which way the robot faces and keeps its wheel error small. A robot without one still feels what is directly ahead.
modular.feedback.role.robot_sensor.tip: What the robot can sense beyond touch.
robot.feedback.channel.heading: Heading
feedback.jei.info.robot_beacon: A landmark. A robot within a few blocks of it knows exactly where it is again: its dead-reckoning error, which grows with every block it rolls, is wiped.
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_loader: A beacon of its own that keeps the ground a robot stands on awake while it works, so it does not halt when you walk away. It drains the robot's battery, and only so many chunks may be held this way across the server.
modular.feedback.role.robot_loader.tip: Keeps the robot's chunk loaded while it works.
robot.feedback.cap_chunk: Too many robots in this chunk
robot.feedback.cap_dimension: Too many robots in this dimension
feedback.jei.info.robot_arm: A robot fixed on a mount and run off an electrical line instead of a battery. It works the space it faces: breaks, places, picks up, drops, and puts items into or takes them out of a container or machine, and can switch a machine on or off. Right-click it with a Punch Card to load a program, sneak-use one to take the loaded program out, with a Data Connector to step through its channels for a Programmer card, with any other item to put it in its cargo; sneak with an empty hand to take a stack out. It acts only while its line feeds it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.robot_radio: The robot end of a radio link. Paired with a Radio Mast it lets a Controller read the robot's senses and drive its actions from a distance, as far as the mast's power reaches.
modular.feedback.role.robot_radio.tip: Lets a Radio Mast reach the robot.
robot.feedback.channel.slot_state: Chosen slot state (0 free, 1 mine, 2 another's, 3 done)
robot.feedback.channel.post: Post a haul in chosen slot
feedback.jei.info.robot_board: A board of sixteen slots a fleet shares over radio, a sink on an electrical line. Each slot is free, claimed by one robot or done, and holds a figure. A robot with a radio part that the board hears chooses a slot, claims it while its Claim switch is on (the claim lapses half a minute after the robot stops refreshing it, so a lost robot holds nothing), marks it done, or posts a haul in it. The board reaches as far as the power behind it, as a Radio Mast does, and noise drowns a robot the same way. It hears only as many robots as the current pays for, the nearest first, and a faster circuit hears more on the same current; a robot it does not hear reads nothing from it. A base Controller reads every slot's state and figure with Sensor cards and posts or clears slots with Actuator cards.
feedback.jei.info.robot_mast: The base end of a robot radio link, a sink on an electrical line. Select the mast with the Data Connector, then use the Connector on a robot that carries a radio part to pair them. A Controller's ordinary Sensor cards then read the robot's senses through the mast and its Actuator cards hold the robot's actions on or off. The link reaches as far as the power behind it, more on a higher band; out of range or in noise it hears nothing and every action is let go. Sparks drown it: an arc head within a few blocks of the robot or the mast. A mast boxed in by lead-lined chests does not hear it at its own end.
modular.feedback.desc.part.respirator_fa: The part of a respirator that seals over the nose and mouth. Soft sheet (leather, cloth) seals the face.
modular.feedback.desc.part.filter_cartri: A cartridge of porous media (charcoal) that concentrates oxygen from thin air. A deeper bed works in thinner air and lasts longer, and makes breathing harder. It wears with use.
modular.feedback.desc.part.air_cylinder: A small cylinder that holds air for a respirator. A thicker wall of a strong metal holds more. The Compressor fills it.
modular.feedback.fig.breath_floor.tip: The least oxygen the filter can still concentrate. A deeper bed reaches thinner air.
modular.feedback.fig.air_capacity.tip: How much air the cylinder holds. A thicker wall of a stronger metal holds more.
modular.feedback.fig.filter_life.tip: How long the filter works in thin air before it is spent. A deeper bed lasts longer.
modular.feedback.fig.breath_drag.tip: Share of sprint speed a filter takes off while the mask is worn. A deeper bed resists more.
feedback.jei.info.radiator_panel: A plate that sheds heat from a vessel it touches where the air is thin or gone. In a vacuum a vessel keeps all its heat, so a panel is the only way it cools.
feedback.jei.info.air_valve: A wall valve. Air from a pipe (or a compressed-air bucket) goes through it into the sealed cabin it opens on, topping up the air people breathe. A cabin with a hole loses air through it faster than a valve can supply.
modular.feedback.role.face_piece.tip: The part that seals over the nose and mouth. Soft sheet (leather, cloth) seals the face.
modular.feedback.role.filter.tip: A cartridge of porous media (charcoal). A deeper bed works in thinner air and lasts longer, and makes breathing harder.
modular.feedback.desc.part.roll_body: A cylinder of stock for a Rolling Mill. Its material, mass and diameter set how hard the mill may drive it; a wider roll carries more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.die_blank: A drawplate for a Wire Drawer. Its material and mass set how hard a draw it can take; a wider bore leaves a thinner wall that carries less.
modular.feedback.desc.part.lathe_blank: A cutting insert for a Lathe. Its edge hardness sets what it can cut; its material and rake set how hard a pass it can take.
modular.feedback.desc.part.drill_blank: A drill for a Drill Press. Its edge hardness sets what it can cut; its material and flute set how hard a feed it can take.
modular.feedback.desc.part.wheel_blank: An abrasive wheel for a Grinding Wheel machine. The grit sets what it can cut; a finer grit cuts gently and sheds slowly. Grit is used up whenever it cuts.
modular.feedback.role.roll.tip: The roll. Its metal and diameter set how hard the mill may drive it; it is what the mill wears.
modular.feedback.role.die.tip: The die. Its metal and bore set how hard a draw it takes; it is what the drawer wears.
modular.feedback.role.bit.tip: The bit. Its edge sets what it can cut and its body how hard it can be driven; it is what the machine wears.
modular.feedback.role.wheel.tip: The wheel. The grit sets what it can cut and how hard it can be driven; it is consumed by cutting.
feedback.jei.info.roll: The roll of a Rolling Mill. Right-click the mill with one to seat it; empty-handed, take out the skin, then the workpiece, then the roll. With no roll the mill does nothing.
feedback.jei.info.wire_die: The die of a Wire Drawer. Right-click the drawer to seat it; empty-handed with nothing in the die, take it out. The fast draw uses the die's full ceiling and may snap the wire; slow takes about a third.
feedback.jei.info.lathe_bit: The cutting bit of a Lathe. Its edge hardness sets what it can cut; a pass the bit cannot clear wears it.
feedback.jei.info.drill_bit: The bit of a Drill Press. Its edge hardness sets what it can cut; a push the bit cannot clear wears it.
feedback.jei.info.abrasive_wheel: The wheel of a Grinding Wheel. The grit sets what it cuts and is used up by every cut. A bald wheel cuts nothing.
feedback.jei.info.wire_drawer: Draws a rod into wire through a die. Seat a wire die by right-clicking with it; the die sets how hard a draw it takes. Sneak with an empty hand to switch between slow, which is safe and takes about a third of the die's ceiling, and fast, which may snap the wire. With no die the drawer does nothing. A circuit used on it (an empty hand takes it out after the die) cuts the chance a fast draw snaps the wire, by its noise.
feedback.jei.info.lathe: Turns stock chucked in it down with a lathe bit. Seat a bit by right-clicking with it; the bit's edge sets what it can cut, and a pass it cannot clear wears it. Sneak with an empty hand to switch between a light and a heavy pass. With no bit the lathe does nothing. Seat a thread rod in the carriage with right-click as its feed screw: each piece you chuck comes out a little off its measure, and the carriage sets how much. A bare carriage slid by hand wanders most; a cut thread feeds almost exactly; a rolled thread has backlash; a softer metal flexes more than a harder one. An empty hand takes the bit out, then the screw.
feedback.jei.info.drill_press: Drills stock with a drill bit. Seat a bit by right-clicking with it; the bit's edge sets what it can cut, and a push it cannot clear wears it. Sneak with an empty hand to switch between a slow and a fast feed. With no bit the press does nothing. A circuit used on it (an empty hand takes it out after the bit) cuts the chance a fast feed snaps the bit, by its noise.
feedback.jei.info.grinding_wheel: Grinds stock against an abrasive wheel. Seat a wheel by right-clicking with it; the grit sets what it can cut, and every cut uses grit up. With no wheel the machine does nothing.
modular.feedback.axis.aperture.tip: The hole the wire is drawn through. A wider bore leaves a thinner wall that carries less.
modular.feedback.axis.diameter.tip: The roll's width across. A wider roll carries more of the mill's drive.
modular.feedback.axis.flute.tip: The drill's flute. A deeper flute clears chips but leaves a weaker core that carries less.
modular.feedback.axis.grit.tip: Grit size, higher is finer. A finer wheel cuts gently and is driven less hard; a coarse one drives harder and sheds faster.
modular.feedback.desc.part.jet_compresso: The compressor of a jet. Its diameter is the intake; its stages squeeze the air before the flame, for more push from the same fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.jet_nozzle: The nozzle of a jet: it turns the hot gas into a fast stream.
modular.feedback.role.jet_compressor.tip: The compressor. A wider intake swallows more air and burns more fuel. More stages push harder per fuel but are heavier, and spin the blade tips faster, which the metal must hold.
modular.feedback.role.jet_nozzle.tip: The nozzle. A converging one is the same at any speed. A divergent one wastes thrust at rest and pays back at speed.
modular.feedback.role.combustor_liner.ti: The wall of the flame. The fuel's flame must stay under the heat this metal stands, or it wears.
modular.feedback.role.turbine_blades.tip: Blades in the exhaust that drive the compressor. They sit in the hottest gas: cobalt, tungsten and cermet stand what iron cannot.
modular.feedback.role.afterburner.tip: A reheat stage behind the turbine. A second controller level burns much more fuel in the exhaust for a big push; its metal must stand the extra heat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.compressor: Heavy and long: the most squeeze, and the fastest blade tips.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_con: A plain narrowing: the same push at any speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_div: A narrowing then a widening: wastes push at rest, gains it as the craft speeds up.
message.feedback.jet.on: Jet at full, %s mB of fuel
feedback.jei.info.jet: Pushes the body it is part of along its facing: a compressor draws air through the intake, fuel burns in it and the nozzle throws it back. Fuel comes from a pipe or bucket; right-click for full or idle, or set the throttle (and an afterburner level) from a controller card. It lights only while a shaft turns it at 20 RPM or the craft is moving fast through the air, then holds itself. Thin air and speed both cost thrust. It needs air (not the End, not underwater). The liner, blades and compressor tips wear if the flame is too hot or the tips too fast; slamming the throttle up stalls it.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.aerosp: A book on swallowing the air you fly through, setting it alight and throwing it behind you. The faster you go, the less each pound of it gives you.
item.feedback.treatise_aerospace_4: Aerospace Treatise IV: The Wandering Lights
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.aerosp: A book on the bright points that slide against the stars from night to night, and why. They have had a lot of nights to think about it.
advancement.feedback.progress.space.firs: Hold a sharp telescope on a planet on a clear night and see it as a disc.
advancement.feedback.progress.flight.jet: A thruster carries all it throws. A jet borrows the rest from the sky.
feedback.jei.info.freewheel: An overrunning clutch: one shaft in, one shaft out. The input drives the output only while it turns the faster, the same way. When the output outruns the input (a rotor turned by the air, a flywheel coasting) it is let go and keeps its own speed; the output never drives the input back.
jade.feedback.air.jet.4: Flamed out: needs a starter or more speed
modular.feedback.axis.bed.tip: How deep the filter bed is. A deep bed catches more and lasts longer, and chokes the flow harder; a thin one breathes easy and is spent sooner.
modular.feedback.axis.core.tip: How long the coil's core is. A longer core carries more flux and takes more stock and weight.
modular.feedback.axis.dose.tip: How much one press of the dispenser lets out. A large dose empties the tank faster; a small one stretches it.
modular.feedback.axis.focal_length.tip: How far the lens sits from its focus. A long focus magnifies more and narrows the view; a short one sees wide.
modular.feedback.axis.rim_width.tip: How wide the rim is around the shield's face. A wider rim takes the hits at the edge and weighs more; a narrow one is light.
modular.feedback.axis.span.tip: How wide the tread spans across. A wide tread spreads the load and grips more, and takes more stock and weight.
modular.feedback.axis.stroke.tip: How far the part travels each stroke. A long stroke moves more per push and is slower; a short one is quick and moves less.
modular.feedback.role.third_head.tip: A third working face on a multi-headed tool.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.broad_roll: A wide roll: it takes the plate across a wide face and wants more drive.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.narrow_rol: A narrow roll: it squeezes harder along a line and needs less drive.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cup_wheel: Grinds with the rim of a cup: it reaches into corners and cuts flat faces.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.straight_w: A plain disc: it grinds on its edge, even and easy to dress.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_beari: A long bearing land: the wire leaves straighter, and drags harder through the die.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.short_bear: A short bearing land: it drags less and wears the die more slowly, but holds the size less well.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.negative_r: The edge leans back from the work: a strong, blunt cut that takes hard stock and interruptions.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.positive_r: The edge leans into the work: a keen, light cut that peels soft stock, and chips on hard.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.spade_flut: A flat spade: cheap and quick to grind, it cuts coarse and clears chips poorly.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.twist_flut: A twisted flute: it carries chips up and out of the hole and cuts a clean bore.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheels: Rolls on wheels: fast and cheap on flat ground, stopped by a step.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.legs: Walks on legs: it steps over what a wheel would stop at, and is slower and costlier.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor: Lifts on rotors: it crosses any ground, and burns the battery to stay up.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.gas_cell: Floats on a gas cell: slower than a rotor, lifts far more, holds its height with no power at all and drifts nowhere when its power dies.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.probe: A touch probe: it reads what is in the block ahead.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rangefinde: A rangefinder: it reads how far away the nearest thing ahead is.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.laser: A laser sight: a diode and a small lens that throw a thin red beam along the barrel, so the point the gun is aimed at shows on whatever it falls on, and dust in the beam glows. It runs on a battery loaded into the gun (right-click the gun with a battery) and draws it flat in time.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_rangefin: With a charged battery loaded in the gun, prints the distance to what the muzzle points at under the crosshair, in whole blocks.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_laser: With a charged battery loaded in the gun, shows a red beam from the muzzle to the point aimed at.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.inertial: An inertial unit: it reads the robot's own motion and heading.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.electr: A book on wrapping wire round iron and calling it a magnet. The margins are full of someone's sparks.
A book on charge kept in glass and current coaxed from acid. Read it dry; the jar is not the only thing that should be insulated.
A book on switching current with nothing that moves, from glowing glass to quartz that keeps time. The tubes were retired, though the author insists they were only resting.
A book on making light keep step with itself: a flash into a clear crystal, two mirrors, and a beam that stays narrow for a long way.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.roboti: A book on putting a chassis, a brain and a radio together into a machine that gets about. Chapter nine is on what to do when it gets about without you.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.materi: A book on heating metal and cooling it at the right speed. The whole thing is about timing, and the dedication page is late.
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.nuclea: A book on splitting heavy atoms and keeping the chain polite. The last chapter is a single page that reads 'Drop the rods.'
gui.feedback.research_table.blurb.experi: A book on what happens when you pick up an orb and cannot say where to put it. Mostly vessels, and what to do when they are full.
A book on getting experience out of things that were keeping it: sculk, ore, villagers and the smelter. The sculk chapter hums.
A book on spending experience, and why you will not like the rate. The last chapter is mostly an apology.

How many attachments the wiring can carry current to. Heavier wiring (more turns, a better conductor) feeds more.
Short focus reaches further; long focus sees thermal farther (sight x%1$s here). Keeping glare off: %3$s, %2$s Eu a time. Needs the suit powered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.spring: Soft and long cushions a fall; stiff and short throws the jump (+%1$s%% here). A hard landing stomps for %2$s damage a block fallen. Works unpowered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.actuat: Short stroke strides fast; a long one lifts the foot over a step (+%1$s blocks here). Draws %2$s Eu a tick while striding.
A narrow pad bites the ground; a wide one pushes water (+%1$s%% water speed here). Works unpowered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.filter: A thin bed passes air and lengthens breath; a deep one scrubs poison, nausea and hunger: %1$s. Each scrub costs %2$s Eu. Works unpowered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.therma: A thin plate sheds heat (cooling x%1$s); a thick one resists fire. Frost kept off the skin: %2$s, %3$s Eu a time. Works unpowered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.thrust: The throat sets push and fuel burn together: x%1$s of the middle throat. Burns fuel from a bucket in your pack.
A thin plate turns shots (-%1$s%% here); a thick one takes blasts and shrugs off a shove (knockback resistance %2$s%%). Works unpowered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.coil.t: A long core reaches; a short one pulls hard. Draws %1$s Eu a tick while pulling, and only pulls what is magnetic.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.dispen: Doses what you carry: the dose axis sets the millilitres a use, the strength how well it holds against the metal. Needs the suit powered.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.cost.t: What the attachments draw while they work, added up, and the module's whole mass. Each class has its own cost on its line.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.suit.abilit: What the held parts add to the suit's wheel. A circuit lets a lens scan and a heat plate mask; a motor lets a heat plate vent; a cell lets a magnet pulse.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.pack.free.t: What the pack can hold, in contents, before it slows the wearer: the carry rating less the pack's own mass.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.bed.heal.ti: The share of your health a night gives back: half the comfort, and in snow country less by the bed's warmth.
An effect the meal gives when eaten, how long it lasts and how long after eating it comes on. Fat and fiber slow the coming-on and stretch the effect.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.dish.seal.t: How well the container shuts: an open one dries, heats and soaks quickest, a covered one half as much, a sealed one not at all, and a sealed one does not spill.
More food than the container holds. Carrying it spills the wettest part until it fits, unless sealed.
