modular.feedback.desc.part.launcher_seat: The store of a launcher. Its variant is how it holds work: a spring cocked by hand, a reservoir pumped with gas, a solenoid fed by a battery or jar, or a boiler heated until its water pushes. The metal's stiffness and the part's volume set how much it holds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.spring_sea: A coiled spring cocked by hand with the reload key. The time is its stored work over your strength; a spring stronger than its receiver takes a set each cocking, and far past it snaps.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.reservoir_: A pressure vessel pumped up with the reload key. The first shots are the hardest and pressure falls with each one. Pumping past the walls' limit weeps, and far past it bursts and hurts you.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.solenoid_s: A coil that throws the piston from a battery or Leyden jar seated in the receiver. A jar dumps its charge in one hard push; a battery gives a steady, lighter one. Right-click a cell onto the launcher to seat it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.steam_seat: A small boiler. Fill it from a water bucket with the reload key and heat it; it pushes by its steam pressure. A cold boiler gives a weak push, and a cold enough one will not fire. Each shot spends water and heat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.inertia_fu: Sets a shell off on any hit, a body it passes through as well as the surface that stops it. In a shell its delay is the time it takes to arm.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.proximity_: Arms after its delay, then sets the shell off when a body or a block comes near its path. It costs a sensing sweep each tick it flies.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_tank: The tank a caster holds its fluid in. The wall's thickness over the tank's width against the metal's strength is the pressure it holds before it weeps; a longer tank holds more. A fluid that eats the metal or runs it hot wears it, and one that runs it past melting lets go.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_nozzle: Where the stream leaves. A narrow bore throws a stream far and hard; a wide one passes more fluid and spreads it. Its variant sets how the stream fans, and an atomiser breaks it into a mist that mixes with air.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_receiv: The body the tank, valve and nozzle are fixed to, and the hand holds. Its variant is how it carries them: a squirt frame, a long lance frame or a pack with a hose.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.squirt_fra: A short body with the tank on top and a grip under it. Light and quick, and it holds its pipe no more truly than the metal of its barrel allows.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.lance_fram: A long gun frame with the tank slung under a long pipe. A long pipe keeps the stream together over a longer reach and a narrower cone, and a bigger tank fits; it carries a good deal of metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.backpack_f: A wand on a hose from a tank worn on the back: two tanks' worth of fluid and a great deal of metal. The hose loses some of the pressure on the way to the nozzle and the wand's short pipe reaches less.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_valve: The valve the trigger opens and closes. A fluid it cannot take eats its seat.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_pump: What drives the stream at a steady head, whatever the tank's pressure: a hand pump worked with the reload key, or a motor on a seated battery. With nothing to move it runs dry and wears.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.hand_pump: A pump worked with the reload key. Each stroke primes the stream for a while; a longer stroke primes it for longer, and its metal's strength sets its head.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.electric_p: A motor that holds the stream at its head for as long as the trigger is held, after a short run-up. A bigger motor in a stronger metal holds a higher head. It draws charge from a battery or Leyden jar seated in the caster, more the wider the bore and the higher the head; right-click the cell onto the caster to seat it.
modular.feedback.axis.motor.tip: The size of the motor. A bigger motor holds a higher head and is heavier; the walls still hold the limit.
modular.feedback.desc.part.caster_pilot: A small flame at the nozzle's end, fed by a trickle off the tank while the valve is open. It lights a stream of a fluid that burns, and the campfire, candle or flammable block its tip touches. A fluid that does not burn leaves it cold, and water over the muzzle puts it out. A wider orifice burns more fluid; a metal that cannot take a hot fluid wears.
modular.feedback.role.pilot.tip: A flame at the nozzle's end that lights a stream of a fluid that burns. A wide bore with a flame at the muzzle lets a volatile stream burn back into the tank.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pilot: A small standing flame right at the muzzle. It burns little fluid and lights the stream where it leaves.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.torch: A longer flame that stands out in front of the muzzle and lights what it reaches, at the price of more metal and more fluid burned.
modular.feedback.role.tank.tip: Holds the fluid and its pressure. The wall's thickness and the metal's strength set what it holds before it weeps and then lets go; its length sets how much fluid it takes.
modular.feedback.role.nozzle.tip: Shapes the stream. A narrow bore reaches far and pushes hard; a wide one passes more fluid and spreads it.
modular.feedback.role.valve.tip: The switch the trigger works: held open it lets the stream through. A fluid its metal cannot take eats it.
modular.feedback.role.drive.tip: A pump that drives the stream at a steady head while it is worked. Without one, the tank's own pressure throws the stream and falls as it empties.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fan: A flat fan that covers a wider patch of ground and several targets at once, and reaches no farther than its pressure lets it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.mist: A wide spray of fine drops: it covers a lot at close range and pushes little.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.atomiser: Breaks the stream into a fine mist that mixes with the air. A fluid that burns forms a cloud that a spark or an ember sets alight, and a cloud that is thick enough goes up.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jet: A tight jet: it holds together over distance and puts all its push into one place.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_capacity.tip: How much fluid the tank holds. A longer tank holds more.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_rating.tip: The pressure the walls hold before they weep. A thicker wall of a stronger metal holds more; past it they weep, and well past it they let go.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_reach.tip: How far a stream of water reaches at the pressure the walls hold, or at a pump's head. A narrower bore reaches farther.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_flow.tip: How much water the nozzle passes in a tick at that pressure. A wider bore passes more.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_head.tip: The steady pressure the stream is made at: a pump's head, or what the walls hold with no pump. Under 4 Pu nothing leaves the nozzle.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_resist.tip: The weakest resistance among the tank, valve and nozzle, 0 to 1. A fluid that eats metal wears the part that resists least first.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_service.tip: The hottest fluid the tank walls hold before they soften. Hotter than this wears the tank; far hotter lets it go.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_pump_load.ti: What the pump would drive over what the walls hold. Past 0.8 the walls hold the pump back to 0.8 and it wastes its strength.
modular.feedback.fig.caster_drive.tip: 0 the tank's own air, 1 a hand pump, 2 a motor.
feedback.gloss.modular.feeble: head under %s Pu: a stream does not leave the nozzle
feedback.gloss.modular.short: a stream reaches under %s blocks at the head it is made at
feedback.gloss.modular.pump_held_back: the pump would drive over %s of what the walls hold, so the walls hold it down
feedback.gloss.modular.undriven: no pump fitted: the stream runs only on the tank's own air
feedback.gloss.modular.corrodible: a part resists corrosion under %s: an aggressive fluid eats it fast
feedback.jei.info.potion_fluid: A brewed potion as a fluid. A potion bottle holds 250 mB of it: drop one on a fluid caster in an inventory to pour it in, or an empty glass bottle to take 250 mB out. It keeps what the bottle had (effect, level, length, potency) and fades the same in a tank. Two potions of one brew run together in a caster; different brews do not. Sprayed, it gives its effect to what it hits.
message.feedback.caster.flashback: The flame runs back up the stream!
feedback.jei.info.caster: A fluid caster throws a stream of whatever its tank holds. Fill the tank with a bucket, a pipe, or by using the caster on a placed tank (which also pressurises it); sneak-use pours it back. Hold left click to open the valve. A caster with no pump is a pressurised tank: the reload key works its air pump to raise the pressure, which throws the stream and falls as the tank empties. A caster with a hand pump drives the stream at a steady head while the reload key keeps it primed. One with an electric pump holds the stream at its head while the trigger is held, after a short run-up, and draws charge from a battery or Leyden jar right-clicked onto it, more the wider the bore and the higher the head. The fluid's own properties decide the effect: a hot one scalds and, hot enough, sets what it hits alight, a cold one chills (the colder, the faster, and deep cold freezes flesh), water douses fire and waters farmland and fills a cauldron, one that burns lights from a flame in its path and sets what it hits alight for as long as it burns, an oxidiser feeds a fire already burning, a thick one clings and slows, an acid or a base burns flesh and bites armor by how far its pH is from neutral, a toxic one poisons, a radioactive one withers, an unstable spatial one hops what stands near, and a heavy flow shoves what it hits (a fast, dense one cuts). A fluid hotter than its boiling point is a gas: it does not stream but leaves a cloud, poisonous if toxic, explosive if it burns. An atomiser makes a mist of a fluid that burns, which a flame sets off. Pressure over what the walls hold makes the tank weep, then burst; a fluid that eats the metal or runs it hot wears the parts; a burning volatile stream through a wide nozzle flashes back into the tank; a pump worked dry wears. A brewed potion goes in as fluid: a potion bottle dropped on the caster in an inventory pours its 250 mB in, and an empty glass bottle takes 250 mB out. Sprayed, a potion gives each body it hits its effect for the share of a bottle's length that lands on it, works its place effects where it lands, and an atomiser leaves a mist that doses whatever stands in it. Two potions of one brew run together; a potion kept in the tank fades like one in a bottle.
skill.feedback.move.crack_vial.desc: Cast: a potion bottle from your pack smashes on the body at arm's length: a whole dose on that one body, none spread, and a small stagger. The first cast opens a bottle and every potion use here draws down its 250 mB. No live potion, no cast.
skill.feedback.move.fume.desc: Cast: two bottles' worth of dose burst on the floor ahead and hang as a mist that doses whatever stands in it, you included. Spends potion from the pack.
skill.feedback.move.cascade.desc: Cast: a potion thrown at the body you face breaks on it, and what runs off lands as a second dose on the nearest other body within a few blocks. Spends two doses from the pack.
skill.feedback.move.tainted_wound.desc: Rider on Rend: also runs a dose of the pack's potion into the target it opens. Spends potion from the pack; without one, Rend is unchanged.
message.feedback.shove.fixed: That is not a loose body: it is part of the ground.
message.feedback.shove.light: Too light to take hold of.
message.feedback.shove.standing: You cannot shove what you stand on.
feedback.programmer.text.bad_signal: %s is not a signal a sensor reads
feedback.programmer.text.bad_arg: %s is repeated or is not a kind, color or reduction here
feedback.data_connector.mode.paint: color a link (dye in the other hand)
feedback.data_connector.not_painted: Select the Controller, then a node linked to it
gui.feedback.computer.internal_empty: Nothing saved here. Right-click a drive and choose Save to internal disk to keep what is on it.
gui.feedback.computer.file_too_big: That file is too big to keep
gui.feedback.computer.app_move_only: An app is installed once: move it to a disk, not copy it
modular.feedback.desc.part.piston_cylind: The cylinder of a piston. Its bore is the area the gas pushes on; its wall against that bore is the pressure it stands before it bursts.
modular.feedback.role.piston_cylinder.ti: The cylinder. A wide bore pushes harder and swallows more gas a stroke; a thick wall of strong metal stands higher pressure.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cylinder_p: A drawn tube closed at one end.
modular.feedback.desc.part.piston_rod: The rod of a piston. Its length is how far the head reaches.
modular.feedback.role.piston_rod.tip: The rod. A longer one reaches further and takes more gas for each stroke.
modular.feedback.axis.reach.tip: How many blocks the head travels out.
modular.feedback.role.piston_seal.tip: The seal round the head. A soft one keeps the gas in; a hard one lets some slip by each stroke.
modular.feedback.role.sticky_face.tip: A sticky face on the head (slime) pulls the block behind it back when the rod comes in.
figure.feedback.block.Area.label: Bore area
figure.feedback.block.Reach.label: Reach
figure.feedback.block.Slip: Lets %s of a stroke's gas slip by
figure.feedback.block.Slip.label: Slip
figure.feedback.block.Sticky.label: Sticky face
feedback.jei.info.piston_block: Redstone only carries a signal, so a signal alone does not move a piston: each stroke out also uses gas from a gas tank, pressure vessel, compressor or pipe touching the cylinder on any face but the front, as much as the bore and reach sweep. A controller switch moves it the same way. What it can push is the weight of the whole line against the bore and how full the gas holder is; a line too heavy blows the gas and wears the seal. Gas over what the cylinder's wall stands bursts it. A slime face pulls the block behind the head back with it.
modular.feedback.desc.part.note_body: The body of a note block. Cut it to a pitch; the noisemakers fitted to it do the sounding.
modular.feedback.role.note_body.tip: The body. Its pitch is the note it plays when first placed; an empty hand steps it afterwards.
modular.feedback.axis.pitch.tip: The note the block plays when placed, in semitones over the lowest of two octaves.
modular.feedback.desc.part.noisemaker: The part of a note block that sounds. Its shape is the instrument; its material sets how loud it rings and how high.
modular.feedback.role.noisemaker.tip: The noisemaker: its shape is the instrument. A harder one rings louder; a heavier one plays lower. A second can sound with it.
figure.feedback.block.Pitch.label: Pitch
figure.feedback.block.Voices.label: Noisemakers
feedback.jei.info.dispenser_actuator: Fits into a spring dispenser (use it on the dispenser). When the spring releases, the arm presses the first item in the dispenser against the block in front, or the one beyond an empty cell, as a hand would use it: bone meal on a crop, flint and steel, a bucket, shears, a block set down. Without it the spring throws the item out.
modular.feedback.desc.part.second_noisem: A second noisemaker for a note block: it sounds with the first, so the block plays two instruments at once.
An optional second noisemaker. It sounds together with the first; its own material sets how loud and how high.
tooltip.feedback.rack_fitting.cabinet: Holds a few single pieces, each keeping its own state
tooltip.feedback.rack_fitting.cold_plate: Chills the bay while a refrigeration unit holds the rack cold
tooltip.feedback.rack_fitting.liner: Lead-lined: keeps the bay's radiation in
feedback.jei.info.rack_fitting_cabinet: Use on an empty rack bay. The bay then holds up to 16 single pieces to a modest weight, any item, each keeping its own wear, charge and other state, so worn tools and parts need no pallet each.
feedback.jei.info.rack_fitting_cold_plat: Use on an empty rack bay, beside its container fitting. While a refrigeration unit touches or cools the rack, food in the bay spoils at the cold rate. With no running unit the bay spoils at the room's rate and looks fine until opened. Sneak and use an empty hand on the empty bay to take the plate out.
feedback.jei.info.rack_fitting_liner: Use on an empty rack bay, beside its container fitting. Radioactive goods in the bay give off only what a lead lining lets out. A bare bay lets all of it out. Sneak and use an empty hand on the empty bay to take the liner out.
tooltip.feedback.rack_fitting.hopper: Holds one loose stuff by weight
tooltip.feedback.rack_fitting.bin: Holds a few kinds of tiny pieces
tooltip.feedback.rack_loaded: Loaded: its stock comes with it
screen.feedback.dock.watch_use: Click: watch the picked line. Right click: clear.
feedback.channel.dock.switch: Switch (on lets retrievals run, off holds them)
feedback.channel.dock.watch_1: Watch 1 (a pulse asks for a stack)
feedback.channel.dock.watch_2: Watch 2 (a pulse asks for a stack)
feedback.channel.dock.watch_3: Watch 3 (a pulse asks for a stack)
feedback.channel.dock.watch_4: Watch 4 (a pulse asks for a stack)
screen.feedback.dock.cancel: Click to drop from the queue
screen.feedback.dock.state.no_head: No shuttle head behind the dock
modular.feedback.desc.part.rack_frame: The uprights of a pallet rack. The metal's strength sets what the bays bear; a frame that burns makes a rack that burns.
modular.feedback.desc.part.rack_shelf: The decks of a pallet rack. The metal's strength sets what a bay bears and its service temperature how hot a load may be.
modular.feedback.role.rack_frame.tip: The uprights. A bay bears what the weaker of frame and shelf allows.
modular.feedback.role.rack_shelf.tip: The decks. A load hotter than the metal's service temperature wears them and lowers what the bays bear.
figure.feedback.block.Rating.label: Bay strength
feedback.jei.info.pallet_rack: A shelf unit of eight bays, two across, two up and two deep, built from a frame and shelves. Stand racks against either side of a warehouse rail, up to eight high. A bay holds one kind of stack as a pallet unless a fitting is put in it. The weaker of frame and shelf sets how much a bay bears. A load hotter than the shelf stands wears it. Use an empty hand on a bay to read it. A broken rack keeps its stock. Use a reader module on a rack to make it take only goods recorded in one band; each use moves to the next band and a sneaking use clears it.
feedback.jei.info.warehouse_rail: The track of a warehouse carriage. Lay it in a straight line, up to 64 long, running on from a Shuttle Head. Pallet Racks against either side join the aisle.
feedback.jei.info.shuttle_head: Drives a warehouse carriage. Set it between the Warehouse Dock and the first rail, facing down the rail, and turn it with a shaft from either side. Faster shafts mean shorter trips; heavy loads take more strength.
feedback.jei.info.warehouse_dock: The end of a warehouse aisle. Feed it from any side by belt, hopper or hand-off and the carriage files the goods: with the same stack first, else in the nearest bay with room. Right-click to search the stock and ask for it. Retrieved goods leave from its front onto a belt or into a container, or can be pulled from any side. A full output holds retrievals back while storing goes on. Sneak and use an empty hand on the dock to take back whatever waits in the intake. Use a belt reader module on a side or the top to fit it as a head: what the heads read of a load is recorded with it, for rack filters and property searches. Click a fouled head with an empty hand to wipe it, sneak to take it off. Powered heads need a wire against the dock.
feedback.jei.info.rack_fitting_hopper: Use on an empty rack bay. The bay then holds a single loose stuff (grain, granular goods, ore, dust and crushed forms) by weight alone, with no limit on count. Sneak and use an empty hand on the empty bay to take it out.
feedback.jei.info.rack_fitting_bin: Use on an empty rack bay. The bay then holds up to eight kinds of pieces of 0.2 Mu or less each, to a modest weight. Sneak and use an empty hand on the empty bay to take it out.
figure.feedback.block.Condition.label: Condition
screen.feedback.dock.state.away: Away: its chunk is not loaded
feedback.jei.info.catalogue_desk: One index over several warehouse aisles. Use the Data Connector on the desk and then on a Warehouse Dock to link them; a better circuit reads more docks. It needs its built-in circuit and a little LV current from a wire beside it. Search the list and ask for an amount: the order is shared among the docks holding it, soonest first, and each share leaves from its own dock. Hover a line to see which docks hold it and the status line to see how each dock is doing. Type a name over the title of a dock screen to tell the docks apart.
screen.feedback.dock.name: Dock name
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_scratch: Reads the hardness of passing cargo and sweeps one band (soft, mid or hard) to its side. Click to choose the band. Its point blunts on the hardest stuff and reads it poorly. Also fits a Warehouse Dock as a reader head.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_drag: Reads the grip of passing cargo and sweeps one band (slick, mid or grippy) to its side. Click to choose the band. A sticky piece reads grippier than it is. Also fits a Warehouse Dock as a reader head.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_spark: Tells the kind of passing cargo by spark and flame, and sweeps one kind to its side. Click to choose it. Alloys, coats and soft metals muddy the test. Also fits a Warehouse Dock as a reader head.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_thermo: Reads how hot passing cargo is and sweeps one band (cold, warm or hot) to its side. Click to choose the band. A bright surface reads colder than it is. Draws a little current. Also fits a Warehouse Dock as a reader head.
modular.feedback.desc.part.armour_studs: A strip of rivets for the outside of armor. Set closer together they stop more thrusts and bite whoever strikes the wearer, and take more stock and weigh more.
modular.feedback.desc.part.armour_lining: The padding worn under the plate. A thicker lining takes more of a blow and weighs more.
modular.feedback.axis.spacing.tip: How far apart the studs sit. Closer studs are more of them: they stop more thrusts and bite harder, and take more stock and weigh more.
